system.description: Your own two hands.
Brass, bought "as a paperweight" off a stall in Ridley Road. Illegal to carry.
Swung from the hand. Doubles as a lock nobody trusts.
Improvised and nasty. A hit that does any damage also causes Bleeding. Smashes on a Proper Mess.
From the pub. Long reach, snaps easily.
Doubles as a tool: it opens a cheap door (Graft, one band easier).
Willow. Kept in the car "for the nets".
Aluminium. Nobody in Hackney has ever played baseball.
Opens doors, shutters and skulls. Counts as a tool for breaking in.
A seven iron from a bag in a Range Ruler boot.
Carrying one is a crime on its own if you are searched. A Smashed It hit causes Bleeding.
Folds into a pocket. Still a knife to the custody sergeant. A Smashed It hit causes Bleeding.
Serrated, green-handled, banned. Everyone who sees it calls the police. A Smashed It hit causes Bleeding.
Big, ugly, illegal. Draws attention the moment it comes out.
Off the wall of a stairwell. Through a door in one swing.
A rusty little automatic. Small, quiet for a gun, unreliable.
A blank-firer drilled out in a garage in Leyton. Jams on a Proper Mess.
A proper modern 9mm. Comes in a sock, never asked about.
An old .38, somebody's granddad's from the war. Six shots, never jams.
A chromed .50 that kicks like a horse. Off Your Game for anyone with Muscle d4.
A converted Mac-style machine pistol. Can fire a burst.
Compact, sprays more than it aims. Can fire a burst.
Met ARV issue. Never for sale; taken off a Trojan unit at your peril.
Two barrels, short range, very loud. At Engaged range it adds +2 impact.
Six in the tube. Clears a room and wakes the street.
A legal-ish double-barrel from Essex. Licensed to someone else.
For pigeons. Still gets you nicked if you point it at someone.
Bolt action with a scope. Hits anything you can see.
An AK that came in a lorry of washing machines. Can fire a burst.
Met ARV carbine. Never for sale.
Every building site in E9 has a pile.
Aimed down a street on bonfire night. Also a decent distraction.
A milk bottle, petrol and a rag. A hit sets the target Burning; a miss sets fire to whatever is next to them.
Fills the area: everyone in it is Gassed and nobody can be targeted from outside until it clears.
Hits everyone Engaged with the target too. Where did you even get this?
Police issue. Everyone Engaged with the target is Stunned.
Police issue. A hit also inflicts Stunned and Prone.
Police issue. A hit inflicts Gassed.
Police issue.
GM only. If one of these turns up in Hackney, the whole Met turns up after it. Hits everyone Engaged with the target.
A box of a hundred. Fits the Pocket .22.
A box of fifty. Fits the Converted Pistol, Polymer Nine, Machine Pistol and Micro SMG.
A box of fifty for the Service Revolver.
Twenty for the Hand Cannon. Each one costs six quid.
A box of twenty-five cartridges for any shotgun.
Thirty for the Kalash.
Twenty for the Hunting Rifle.
A tin of five hundred.
Police issue. Never sold.
Police issue. Never sold.
Police carbine magazine. Never sold.
One rocket for the launcher. GM only. Never sold.
Thick enough to take the edge off a punch.
Old-school. Takes the edge off a knife and a slide down the tarmac.
Leathers and a lid. Reduction 2, and coming off a bike does half damage.
Covert vest under a hoodie. Police wear the hi-vis version.
Covert body armour. Stops a pistol round; you still feel it.
Met-pattern body armour.
TSG kit. +3 Guard while you hold it; you cannot use a two-handed weapon.
Cut cable locks and cheap D-locks: bike locks are one band easier.
Through any bike lock in seconds: two bands easier. Shrieks — anyone near notices.
Clones keyless-entry fobs from the doorstep: car locks two bands easier, silently.
Plugs into the OBD port and teaches the car a new key. Car locks two bands easier and the car starts clean (no hotwire).
Old-school door opener: older cars one band easier.
For the ignition barrel. No easier, but you can try.
For doors and padlocks: one band easier, and silent.
Slow and quiet. Gets through a padlock hasp or a cheap chain given a minute.
Patch up a motor: a Graft roll (Medium) restores Body (Sorted 2, Smashed It 4, Legendary all) or fixes a flat tyre.
Five litres. Refuels a vehicle, or makes three Petrol Bombs with some milk bottles.
A pair of number plates off a written-off car. Swap them (Graft, Easy) and the police scanner reads the new plate.
Tag a wall, or cover a stolen bike's frame so it is not recognised.
Pay-as-you-go, no contract. Pat only texts this number.
Listen to the Met on an old Airwave scanner: Savvy steps up one die to spot police coming, and you hear when the helicopter goes up.
Watch a target from a rooftop. Savvy one band easier for casing a job.
Bright LED torch. Also good for blinding someone for a moment (Front vs their Bottle).
A pack of heavy-duty ties. Restrain a Grabbed or Down person: they are Cuffed.
Fixes everything. Silences everyone.
A good fake driving licence: Front steps up one die when the police ask who you are.
Topped up. Get on a bus without paying cash.
Hides your face. Witnesses can't describe you: a witnessed crime adds 1 less Heat (minimum 0) while you wear it — but wearing one in daylight is a look.
A decent D-lock for your own ride. Locked bikes need a Hard roll to nick.

A ten-pound bag. Take it: Blazed (+1 Bottle, -1 Savvy and Wheels), then Foggy.

Caught with a bag: a caution and +0 Heat. Caught with a lot of it: that is dealing.

A gram wrap. Take it: Wired (+1 Front and Bottle), then Crashing.

Caught carrying: +1 Heat.

Pressed pills stamped with a logo. Take one: Loved Up (+2 Front, -1 Aim and Savvy), then Wrung Out.

Caught carrying: +1 Heat.
Street Xanax. Take one: Numb (Shaken and Bricking It stop working; -1 Moves and Aim), then Jittery.
A balloon of laughing gas. Giggling for a couple of minutes (-2 Savvy, -1 Front). The canisters litter every park in E9.
Gym-bought steroids. Take a course: Pumped (+1 Muscle, -1 Front), then Roid Rage.
Patch Up (Savvy, Medium) removes Bleeding or Hurt and heals 2. Three uses.
Stops Bleeding. No roll needed if nobody is hitting you.
Co-codamol from the chemist: Numbed (In Pain and Hurt stop working) for an hour, and removes In Pain.
Buzzing (+1 Moves) for half an hour and removes Knackered.
A four-pack. One can: Dutch Courage (+1 Bottle). A second while you have it: Mullered.
Removes Gassed.
Removes Shaken. Twenty in a pack.
A sandwich, crisps and a drink. Heals 1.
Four wings and chips from Chicken Palace. Heals 2.
Large doner, chilli sauce. Heals 2 and removes Mullered.
At Uncle's Cafe. Heals 4 and removes Bruised and Knackered.
With liquor, from the shop on Broadway Market. Heals 3 and removes Shaken.
Grey trackies and a hoodie. You look like everyone else on the estate.
Head to toe in black. Witnesses cannot describe you, but anyone who sees you assumes the worst.

system.biography: Chrome pegs, a gyro and a sticker-bombed frame. Every estate in Hackney has three. The Chainring pays £40–60 for a clean one.
Front suspension, knobbly tyres, a D-lock that is usually better than the bike. Goes over the Marshes, down the towpath and through Victoria Park.
A featherweight carbon racer worth more than most of the cars on Mare Street. Its owner locks it to a lamppost with two locks and a prayer.
Twenty kilos of red steel from a docking station. Anyone can ride one; nobody will buy one. Untraceable, so the cops do not care.
A rental scooter with the speed limiter ripped out. Silent, foldable, illegal on the road and everywhere else.
Pedal-assist bike with an insulated box on the back. Start a Courier shift from the driver seat to take delivery jobs.
The noise of every high street at 11pm. Top box, pillion seat, L-plates optional. Doubles as a courier bike.
An unregistered off-road bike that wheelies the length of the Marshes. No plate, no insurance, no brakes worth mentioning.
A naked 650 commuter bike. Light, quick, forgiving, parked outside every pub in Shoreditch.
A litre superbike with a howl you hear three postcodes away. Nothing on the road catches it in a straight line; the corners are your problem.
Metro Police traffic motorcycle: lights, siren and an ANPR plate scanner. Start a Police shift from the driver seat.
The London black cab: six passengers, a turning circle of 25 feet and a driver who has done The Knowledge. Start a Taxi shift to pick up fares.
A silver hybrid saloon with a phone cradle on every surface. Silent under 20 mph. Works taxi shifts like the cab, tips are worse.
Britain's favourite small car, therefore Britain's most stolen small car. A screwdriver and some nerve.
A small hatch with a big turbo and a bigger exhaust. Popular with lads who say "bruv" at speed.
A dad's estate car with a roof box and a dog guard. Nobody looks twice at it, which is the whole point.
Keyless entry, tinted glass, never once off-road. A relay box and twenty seconds, if you know what you are doing.
A hand-built British grand tourer. Mayfair money parked on a Hoxton street.
A V12 wedge on a sheikh's plates. Seen in Knightsbridge, very occasionally in Shoreditch, never twice.
An imported American muscle car with a blower through the bonnet. Loud enough to set off car alarms in Dalston.
A dented white Transit-style van with "NO TOOLS LEFT IN THIS VEHICLE" on the back doors (there are tools). Courier jobs; also the classic getaway.
Plays "Greensleeves" at 90 decibels. Sells cones, and, everyone on the estate knows, rather more than cones.
Battenburg-livery response car: lights, siren, ANPR plate scanner, cage in the back. Start a Police shift from the driver seat.
The riot van. Six seats, four of them behind a cage.
Armed Response Vehicle. When one of these turns up you are on four stars.
Front-line ambulance: lights, siren, a stretcher bay. Start a Paramedic shift and get patients to Homerton or the Royal London.
A fire engine with a 13.5 m ladder and 1,800 litres of water. Start a Firefighter shift to answer fire calls.
A red double-decker on the 38 to Victoria (it never gets past Dalston). Start a Bus shift to run the route stop to stop.
Police air support. It flies over the street grid, sees everything and tells every car on the radio. Appears at three stars.

Patricia Okonedo runs "Pat's Cycle Repairs" under the railway arches on Morning Lane: half honest bike shop, half the biggest bike-theft ring in E8. She is everyone's auntie and nobody's fool. She pays cash, on the nail, and never forgets a debt.

She knows every bicycle in the borough, including the ones she has not seen yet. Tea before business. Cash after inspection.

Pat wants a crew that earns quietly. She can source tools, buy stolen bicycles and set orders through the Blower. She expects loyalty, not cruelty.

Pat's mechanic. Can strip a stolen road bike to unrecognisable parts in eleven minutes. Speaks mostly in derailleur.

Workshop mechanic, dry wit, permanent mug of tea.

Spanner repairs the crew’s kit and notices mismatched stories as readily as mismatched wheels. He knows Jaz is better than the work she is doing.

Pat's nephew, twenty, permanently on a BMX. Kez scouts the bikes — which lock, which street, how long until the owner comes back — and texts you tip-offs.

A sharp-eyed runner whose phone is always vibrating.

Kez trades information: where the bikes are, which road is closed, who is suddenly spending money. Treat them as a person with ambitions, not an infallible quest marker.

Owns Chicken Palace on Mare Street and the flat upstairs you rent. Late with rent is fine. Police at the door is not.

Chicken Palace’s owner. Friendly, observant, impossible to rush.

Mo lets the crew use the flat upstairs. He needs the downstairs business kept out of whatever is happening above it. He will help Femi, but will not lie about an injury.

Runs the Lea Boys, a rival bike crew working out of Leyton across the Marshes. Wants Pat's patch. Thinks you are it.

The Lea Boys’ lanky organiser. Never raises his voice when someone else is watching.

Stretch buys debts, recruits frightened people and calls it opportunity. He wants Pat’s routes and believes Danny is the cheapest way in.

01 · Player Guide

Welcome to the ends

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Hackney. Rent is due, your phone is cracked, and Auntie Pat wants bikes. You live in the gap between the next job and the next payday. The Chainring is your crew; London is full of work, grudges and a better angle.

Before the first night

Agree the tone and boundaries together: comic capers, grounded crime or something between. Talk about police violence, injury, addiction, debt and bystanders. Anyone can pause the fiction. The opening does not require cruelty to uninvolved people.

Your first five clicks

  1. Open your assigned character or finish the creation wizard.
  2. Click a stat on the sheet and choose the agreed difficulty.
  3. Open the Blower with Alt+B and read the current job.
  4. Right-click a motor, board the driver seat, then move the motor.
  5. Use a map exit’s travel button; use Alt+N for the route.
When it kicks off

Read each chat card and answer it. Chase assistance is off by default. If the table enables it, NPC actions still wait for Continue and each new round waits for Begin round.

Keep it to hand

01 · Player Guide

Read your character sheet

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

The top strip shows Health, Hustle, cash and Heat. On the Street holds the nine stat dice, Guard and ready weapons. Target someone with Foundry’s T control, then click the weapon. First aid posts a treatment card for the patient or GM; Heal/Damage are direct bookkeeping controls for agreed effects.

Kit & Perks holds weapons, protection, tools, outfits and consumables. Drag items from the compendium or buy them at a shop. Wear/equip an item to activate its protection; use the item’s Use or Reload control for its action. One worn armour item applies at a time.

Rep & Conditions holds XP, level-up and condition controls. The sheet calculates modifiers and lists the sources. Stash is stored property, separate from carried cash. The identity fields tell the table who you are; they do not automatically create an NPC crew or property income.

Keep it to hand

01 · Player Guide

Make a new face

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

  1. Choose an adult character (18+), name, ends and look.
  2. Choose a background, then assign one d8, three d6 and five d4 across the nine stats. The suggested spread is editable.
  3. Pick one of that background’s three perks. Take its starting kit and cash, plus one optional extra.
  4. Add a hustle, vice, bond and ambition. Review and finish the creation wizard.

Start at Rep 1 with 0 XP, Health 8 + Grit modifier, Hustle 3, and Fists. Guard is calculated on the sheet. Finishing creation adds the kit; it does not spend a level-up.

01 · Player Guide

The roll

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Call the stakes first

Say what you want, what failure risks and whether this is a check, an opposed roll, teamwork or a progress challenge.

Effort d6 + Stat die + Stat modifier + other modifiers. Both dice normally explode: roll again on their highest face and add it, repeating when necessary.

Stat dieModifier
d4+2
d6+3
d8+4
d10+5
d12+6
d20+10

Difficulty

BandNormal base chance
Easyabout 85%
Mediumabout 60%
Hardabout 35%
Long Shotabout 12%

The system solves a target from your normal, unboosted dice. Hustle and a relevant perk improve the roll against that fixed target. An explicit target, such as someone’s Guard, takes precedence.

Buy an edge before rolling

ChoiceEffect
1 HustleStep Effort up one die.
2 HustleGain On a Roll for this roll.
One relevant perkStep the Stat die up once. Select it in the roll dialog.
On a RollBoth dice explode on their top two faces.
Off Your GameNeither die explodes. With On a Roll, the two cancel to normal explosions.

The die ladder is d4 → d6 → d8 → d10 → d12 → d20. Before the Empire tier, a temporary step above d12 becomes +2 instead. Condition penalties, worn protection and driving modifiers are applied by the sheet. On a Roll and Off Your Game sheet toggles clear after the roll.

Read the margin

Margin = total − target.

MarginResultProgress / consequences
−4 or lessProper Mess0 / 2
−3 to −1Bad Luck0 / 1
0Just About1 / 1
1–3Sorted1 / 0
4–7Smashed It2 / 0
8+Legendary3 / 0

A Bad Luck can become 1 progress and 1 consequence if the table accepts a cost. In teamwork, average everyone’s totals, round down, then read one margin. In a progress challenge, apply each contribution to the two tracks instead.

Explosions and breakthroughs

1 explosion: Nice One. 2: A Blinder. 3: Absolute Scenes. 4+: Front Page. These invite an appropriate fictional breakthrough; they do not automatically add flat damage. The hit card offers higher-severity conditions when relevant.

01 · Player Guide

Outcomes and combat

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Guard = passive 3 + base Guard (normally 4) + the better Moves/Grit modifier + equipped armour’s Guard bonus + conditions. A vehicle uses 6 + twice Size. An attack total that reaches Guard hits.

Damage = max(0, floor(margin + Impact − armour reduction)). Spend the correct ammo and resolve the chat card. The target’s owner or GM can Take hit or use an available Dodge reaction. A successful Moves roll reaching the incoming attack total avoids the whole hit; trying still spends the reaction. One card cannot apply damage twice.

DamageSeverityGM condition choices
0No harmNone
1–2Minor — bruised, shaken, knocked downBruised, Shaken, Prone
3–4Moderate — hurt, stunned, heldHurt, Stunned, Restrained
5–6Severe — bleeding, broken, scared stiffBleeding, In Pain, Broken, Bricking It
7+Critical — down and maybe outDown, Broken, Bleeding

With automatic damage off (the default), the GM may add one appropriate severity condition on a hit. It is a choice, not the whole list. A weapon’s own effect may also apply. Automatic damage changes who applies the numbers; it does not turn every suggested condition into an automatic effect.

  1. Select the participants and open the Combat Console. Begin a round: everyone rolls speed dice and reveals them. The GM can force a reveal; players reveal their own dice.
  2. Take the next action in the queue. Each speed die buys one action; roll attacks from the sheet, use a listed action, or agree another action with the GM.
  3. Resolve incoming hits, evasions, police decisions and other chat responses. Press Done for your action. An assisted NPC action pauses at Continue.
  4. At the end of the queue, review round-end harm and choices. Press Begin round to continue.
Moves dieSpeed dice
d41d6
d6 / d82d6
d10 / d123d6
d204d6

Stunned and Knackered each remove one speed die, minimum one. Down, Cuffed and surrendered characters get no actions. Highest speed die acts first; ties use Moves, then PC priority, name and die order. Reactions refresh each Console round. NPCs follow the queue as separate actors.

Common actions

ActionResolution
MoveUp to 6 squares on foot alongside your action in a chase.
Attack / reloadUse the weapon or reload control; the action ends when its responses are resolved.
AimSpend an action to step Effort up on the next shot.
Dodge action+2 Guard for this round; separate from a rolled Dodge reaction.
Grab / break freeGrab in reach. To break free, Muscle or Moves against the grabber’s Guard.
CuffEngaged with a Grabbed, Down, Restrained, Stunned or surrendered target. Automatic on Down/surrendered; otherwise Muscle against Guard −2.
Get up / yield / interactUse the Console’s appropriate action or agree the action with the GM.

Ranges and cover

Band / coverEffect
EngagedUp to 1.6 squares.
NearUp to 10 squares.
FarUp to 25 squares.
DistantBeyond 25 squares; distant fire −1.
Light cover+2 Guard.
Heavy cover+4 Guard and +1 armour reduction.
Full coverNo ordinary direct shot through it.

Weapon details

Burst uses 3 rounds for +2 Impact. A shotgun gets +2 Impact Engaged; a rifle suffers −2 to hit Engaged. A driver can fire a one-handed weapon at −2; two-handed fire from the driver seat is refused. A passenger fires at −1. Enclosed riders get +2 Guard, exposed riders do not, and a windowless seat cannot attack out.

Using Foundry’s core tracker

The core tracker uses exploding d6 + Moves modifier initiative, one action and one zone move per turn, with a reaction returning at the start of your turn. Bleeding deals 1 at turn end and Stunned clears there. Apply Burning’s 2 damage once per round manually on that tracker. The Console applies both round-end damage effects. Use the Console for the speed-die chase flow.

01 · Player Guide

Vehicles and London

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Right-click a motor and choose a seat. One driver steers; gunner/operator and passenger seats have their own roles. Riders shrink to half-square markers and travel with the motor. You must be beside it, with access to the chosen seat; cage seats open from outside. Driver permissions follow the seated character. Exit before trying to move your person independently.

A driving Wheels roll uses the motor’s Performance in place of Effort, plus your Wheels die and modifier, plus Handling. Each flat tyre steps Performance down once, gives Handling −2 and removes 2 Speed. Two flats also remove one vehicle speed die. A motor below half Body has about 85% Speed, rounded, minimum 2.

The chase drive gauge

BandDistance per actionHandling / check
GreenUp to effective SpeedNormal; no speed check.
YellowUp to rounded 1.5 × Speed−1 Handling; Medium Wheels check.
RedUp to rounded 2 × Speed−2 Handling; Hard Wheels check.
Beyond redRefusedEnd the action or choose another route.

Driving into a new band asks for its check once in that action. Movement is measured cumulatively, not reset by making several short drags. With Body 0, red is limited to the yellow distance. The green/yellow/red gauge belongs to chase actions; ordinary travel still checks collisions.

Passing over another motor

A move whose swept path crosses another vehicle’s body triggers an evasive manoeuvre, including normal travel outside combat. With automatic travel evasion enabled (default), the driver’s real Wheels roll appears in chat without opening a dialog. Turn that setting off for an owner/GM roll button. A player-owned empty vehicle drag can use the owner’s character; seat a driver for an unambiguous pilot.

ResultCollision
Sorted / Smashed It / LegendarySwerved clear.
Just AboutScrape: 1 Body each.
Bad LuckCollision damage rises with pace and vehicle size.
Proper MessHarder collision, riders take 2 damage and are Shaken; the move stops.

Evasion is Easy in green/ordinary travel, Medium in yellow and Hard in red. The unresolved roll and damage response hold movement and the next turn. An overlap already present at the start of a move is ignored so vehicles can separate. The crash is logged on the vehicle.

Road and vehicle abilities

Ordinary motors suffer −2 Wheels off-road. Off-road kit changes that to +1; nimble bikes avoid the penalty. Blue lights give +1 Wheels and ask traffic to yield. A cab’s tight turn adds +1 at junctions. Exposed seats have no cover; windowless seats cannot shoot out. Foldable vehicles can be carried only when empty. Docked hire bikes have no fence value. ANPR-equipped drivers can target a plate within 12 squares and scan it.

Police vehicles roll speed dice from Performance: d4 gives 1d6; d6/d8 2d6; d10/d12 3d6; d20 4d6. A driver uses the better of their own action count and the motor’s. Two flat tyres or 0 Body each remove one vehicle die, minimum one; burning and parked police units have no driving actions. Ordinary civilian traffic uses its shared phase instead of individual speed dice.

Assistance starts OFF

Chase combat does not start itself by default. The GM can start a chase from the Combat Console; a participating player can manage it in Self-play. World settings can opt into automatic chase starts or NPC assistance. Turn Assist on or off for the current chase in the Console.

  1. Begin a round and reveal speed dice. PCs and each police unit receive their own action entries. Ordinary, unoccupied civilian traffic receives one shared Traffic phase at the end of the queue.
  2. For a PC action, move and choose your action, answer its chat cards, then press Done. A police unit acts separately. With Assist on, it takes only that action, animates it, and stops for Continue.
  3. Resolve every pending hit, driving check, evasive manoeuvre, PIT or police decision before advancing. Responses do not time out. Police and ambient traffic hold while a decision is open.
  4. All moving civilian traffic advances together in its shared phase. Review the round, then press Begin round. No automatic chain of new rounds.

NPC assistance waits 3 seconds by default before acting; the world setting allows 2–10 seconds. The Continue gate remains whatever delay you choose. The helicopter follows through its turns rather than teleporting to the suspect.

Finish the pursuit

At round end, a wanted PC more than 30 squares from every pursuing police unit loses one star. Repeat escapes until 0. If the police lose visual contact (all beyond 14 squares), the chase can enter searching; the search checks whether you remain unseen rather than bringing police straight back to you. The helicopter still matters outdoors at high Heat. A successful stop response follows the one-star and one-opening procedure below.

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

A map exit waits for pending decisions. After crossing, the chase resumes on the destination map with a new round. A police-shift pursuit callout has its own small gap track; its rules are in Work the Borough and do not replace this wanted-PC chase.

Keep it to hand

01 · Player Guide

Heat, cash and consequences

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

StarsWanted stateResponseOut of sight to lose 1 star
0CleanNobody is looking for you.—
1ClockedA patrol has your description. Cops who see you will stop you.45 seconds
2WantedArea cars hunt you and give chase on sight.60 seconds
3India 99The NPAS helicopter is up: it spots you anywhere outdoors on this map.90 seconds
4TrojansAn Armed Response Vehicle joins the hunt. Its officers will shoot.120 seconds
5LockdownRoadblocks on the exits of the map. Every spare unit joins in, up to the map's police limit.150 seconds

Crime Heat is added when a crime is witnessed, and each crime has a ceiling it cannot push you past. Thieving, carjacking, graffiti and bad driving never take you above 1 star, however often you do them. A fight tops out at 2 stars and gunfire at 3. Only taking a life brings 4 stars and armed police; a second killing, or killing a police officer, brings 5. A police witness adds +1, up to the same ceiling (killings excepted). A lesser crime never lowers your Heat. The GM can report a crime or set stars on the sheet. The system records recent crimes for stop outcomes; setting stars alone does not invent a gun crime.

Witnessed crimeHeat
Pickpocketing1★ at most
Nicking a bike1★ at most
Nicking a car1★ at most
Carjacking1★ at most
Witnessed illegal graffiti1★ at most
Dangerous driving1★ at most
Failing to stop for police+1★, up to 2★
Assault+1★, up to 2★
Assaulting a police officer2★
Stealing a police vehicle2★
Firing a gunat least 2★, up to 3★
Killing someoneat least 4★, up to 5★
Killing a police officer5★

Police vehicles sent: 1 at 1 star, 2 at 2 stars, 2 and the helicopter at 3 stars, 3 at 4 stars including an Armed Response Vehicle, and 6 at 5 stars with roadblocks. There are never more than the GM's Heat: most police vehicles on a map setting (4 unless changed); the helicopter and officers on foot are extra. When the stars come down, extra units that no character can see go back to base.

On ordinary streets, stay more than 14 squares from police to cool down. At 3+ stars the helicopter observes outdoors across the map; get indoors or resolve the chase. During a turn-based chase, use its round-end escape and search rules. Ordinary cooldown does not run over a live Console fight or an unresolved police stop.

A police stop

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

Busted and Wasted

Busted: custody, Heat 0, at least 1 Health and +1 Known to police. Lose the smaller of your cash or max(£100, rounded 20% of cash). Weapons except Fists, ammo, drugs and police/paramedic uniforms are confiscated. Conditions clear except Broken. Your stash is safe.

Wasted: hospital, full Health and Heat 0. Lose the smaller of your cash or max(£50, rounded 10% of cash). Conditions clear except Broken; Down counters reset. Wasted does not promise a Hustle refill. Stash remains safe.

01 · Player Guide

Work, recovery and growth

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

  1. Get into a job-capable motor as driver. Right-click it or use the Blower to start the matching shift.
  2. Accept or decline the incoming Blower offer. Read its current stage and follow the sat nav to the named pickup, patient, incident or stop.
  3. Use the linked roll button when prompted; supply a free passenger, prisoner or patient seat when needed. Complete the handover to finish the call.
  4. Cash, XP and any standing are paid to the recorded shift driver. Crew may help with authorised call rolls; cash is not automatically split among riders. End the shift when done.
WorkLoop
TaxiPick up with a spare seat, drive to the destination; fare and tip depend on the route, time and ride result.
CourierCollect then deliver; time left and parcel damage affect the pay.
PoliceANPR sweep, scripted pursuit or disturbance; make the arrest, load a cage seat and hand over at custody.
ParamedicTreat with Savvy Medium, load a free patient seat, stabilise on the way and hand over at A&E.
FireGet on scene and hose it down: Grit Hard, 4 progress before 3 consequences.
BusFour stops including a district crossing. Each stop pays; completing the route adds £10 and 1 XP.
The ChainringAsk Pat for an order, find the specified models, deliver the accepted stolen motors to her.

Deadlines and patient deterioration use the job clock. Pausing the world/shift clock protects remaining time; resuming adjusts the deadlines. A Banana Watch calendar jump is a different clock. Map transitions carry active calls, passengers and routes with you.

Service / actionWhat happensRequirements / default cost
First aid on sheetSavvy Medium; +2 Health, remove Bleeding and Hurt once per injury. Patient/GM applies.Within 2.2 squares.
RestFull Health and Hustle. Clears conditions except Broken, Cuffed, Restrained and Grabbed. Clears up to 2 Heat.Safehouse/flat, not Bleeding, Heat below 3 and police farther than 14 squares.
A&EFull Health; clears conditions except Broken.Free; refused at Heat 2+. Broken still needs its week and GM confirmation.
Change clothes (service)Lose 1 star.£25; police cannot observe you.
Respray & new platesClear Heat and the ANPR marker, replace plate. The car remains stolen.£100; police cannot observe you.
GarageFull Body, clear flats and field-patch limit. Cannot restore a burned-out wreck.£10 × (missing Body + 6 per flat).
Own outfitApply that item’s Heat drop at 1–2 stars if unseen; 10-minute change cooldown.Use Wear on the owned outfit. No Heat drop at 3+.

Service prices are world settings; the Local services menu shows the actual quote before purchase. At Heat 3+ a helicopter outdoors counts as observation for paid services. Wearing a disguise in sight of real officers can create trouble instead of erasing it.

Field repair is a separate action

The vehicle-sheet Patch up move is limited until a garage repair and uses its own result card. A Toolkit use rolls Graft, Medium, and changes one flat first; otherwise it repairs 1 / 2 / 4 / full Body on Just About / Sorted / Smashed It / Legendary. Read the item control being used; neither is a paid garage visit.

A job pays cash and XP to its recorded driver; mission rewards use the registered mission crew. Spend XP through the Level up wizard: odd levels raise a stat, even levels add a perk, every third level adds Growth, and each new tier adds Hustle. The full ladder runs to 33.

Keep it to hand

01 · Player Guide

Live pirate radio

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

The Blower

Alt+B or the phone control opens your Blower. Choose your PC and read Heat, cash, current ride, shifts, Pat’s orders and mission briefs. Use the card’s current action and sat nav; older completed chat cards are records of what happened.

Sat nav

Alt+N or the navigation control opens the map route. It follows real roads and the next active destination. Choose a contact or service manually when needed. Routes are private to your player; fold, zoom or use heading-up view. A wanted-ride sale route sends you to a suitable target until you are actually driving the motor the buyer wants, then points to the drop-off.

Pirate radio

Open the radio from the Blower or scene controls. Choose one of six live presets and press Listen to unlock audio in your browser. Audio is streamed from the station, so availability depends on that station. In a shared car the driver chooses the station; each rider keeps their own volume and mute. Off-car listening is personal. Studio links open the station’s chat or contact site/app; they do not send a message for you.

Crew bar

Your assigned PC comes first. Hover for Health, Hustle, cash and Heat; click to view the character, right-click to open the sheet. Use the grip to move the bar and double-click to fold it. The GM can view the whole crew.

Banana Watch and drug effects

The Banana Watch shows the world clock, or real London time if selected. Unpaused world time normally advances one second per second. The GM’s crown can set the date or jump by 15 minutes, an hour, six hours, a day or a week. Drug screen effects are personal to your owned PC: Full, Subtle or Off in client settings; reduced-motion uses Subtle. The GM has a preview. Turning the screen effect off does not remove the condition’s mechanical effects.

01 · Player Guide

When a fight goes wrong

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

At 0 Health, Down is added and you cannot act; Down also gives −4 Guard. In the Console, each round spent Down adds one to the counter. At three Down rounds you are Wasted. A Proper Mess on the Grit / Stay Conscious check can make you Wasted immediately; an ordinary failed check does not do so by itself.

The sheet’s First aid action targets someone within 2.2 squares: roll Savvy, Medium. On success the patient’s owner or GM presses Apply: +2 Health and remove Bleeding and Hurt. Only one treatment applies per injury; new damage opens a new opportunity. Healing above 0 removes Down and resets its counter.

A First Aid Kit is a separate consumable: its own Savvy check, healing and removals are shown in the kit table. A failed use consumes the kit. Do not apply the consumable and the sheet’s treatment as if they were the same button.

Resolve the situation

Stop the bleeding, get the casualty safe, and choose help or surrender when appropriate. Review Wasted and Busted costs before the GM applies those outcomes.

02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

The first night

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

Opening read-aloud

The train passes so close overhead that the tea trembles in its mug. Beneath the railway arch, a wheel turns in Spanner’s stand with a soft, steady tick. Auntie Pat is counting notes on a rubber mat. She looks up as you come in. “Right. Nobody’s dead, nobody’s late, and I’ve got a customer. Let’s try and keep all three of those things true.”

Introduce the crew

Ask each player where they slept, what is due before Friday, and who they last disappointed. Pat offers tea. Kez has two locations on their phone. Spanner lends bolt cutters if the party did not buy a set. Nobody starts owing a debt they did not agree to play.

Teach selecting a token and opening the sheet. Let each player make a harmless practice Medium roll. Explain that a practice result has no Heat. Open the Blower and show how to follow an instruction before turning the clocks on.

Campaign pressure clocks

Track Pat’s trust (0–4), the Lea Boys’ interest (0–4), and Vale’s case (0–4) in GM notes. A clean delivery raises trust. Public cruelty or lying about a loss lowers it. A visible incursion on Stretch’s patch raises interest. Repeated witnesses and plates raise the case. These are GM story clocks; they are distinct from the automated Heat stars.

A clean recovery earns Pat's Renown and opens the night shed's receiving hall (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM7}). The crate's clearance papers point to @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB8} Orchard Lease Office — first thread of the Quiet Ledger. Backing Stretch changes who sits across from you in @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.edb072b261a9b83d]{LB2}.

02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

Adjudicate the streets

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

Call the stakes first

Say what you want, what failure risks and whether this is a check, an opposed roll, teamwork or a progress challenge.

Effort d6 + Stat die + Stat modifier + other modifiers. Both dice normally explode: roll again on their highest face and add it, repeating when necessary.

Stat dieModifier
d4+2
d6+3
d8+4
d10+5
d12+6
d20+10

Difficulty

BandNormal base chance
Easyabout 85%
Mediumabout 60%
Hardabout 35%
Long Shotabout 12%

The system solves a target from your normal, unboosted dice. Hustle and a relevant perk improve the roll against that fixed target. An explicit target, such as someone’s Guard, takes precedence.

Buy an edge before rolling

ChoiceEffect
1 HustleStep Effort up one die.
2 HustleGain On a Roll for this roll.
One relevant perkStep the Stat die up once. Select it in the roll dialog.
On a RollBoth dice explode on their top two faces.
Off Your GameNeither die explodes. With On a Roll, the two cancel to normal explosions.

The die ladder is d4 → d6 → d8 → d10 → d12 → d20. Before the Empire tier, a temporary step above d12 becomes +2 instead. Condition penalties, worn protection and driving modifiers are applied by the sheet. On a Roll and Off Your Game sheet toggles clear after the roll.

Read the margin

Margin = total − target.

MarginResultProgress / consequences
−4 or lessProper Mess0 / 2
−3 to −1Bad Luck0 / 1
0Just About1 / 1
1–3Sorted1 / 0
4–7Smashed It2 / 0
8+Legendary3 / 0

A Bad Luck can become 1 progress and 1 consequence if the table accepts a cost. In teamwork, average everyone’s totals, round down, then read one margin. In a progress challenge, apply each contribution to the two tracks instead.

Explosions and breakthroughs

1 explosion: Nice One. 2: A Blinder. 3: Absolute Scenes. 4+: Front Page. These invite an appropriate fictional breakthrough; they do not automatically add flat damage. The hit card offers higher-severity conditions when relevant.

Guard = passive 3 + base Guard (normally 4) + the better Moves/Grit modifier + equipped armour’s Guard bonus + conditions. A vehicle uses 6 + twice Size. An attack total that reaches Guard hits.

Damage = max(0, floor(margin + Impact − armour reduction)). Spend the correct ammo and resolve the chat card. The target’s owner or GM can Take hit or use an available Dodge reaction. A successful Moves roll reaching the incoming attack total avoids the whole hit; trying still spends the reaction. One card cannot apply damage twice.

DamageSeverityGM condition choices
0No harmNone
1–2Minor — bruised, shaken, knocked downBruised, Shaken, Prone
3–4Moderate — hurt, stunned, heldHurt, Stunned, Restrained
5–6Severe — bleeding, broken, scared stiffBleeding, In Pain, Broken, Bricking It
7+Critical — down and maybe outDown, Broken, Bleeding

With automatic damage off (the default), the GM may add one appropriate severity condition on a hit. It is a choice, not the whole list. A weapon’s own effect may also apply. Automatic damage changes who applies the numbers; it does not turn every suggested condition into an automatic effect.

Service / actionWhat happensRequirements / default cost
First aid on sheetSavvy Medium; +2 Health, remove Bleeding and Hurt once per injury. Patient/GM applies.Within 2.2 squares.
RestFull Health and Hustle. Clears conditions except Broken, Cuffed, Restrained and Grabbed. Clears up to 2 Heat.Safehouse/flat, not Bleeding, Heat below 3 and police farther than 14 squares.
A&EFull Health; clears conditions except Broken.Free; refused at Heat 2+. Broken still needs its week and GM confirmation.
Change clothes (service)Lose 1 star.£25; police cannot observe you.
Respray & new platesClear Heat and the ANPR marker, replace plate. The car remains stolen.£100; police cannot observe you.
GarageFull Body, clear flats and field-patch limit. Cannot restore a burned-out wreck.£10 × (missing Body + 6 per flat).
Own outfitApply that item’s Heat drop at 1–2 stars if unseen; 10-minute change cooldown.Use Wear on the owned outfit. No Heat drop at 3+.

Service prices are world settings; the Local services menu shows the actual quote before purchase. At Heat 3+ a helicopter outdoors counts as observation for paid services. Wearing a disguise in sight of real officers can create trouble instead of erasing it.

Field repair is a separate action

The vehicle-sheet Patch up move is limited until a garage repair and uses its own result card. A Toolkit use rolls Graft, Medium, and changes one flat first; otherwise it repairs 1 / 2 / 4 / full Body on Just About / Sorted / Smashed It / Legendary. Read the item control being used; neither is a paid garage visit.

02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

Control the pace

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

Present one immediate problem and ask what the crew does. Resolve the chosen action, show the consequence and offer the next meaningful decision. Let a quiet job end cleanly. Use the job clock pause for discussion and the Console’s response gates for fights.

Choose the table’s mode

Story is the default. The GM controls mission starts and chase management. Self-play lets owners of PCs run missions and participating players manage their chase. A GM remains connected as world authority in both modes. Player ownership still applies to rolls and character responses.

ControlDefault / behaviour
Automatic chase startOff. Opt in in world settings; the Console can start one manually.
NPC chase assistanceOff. Assist is also a per-chase Console toggle.
NPC assistance delay3 seconds, adjustable 2–10; every NPC action still waits for Continue.
Automatic travel evasionOn. Rolls real Wheels when crossing another vehicle’s body; manual setting offers a chat roll button.
Automatic hit damageOff. Target owner/GM responds to the hit card.
Automatic crime HeatOn; witnessed incidents feed the Heat rules.
Street Life / jobs / shopsConfigure their world settings; pause the job clock to discuss a callout without losing its deadline.

Unanswered cards are deliberate pauses. Inspect the pending item in chat and resolve it before Done, Continue or Begin round. Do not start another Console fight over the same scene to work around a pending response.

What the GM supplies

Automatic event ticks, cash/XP, seat movement, dice, heat and traffic support the scene. NPC motives, fictional costs, influence favours, campaign fronts, access rights and plot outcomes still need decisions. Pick one consequence and offer the next meaningful choice; do not repeat cards after the situation is settled.

02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

A borough full of hooks

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

Twelve things that could happen next

  • Kez’s phone is stolen, and the thief is using it to accept Pat’s orders.
  • A courier offers a sealed envelope as payment for a repair.
  • A customer wants the bicycle they bought from Pat returned to its previous owner.
  • Spanner’s diagnostic unit shows that several vehicles share an impossible service history.
  • Vale needs a quiet driver for an off-the-record witness meeting.
  • Mo’s landlord arrives with a new padlock and a timetable.
  • A hire bike keeps reappearing outside the flat, no matter where the crew leaves it.
  • Leon wants out of the Lea Boys and has nowhere safe to go.
  • The cab driver recognises a passenger from a photograph Danny keeps folded in his wallet.
  • A fire callout happens at the building where the crew stashed their cash.
  • The person buying cars at Bow Breakers starts paying in favours.
  • A legal courier contract pays less than theft but could give the crew a real exit.

End on a choice

Offer a phone call, a person at the door or a name the crew recognises. Give the next session something specific to begin with. The city should grow out of their choices rather than resetting between jobs.

  4. Choose Story or Self-play. Leave automatic chase start and assistance off until the table wants them.

03 · Work the Borough

Start and finish a shift

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

  1. Get into a job-capable motor as driver. Right-click it or use the Blower to start the matching shift.
  2. Accept or decline the incoming Blower offer. Read its current stage and follow the sat nav to the named pickup, patient, incident or stop.
  3. Use the linked roll button when prompted; supply a free passenger, prisoner or patient seat when needed. Complete the handover to finish the call.
  4. Cash, XP and any standing are paid to the recorded shift driver. Crew may help with authorised call rolls; cash is not automatically split among riders. End the shift when done.
WorkLoop
TaxiPick up with a spare seat, drive to the destination; fare and tip depend on the route, time and ride result.
CourierCollect then deliver; time left and parcel damage affect the pay.
PoliceANPR sweep, scripted pursuit or disturbance; make the arrest, load a cage seat and hand over at custody.
ParamedicTreat with Savvy Medium, load a free patient seat, stabilise on the way and hand over at A&E.
FireGet on scene and hose it down: Grit Hard, 4 progress before 3 consequences.
BusFour stops including a district crossing. Each stop pays; completing the route adds £10 and 1 XP.
The ChainringAsk Pat for an order, find the specified models, deliver the accepted stolen motors to her.

Deadlines and patient deterioration use the job clock. Pausing the world/shift clock protects remaining time; resuming adjusts the deadlines. A Banana Watch calendar jump is a different clock. Map transitions carry active calls, passengers and routes with you.

03 · Work the Borough

Taxi and courier

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Taxi

  1. Take the driver seat of a taxi/minicab and start a shift. Accept the fare on the Blower.
  2. Drive to the pickup and leave a free passenger seat. Follow the arrival prompt; the passenger must board before the drop-off leg.
  3. Take the passenger to the destination. The system pays the driver’s fare and tip according to route, time left and the ride/chat result.

Courier

  1. Start a courier shift on a suitable bike or motor. Accept the pickup.
  2. Collect the parcel, then follow the route to the delivery.
  3. Arrive before the deadline. Damage and time affect the payment.

Each completed call gives 1 XP. Decline an offer you cannot service; end the shift if you are done. The Blower always shows the current stage and deadline.

03 · Work the Borough

Police · ANPR sweep

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

ANPR sweep

Read the Blower for the target plate. Target a motor within 12 squares and use Scan. The street may contain similar decoys: identify the right one. Approach with lights within 5 squares and roll Front Medium to signal a stop. If it stops, get out and approach within 2.6 squares, then Muscle Medium to cuff. A free prisoner cage is needed before loading; drive the prisoner to custody to complete the call.

Scripted pursuit callout

This shift mini-game starts with gap 2. At each requested Wheels roll, the target is round(4 + (getaway Wheels die faces + Performance die faces) / 2 + getaway Handling). Success reduces the gap by progress: Just About/Sorted 1, Smashed It 2, Legendary 3. Bad Luck opens it by 1; Proper Mess by 2 and causes a crash. Gap 0 catches; gap 5 escapes. Follow the call’s arrest and custody prompts after a catch. These gap numbers belong to police work, not the wanted-player Console chase.

Disturbance

Front Medium to calm it, or Muscle Medium to arrest. An arrest needs a spare cage seat and a custody handover. Completing police work awards the driver’s pay/XP and can remove one Heat star.

03 · Work the Borough

Paramedic

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

The patient begins Fading, then worsens every 45 job-clock seconds unless Stable: Stable → Fading → Faltering → Passing → Lost. A Savvy Medium treatment improves it two steps on Smashed It/Legendary or one on Sorted; Just About holds it steady, Bad Luck worsens it one step and Proper Mess two. Get the ambulance within 3.2 squares, use Treat and load, and leave a free stretcher/patient seat. Loading must succeed before the hospital leg can begin. Treat again on the move when asked. Lost or a missed deadline fails the call; a stable handover pays best.

03 · Work the Borough

Fire and bus

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Fire & rescue

Arrive at the fire and use the linked Grit Hard hose rolls. The incident is a challenge: 4 progress before 3 consequences, within 240 job-clock seconds once on scene. Crew can contribute; their rolls add to the same tracks. Proper Mess adds two consequences. A completed fire pays the driver and awards 1 XP.

Bus route

Accept the route, then serve all four stops in order, including the district crossing. Arrival pays each stop’s amount; the complete route adds a £10 bonus and 1 XP. Follow the next-stop route rather than returning to an old ping.

03 · Work the Borough

The Chainring

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Open the Blower or ask Pat for an order. She names the models and count she will accept; a tip-off is a lead, not ownership. Nick the specified motor, mark it stolen through the theft action and bring it to the right buyer. The sat nav looks for an eligible target until you are driving one Pat wants, then routes to the handover.

A sale pays the quoted fence money; completing the order adds the order’s bonus, 2 XP and Chainring standing. Bigger orders unlock with Rep; car work needs Rep 9. An order is side work, separate from the On Your Bike story mission. The same qualifying sale can satisfy an active mission objective if its rule matches.

03 · Work the Borough

Two crews, map crossings and paused shifts

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Each vehicle/shift keeps its own driver, active call and deadline. Check which character the Blower is displaying before responding. Accepted job rolls are available to the authorised crew; shift cash and XP go to the recorded driver, not automatically to every nearby PC.

Use the map exit button to carry the vehicle and its riders over a boundary. The job controller remaps its token references and continues the same stage; a second crew’s call stays with that crew. Pausing a shift or the world clock adjusts deadlines on resume, including patient worsening and offer timers. The Banana Watch calendar is a separate world clock.

Take a moment

Pause to read a call or settle a scene. In a chase, answer all pending chat choices before the map exit or next turn.

04 · Rules at a Glance

Combat and harm

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Guard = passive 3 + base Guard (normally 4) + the better Moves/Grit modifier + equipped armour’s Guard bonus + conditions. A vehicle uses 6 + twice Size. An attack total that reaches Guard hits.

Damage = max(0, floor(margin + Impact − armour reduction)). Spend the correct ammo and resolve the chat card. The target’s owner or GM can Take hit or use an available Dodge reaction. A successful Moves roll reaching the incoming attack total avoids the whole hit; trying still spends the reaction. One card cannot apply damage twice.

DamageSeverityGM condition choices
0No harmNone
1–2Minor — bruised, shaken, knocked downBruised, Shaken, Prone
3–4Moderate — hurt, stunned, heldHurt, Stunned, Restrained
5–6Severe — bleeding, broken, scared stiffBleeding, In Pain, Broken, Bricking It
7+Critical — down and maybe outDown, Broken, Bleeding

With automatic damage off (the default), the GM may add one appropriate severity condition on a hit. It is a choice, not the whole list. A weapon’s own effect may also apply. Automatic damage changes who applies the numbers; it does not turn every suggested condition into an automatic effect.

  1. Select the participants and open the Combat Console. Begin a round: everyone rolls speed dice and reveals them. The GM can force a reveal; players reveal their own dice.
  2. Take the next action in the queue. Each speed die buys one action; roll attacks from the sheet, use a listed action, or agree another action with the GM.
  3. Resolve incoming hits, evasions, police decisions and other chat responses. Press Done for your action. An assisted NPC action pauses at Continue.
  4. At the end of the queue, review round-end harm and choices. Press Begin round to continue.
Moves dieSpeed dice
d41d6
d6 / d82d6
d10 / d123d6
d204d6

Stunned and Knackered each remove one speed die, minimum one. Down, Cuffed and surrendered characters get no actions. Highest speed die acts first; ties use Moves, then PC priority, name and die order. Reactions refresh each Console round. NPCs follow the queue as separate actors.

Common actions

ActionResolution

AimSpend an action to step Effort up on the next shot.
Dodge action+2 Guard for this round; separate from a rolled Dodge reaction.

CuffEngaged with a Grabbed, Down, Restrained, Stunned or surrendered target. Automatic on Down/surrendered; otherwise Muscle against Guard −2.

Ranges and cover

Band / coverEffect
EngagedUp to 1.6 squares.
NearUp to 10 squares.
FarUp to 25 squares.
DistantBeyond 25 squares; distant fire −1.
Light cover+2 Guard.
Heavy cover+4 Guard and +1 armour reduction.

Weapon details

Burst uses 3 rounds for +2 Impact. A shotgun gets +2 Impact Engaged; a rifle suffers −2 to hit Engaged. A driver can fire a one-handed weapon at −2; two-handed fire from the driver seat is refused. A passenger fires at −1. Enclosed riders get +2 Guard, exposed riders do not, and a windowless seat cannot attack out.

Using Foundry’s core tracker

The core tracker uses exploding d6 + Moves modifier initiative, one action and one zone move per turn, with a reaction returning at the start of your turn. Bleeding deals 1 at turn end and Stunned clears there. Apply Burning’s 2 damage once per round manually on that tracker. The Console applies both round-end damage effects. Use the Console for the speed-die chase flow.

At 0 Health, Down is added and you cannot act; Down also gives −4 Guard. In the Console, each round spent Down adds one to the counter. At three Down rounds you are Wasted. A Proper Mess on the Grit / Stay Conscious check can make you Wasted immediately; an ordinary failed check does not do so by itself.

The sheet’s First aid action targets someone within 2.2 squares: roll Savvy, Medium. On success the patient’s owner or GM presses Apply: +2 Health and remove Bleeding and Hurt. Only one treatment applies per injury; new damage opens a new opportunity. Healing above 0 removes Down and resets its counter.

A First Aid Kit is a separate consumable: its own Savvy check, healing and removals are shown in the kit table. A failed use consumes the kit. Do not apply the consumable and the sheet’s treatment as if they were the same button.

Resolve the situation

Stop the bleeding, get the casualty safe, and choose help or surrender when appropriate. Review Wasted and Busted costs before the GM applies those outcomes.

04 · Rules at a Glance

Vehicles and chases

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Right-click a motor and choose a seat. One driver steers; gunner/operator and passenger seats have their own roles. Riders shrink to half-square markers and travel with the motor. You must be beside it, with access to the chosen seat; cage seats open from outside. Driver permissions follow the seated character. Exit before trying to move your person independently.

A driving Wheels roll uses the motor’s Performance in place of Effort, plus your Wheels die and modifier, plus Handling. Each flat tyre steps Performance down once, gives Handling −2 and removes 2 Speed. Two flats also remove one vehicle speed die. A motor below half Body has about 85% Speed, rounded, minimum 2.

The chase drive gauge

BandDistance per actionHandling / check
GreenUp to effective SpeedNormal; no speed check.
YellowUp to rounded 1.5 × Speed−1 Handling; Medium Wheels check.
RedUp to rounded 2 × Speed−2 Handling; Hard Wheels check.
Beyond redRefusedEnd the action or choose another route.

Driving into a new band asks for its check once in that action. Movement is measured cumulatively, not reset by making several short drags. With Body 0, red is limited to the yellow distance. The green/yellow/red gauge belongs to chase actions; ordinary travel still checks collisions.

Passing over another motor

A move whose swept path crosses another vehicle’s body triggers an evasive manoeuvre, including normal travel outside combat. With automatic travel evasion enabled (default), the driver’s real Wheels roll appears in chat without opening a dialog. Turn that setting off for an owner/GM roll button. A player-owned empty vehicle drag can use the owner’s character; seat a driver for an unambiguous pilot.

ResultCollision
Sorted / Smashed It / LegendarySwerved clear.
Just AboutScrape: 1 Body each.
Bad LuckCollision damage rises with pace and vehicle size.
Proper MessHarder collision, riders take 2 damage and are Shaken; the move stops.

Evasion is Easy in green/ordinary travel, Medium in yellow and Hard in red. The unresolved roll and damage response hold movement and the next turn. An overlap already present at the start of a move is ignored so vehicles can separate. The crash is logged on the vehicle.

Road and vehicle abilities

Ordinary motors suffer −2 Wheels off-road. Off-road kit changes that to +1; nimble bikes avoid the penalty. Blue lights give +1 Wheels and ask traffic to yield. A cab’s tight turn adds +1 at junctions. Exposed seats have no cover; windowless seats cannot shoot out. Foldable vehicles can be carried only when empty. Docked hire bikes have no fence value. ANPR-equipped drivers can target a plate within 12 squares and scan it.

Police vehicles roll speed dice from Performance: d4 gives 1d6; d6/d8 2d6; d10/d12 3d6; d20 4d6. A driver uses the better of their own action count and the motor’s. Two flat tyres or 0 Body each remove one vehicle die, minimum one; burning and parked police units have no driving actions. Ordinary civilian traffic uses its shared phase instead of individual speed dice.

Assistance starts OFF

Chase combat does not start itself by default. The GM can start a chase from the Combat Console; a participating player can manage it in Self-play. World settings can opt into automatic chase starts or NPC assistance. Turn Assist on or off for the current chase in the Console.

  1. Begin a round and reveal speed dice. PCs and each police unit receive their own action entries. Ordinary, unoccupied civilian traffic receives one shared Traffic phase at the end of the queue.
  2. For a PC action, move and choose your action, answer its chat cards, then press Done. A police unit acts separately. With Assist on, it takes only that action, animates it, and stops for Continue.
  3. Resolve every pending hit, driving check, evasive manoeuvre, PIT or police decision before advancing. Responses do not time out. Police and ambient traffic hold while a decision is open.
  4. All moving civilian traffic advances together in its shared phase. Review the round, then press Begin round. No automatic chain of new rounds.

NPC assistance waits 3 seconds by default before acting; the world setting allows 2–10 seconds. The Continue gate remains whatever delay you choose. The helicopter follows through its turns rather than teleporting to the suspect.

Finish the pursuit

At round end, a wanted PC more than 30 squares from every pursuing police unit loses one star. Repeat escapes until 0. If the police lose visual contact (all beyond 14 squares), the chase can enter searching; the search checks whether you remain unseen rather than bringing police straight back to you. The helicopter still matters outdoors at high Heat. A successful stop response follows the one-star and one-opening procedure below.

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

A map exit waits for pending decisions. After crossing, the chase resumes on the destination map with a new round. A police-shift pursuit callout has its own small gap track; its rules are in Work the Borough and do not replace this wanted-PC chase.

Rams, tyres and control

A ram does margin + 2 × attacker Size to the target. The attacker takes half that against a motor or a quarter against a person, rounded up. A person hurt by a ram is knocked Prone. A called shot at tyres is −2 to hit and blows one tyre when it succeeds. Resolve a PIT or ram defence card before either side advances.

Band / failureBody damage before protectionRider damage
yellow / Bad Luck20
yellow / Proper Mess40
red / Bad Luck30
red / Proper Mess72

Size 3+ adds 1 Body damage to a loss of control. The incident stops the move; a severe result also applies Shaken. A collision uses both vehicles’ sizes and the pace; read its chat card for each motor’s damage.

Fire and explosions

At 0 Body, a motor catches fire. In a chase it explodes at the end of the next round; outside one, after 15 seconds. A hit dealing 3+ to a burning motor can detonate it immediately. Get everybody out.

Heat and losses

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

StarsWanted stateResponseOut of sight to lose 1 star
0CleanNobody is looking for you.—

Crime Heat is added when a crime is witnessed, and each crime has a ceiling it cannot push you past. Thieving, carjacking, graffiti and bad driving never take you above 1 star, however often you do them. A fight tops out at 2 stars and gunfire at 3. Only taking a life brings 4 stars and armed police; a second killing, or killing a police officer, brings 5. A police witness adds +1, up to the same ceiling (killings excepted). A lesser crime never lowers your Heat. The GM can report a crime or set stars on the sheet. The system records recent crimes for stop outcomes; setting stars alone does not invent a gun crime.

Police vehicles sent: 1 at 1 star, 2 at 2 stars, 2 and the helicopter at 3 stars, 3 at 4 stars including an Armed Response Vehicle, and 6 at 5 stars with roadblocks. There are never more than the GM's Heat: most police vehicles on a map setting (4 unless changed); the helicopter and officers on foot are extra. When the stars come down, extra units that no character can see go back to base.

On ordinary streets, stay more than 14 squares from police to cool down. At 3+ stars the helicopter observes outdoors across the map; get indoors or resolve the chase. During a turn-based chase, use its round-end escape and search rules. Ordinary cooldown does not run over a live Console fight or an unresolved police stop.

A police stop

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

Busted and Wasted

Busted: custody, Heat 0, at least 1 Health and +1 Known to police. Lose the smaller of your cash or max(£100, rounded 20% of cash). Weapons except Fists, ammo, drugs and police/paramedic uniforms are confiscated. Conditions clear except Broken. Your stash is safe.

Wasted: hospital, full Health and Heat 0. Lose the smaller of your cash or max(£50, rounded 10% of cash). Conditions clear except Broken; Down counters reset. Wasted does not promise a Hustle refill. Stash remains safe.

Field repair is a separate action

A Toolkit use rolls Graft, Medium, and changes one flat first; otherwise it repairs 1 / 2 / 4 / full Body on Just About / Sorted / Smashed It / Legendary. A job pays cash and XP to its recorded driver; mission rewards use the registered mission crew. Spend XP through the Level up wizard: odd levels raise a stat, even levels add a perk, every third level adds Growth, and each new tier adds Hustle. The full ladder runs to 33.

On the Hackney Central map. The ambulance callout drops patients at the hospital’s road zone; Wasted characters wake inside A&E. A curtain, a trolley and a nurse who knows when somebody is withholding the useful half of the story.

Fire stations support scenarios. Taxi ranks and named landmarks offer callout destinations. Markets provide contacts and a place to change your look. The wider patch

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Dalston and Stoke Newington

Busy high streets, quieter side roads, markets and more observers than the crew first notices. Useful for a small theft with a large audience.

Haggerston, London Fields and the canal

Bicycles can choose routes a bulky van cannot. A pedestrian shortcut is useful until the person behind you knows it too. Keep the game’s path restrictions visible before a roll commits the plan.

Homerton, the Marshes and Wick

The Lea divides more than the map. Industrial yards, broad crossings and green space make pursuits feel different from the high street. Stretch’s influence lives in who answers the phone, not a painted border.

Stratford, Bethnal Green and Bow

Wider roads, busier destinations, the stadium and the breakers yard. A reliable place to earn money becomes somebody else’s reason to take notice.

06 · The Chainring · Faces

Your crew

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Jaz, Danny, Femi and Sal already know enough about each other to get in the same van. They do not have to agree about what happens when it stops. Read the full backstory on each character’s Identity tab; all four include their contacts and crew bonds.

Jaz Kaur

Wheels d8; Moves, Graft and Bottle d6. A courier with a mechanic’s hands and a garage-shaped ambition. Spanner’s good opinion matters to her. Bike Messenger and Grease Monkey are her situational edges.

Danny “Tealeaf” Doyle

Graft d8; Moves, Savvy and Front d6. A lock, a grin and a debt he does not quite explain. Pat gave him work when work mattered most. Locksmith and Silver Tongue fit the way he gets through a door.

Femi Adebayo

Savvy d8; Front, Bottle and Grit d6. He knows how to read a room and patch somebody up. His lines are clear even when keeping them is expensive. First Responder and Street Reader are his edges.

Big Sal Moretti

Muscle d8; Grit, Bottle and Wheels d6. Door staff, van driver and the person who says “leave it” before something becomes a fight. Door Staff and Hard to Shift are their edges.

06 · The Chainring · Faces

Under the arches

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Auntie Pat

The counter, the kettle, the ledger. Pat buys bikes, sets orders and values a quiet delivery. She protects the people who turn up for her, but she does not forget what something cost.

Spanner Rob

Mechanic and reluctant conscience. Ask him what is broken and he will tell you. Ask him why and you may get an answer you did not want.

Kez

Information has feet and a cracked phone screen. Kez knows where somebody parked and when they normally leave. They have plans of their own.

Mo Rahman

Chicken Palace’s owner and the flat’s anchor to an ordinary street. Kindness does not mean unlimited permission. He needs the business to survive whatever the crew brings home.

06 · The Chainring · Faces

Other people with your number

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Stretch and the Lea Boys

Stretch calls coercion opportunity. The Lea Boys around him are people with loyalties, debts and varying enthusiasm for his plans. An encounter can end with a deal, a refusal or someone deciding to leave.

DS Harriet Vale

She follows the same people and the same plates until a pattern makes a case. A conversation with her can be a threat or a route out. She has limits; do not mistake patience for forgetting.

Add somebody

Each player should name one person outside the crew who would notice if they did not come home. Tell the GM what that person knows, what they need, and the one favour the character would struggle to refuse.

What you can carry

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

The top strip shows Health, Hustle, cash and Heat. On the Street holds the nine stat dice, Guard and ready weapons. Target someone with Foundry’s T control, then click the weapon. First aid posts a treatment card for the patient or GM; Heal/Damage are direct bookkeeping controls for agreed effects.

Kit & Perks holds weapons, protection, tools, outfits and consumables. Drag items from the compendium or buy them at a shop. Wear/equip an item to activate its protection; use the item’s Use or Reload control for its action. One worn armour item applies at a time.

Rep & Conditions holds XP, level-up and condition controls. The sheet calculates modifiers and lists the sources. Stash is stored property, separate from carried cash. The identity fields tell the table who you are; they do not automatically create an NPC crew or property income.

Stand at the named shop/service zone and use Shops or Local services. A shop checks the customer, location, cash, stock and Rep gate; the quote is the actual price. Food, medicine, ammo and tools have Use buttons; wear armour and outfits to apply them. Stock and district prices vary.

Cash is what you carry. Use a safehouse stash to put cash and items aside; the stash survives Busted/Wasted. With automatic purchase handling off, follow the GM’s approval prompt instead of subtracting money twice. Shop gates are Rep 3, 6 and 9 for progressively restricted shelves. Chainring 3 gives Pat’s 10% discount, Street 5 gives 10% in shops, and Wide Boy gives 10%; combined discounts cap at 20%.

Theft and selling

Approach an accessible bike or motor and use its Theft action. The lock sets the Graft difficulty; tools and the chosen roll determine whether the attempt succeeds. Occupied motors require the carjack procedure rather than taking an occupied driver seat. A stolen motor must have its theft marker to sell. Pat buys eligible bikes, Bow Breakers eligible motors, and docked hire bikes are refused. Payout depends on value, Body, whether it is hot, buyer and Rep; use the quoted sale.

Weapons, protection and a way out

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Guard = passive 3 + base Guard (normally 4) + the better Moves/Grit modifier + equipped armour’s Guard bonus + conditions. A vehicle uses 6 + twice Size. An attack total that reaches Guard hits.

Damage = max(0, floor(margin + Impact − armour reduction)). Spend the correct ammo and resolve the chat card. The target’s owner or GM can Take hit or use an available Dodge reaction. A successful Moves roll reaching the incoming attack total avoids the whole hit; trying still spends the reaction. One card cannot apply damage twice.

DamageSeverityGM condition choices
0No harmNone
1–2Minor — bruised, shaken, knocked downBruised, Shaken, Prone
3–4Moderate — hurt, stunned, heldHurt, Stunned, Restrained
5–6Severe — bleeding, broken, scared stiffBleeding, In Pain, Broken, Bricking It
7+Critical — down and maybe outDown, Broken, Bleeding

With automatic damage off (the default), the GM may add one appropriate severity condition on a hit. It is a choice, not the whole list. A weapon’s own effect may also apply. Automatic damage changes who applies the numbers; it does not turn every suggested condition into an automatic effect.

Service / actionWhat happensRequirements / default cost
First aid on sheetSavvy Medium; +2 Health, remove Bleeding and Hurt once per injury. Patient/GM applies.Within 2.2 squares.
RestFull Health and Hustle. Clears conditions except Broken, Cuffed, Restrained and Grabbed. Clears up to 2 Heat.Safehouse/flat, not Bleeding, Heat below 3 and police farther than 14 squares.
A&EFull Health; clears conditions except Broken.Free; refused at Heat 2+. Broken still needs its week and GM confirmation.
Change clothes (service)Lose 1 star.£25; police cannot observe you.
Respray & new platesClear Heat and the ANPR marker, replace plate. The car remains stolen.£100; police cannot observe you.
GarageFull Body, clear flats and field-patch limit. Cannot restore a burned-out wreck.£10 × (missing Body + 6 per flat).
Own outfitApply that item’s Heat drop at 1–2 stars if unseen; 10-minute change cooldown.Use Wear on the owned outfit. No Heat drop at 3+.

Service prices are world settings; the Local services menu shows the actual quote before purchase. At Heat 3+ a helicopter outdoors counts as observation for paid services. Wearing a disguise in sight of real officers can create trouble instead of erasing it.

Field repair is a separate action

The vehicle-sheet Patch up move is limited until a garage repair and uses its own result card. A Toolkit use rolls Graft, Medium, and changes one flat first; otherwise it repairs 1 / 2 / 4 / full Body on Just About / Sorted / Smashed It / Legendary. Read the item control being used; neither is a paid garage visit.

The Smoke — Player's Handbook

Welcome to The Smoke

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Hackney. Rent is due, your phone is cracked, and Auntie Pat wants bikes. You live in the gap between the next job and the next payday. The Chainring is your crew; London is full of work, grudges and a better angle.

Before the first night

Agree the tone and boundaries together: comic capers, grounded crime or something between. Talk about police violence, injury, addiction, debt and bystanders. Anyone can pause the fiction. The opening does not require cruelty to uninvolved people.

Your first five clicks

  1. Open your assigned character or finish the creation wizard.
  2. Click a stat on the sheet and choose the agreed difficulty.
  3. Open the Blower with Alt+B and read the current job.
  4. Right-click a motor, board the driver seat, then move the motor.
  5. Use a map exit’s travel button; use Alt+N for the route.
When it kicks off

Read each chat card and answer it. Chase assistance is off by default. If the table enables it, NPC actions still wait for Continue and each new round waits for Begin round.

Making a Character

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

  1. Choose an adult character (18+), name, ends and look.
  2. Choose a background, then assign one d8, three d6 and five d4 across the nine stats. The suggested spread is editable.
  3. Pick one of that background’s three perks. Take its starting kit and cash, plus one optional extra.
  4. Add a hustle, vice, bond and ambition. Review and finish the creation wizard.

Start at Rep 1 with 0 XP, Health 8 + Grit modifier, Hustle 3, and Fists. Guard is calculated on the sheet. Finishing creation adds the kit; it does not spend a level-up.

Rolling the Dice

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Call the stakes first

Say what you want, what failure risks and whether this is a check, an opposed roll, teamwork or a progress challenge.

Effort d6 + Stat die + Stat modifier + other modifiers. Both dice normally explode: roll again on their highest face and add it, repeating when necessary.

Stat dieModifier
d4+2
d6+3
d8+4
d10+5
d12+6
d20+10

Difficulty

BandNormal base chance
Easyabout 85%
Mediumabout 60%
Hardabout 35%
Long Shotabout 12%

The system solves a target from your normal, unboosted dice. Hustle and a relevant perk improve the roll against that fixed target. An explicit target, such as someone’s Guard, takes precedence.

Buy an edge before rolling

ChoiceEffect
1 HustleStep Effort up one die.
2 HustleGain On a Roll for this roll.
One relevant perkStep the Stat die up once. Select it in the roll dialog.
On a RollBoth dice explode on their top two faces.
Off Your GameNeither die explodes. With On a Roll, the two cancel to normal explosions.

The die ladder is d4 → d6 → d8 → d10 → d12 → d20. Before the Empire tier, a temporary step above d12 becomes +2 instead. Condition penalties, worn protection and driving modifiers are applied by the sheet. On a Roll and Off Your Game sheet toggles clear after the roll.

Read the margin

Margin = total − target.

MarginResultProgress / consequences
−4 or lessProper Mess0 / 2
−3 to −1Bad Luck0 / 1
0Just About1 / 1
1–3Sorted1 / 0
4–7Smashed It2 / 0
8+Legendary3 / 0

A Bad Luck can become 1 progress and 1 consequence if the table accepts a cost. In teamwork, average everyone’s totals, round down, then read one margin. In a progress challenge, apply each contribution to the two tracks instead.

Explosions and breakthroughs

1 explosion: Nice One. 2: A Blinder. 3: Absolute Scenes. 4+: Front Page. These invite an appropriate fictional breakthrough; they do not automatically add flat damage. The hit card offers higher-severity conditions when relevant.
