Harm and Conditions

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Guard = passive 3 + base Guard (normally 4) + the better Moves/Grit modifier + equipped armour’s Guard bonus + conditions. A vehicle uses 6 + twice Size. An attack total that reaches Guard hits.

Damage = max(0, floor(margin + Impact − armour reduction)). Spend the correct ammo and resolve the chat card. The target’s owner or GM can Take hit or use an available Dodge reaction. A successful Moves roll reaching the incoming attack total avoids the whole hit; trying still spends the reaction. One card cannot apply damage twice.

DamageSeverityGM condition choices
0No harmNone
1–2Minor — bruised, shaken, knocked downBruised, Shaken, Prone
3–4Moderate — hurt, stunned, heldHurt, Stunned, Restrained
5–6Severe — bleeding, broken, scared stiffBleeding, In Pain, Broken, Bricking It
7+Critical — down and maybe outDown, Broken, Bleeding

With automatic damage off (the default), the GM may add one appropriate severity condition on a hit. It is a choice, not the whole list. A weapon’s own effect may also apply. Automatic damage changes who applies the numbers; it does not turn every suggested condition into an automatic effect.

At 0 Health, Down is added and you cannot act; Down also gives −4 Guard. In the Console, each round spent Down adds one to the counter. At three Down rounds you are Wasted. A Proper Mess on the Grit / Stay Conscious check can make you Wasted immediately; an ordinary failed check does not do so by itself.

The sheet’s First aid action targets someone within 2.2 squares: roll Savvy, Medium. On success the patient’s owner or GM presses Apply: +2 Health and remove Bleeding and Hurt. Only one treatment applies per injury; new damage opens a new opportunity. Healing above 0 removes Down and resets its counter.

A First Aid Kit is a separate consumable: its own Savvy check, healing and removals are shown in the kit table. A failed use consumes the kit. Do not apply the consumable and the sheet’s treatment as if they were the same button.

Resolve the situation

Stop the bleeding, get the casualty safe, and choose help or surrender when appropriate. Review Wasted and Busted costs before the GM applies those outcomes.

Heat and the Police

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

StarsWanted stateResponseOut of sight to lose 1 star
0CleanNobody is looking for you.—
1ClockedA patrol has your description. Cops who see you will stop you.45 seconds
2WantedArea cars hunt you and give chase on sight.60 seconds
3India 99The NPAS helicopter is up: it spots you anywhere outdoors on this map.90 seconds
4TrojansAn Armed Response Vehicle joins the hunt. Its officers will shoot.120 seconds
5LockdownRoadblocks on the exits of the map. Every spare unit joins in, up to the map's police limit.150 seconds

Crime Heat is added when a crime is witnessed, and each crime has a ceiling it cannot push you past. Thieving, carjacking, graffiti and bad driving never take you above 1 star, however often you do them. A fight tops out at 2 stars and gunfire at 3. Only taking a life brings 4 stars and armed police; a second killing, or killing a police officer, brings 5. A police witness adds +1, up to the same ceiling (killings excepted). A lesser crime never lowers your Heat. The GM can report a crime or set stars on the sheet. The system records recent crimes for stop outcomes; setting stars alone does not invent a gun crime.

Police vehicles sent: 1 at 1 star, 2 at 2 stars, 2 and the helicopter at 3 stars, 3 at 4 stars including an Armed Response Vehicle, and 6 at 5 stars with roadblocks. There are never more than the GM's Heat: most police vehicles on a map setting (4 unless changed); the helicopter and officers on foot are extra. When the stars come down, extra units that no character can see go back to base.

On ordinary streets, stay more than 14 squares from police to cool down. At 3+ stars the helicopter observes outdoors across the map; get indoors or resolve the chase. During a turn-based chase, use its round-end escape and search rules. Ordinary cooldown does not run over a live Console fight or an unresolved police stop.

A police stop

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

Busted and Wasted

Busted: custody, Heat 0, at least 1 Health and +1 Known to police. Lose the smaller of your cash or max(£100, rounded 20% of cash). Weapons except Fists, ammo, drugs and police/paramedic uniforms are confiscated. Conditions clear except Broken. Your stash is safe.

Wasted: hospital, full Health and Heat 0. Lose the smaller of your cash or max(£50, rounded 10% of cash). Conditions clear except Broken; Down counters reset. Wasted does not promise a Hustle refill. Stash remains safe.

Fighting

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

  1. Select the participants and open the Combat Console. Begin a round: everyone rolls speed dice and reveals them. The GM can force a reveal; players reveal their own dice.
  2. Take the next action in the queue. Each speed die buys one action; roll attacks from the sheet, use a listed action, or agree another action with the GM.
  3. Resolve incoming hits, evasions, police decisions and other chat responses. Press Done for your action. An assisted NPC action pauses at Continue.
  4. At the end of the queue, review round-end harm and choices. Press Begin round to continue.

Stunned and Knackered each remove one speed die, minimum one. Down, Cuffed and surrendered characters get no actions. Highest speed die acts first; ties use Moves, then PC priority, name and die order. Reactions refresh each Console round. NPCs follow the queue as separate actors.

Weapon details

Burst uses 3 rounds for +2 Impact. A shotgun gets +2 Impact Engaged; a rifle suffers −2 to hit Engaged. A driver can fire a one-handed weapon at −2; two-handed fire from the driver seat is refused. A passenger fires at −1. Enclosed riders get +2 Guard, exposed riders do not, and a windowless seat cannot attack out.

Using Foundry’s core tracker

The core tracker uses exploding d6 + Moves modifier initiative, one action and one zone move per turn, with a reaction returning at the start of your turn. Bleeding deals 1 at turn end and Stunned clears there. Apply Burning’s 2 damage once per round manually on that tracker. The Console applies both round-end damage effects. Use the Console for the speed-die chase flow.

Guard = passive 3 + base Guard (normally 4) + the better Moves/Grit modifier + equipped armour’s Guard bonus + conditions. A vehicle uses 6 + twice Size. An attack total that reaches Guard hits.

Damage = max(0, floor(margin + Impact − armour reduction)). Spend the correct ammo and resolve the chat card. The target’s owner or GM can Take hit or use an available Dodge reaction. A successful Moves roll reaching the incoming attack total avoids the whole hit; trying still spends the reaction. One card cannot apply damage twice.

With automatic damage off (the default), the GM may add one appropriate severity condition on a hit. It is a choice, not the whole list. A weapon’s own effect may also apply. Automatic damage changes who applies the numbers; it does not turn every suggested condition into an automatic effect.

Motors

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Right-click a motor and choose a seat. One driver steers; gunner/operator and passenger seats have their own roles. Riders shrink to half-square markers and travel with the motor. You must be beside it, with access to the chosen seat; cage seats open from outside. Driver permissions follow the seated character. Exit before trying to move your person independently.

A driving Wheels roll uses the motor’s Performance in place of Effort, plus your Wheels die and modifier, plus Handling. Each flat tyre steps Performance down once, gives Handling −2 and removes 2 Speed. Two flats also remove one vehicle speed die. A motor below half Body has about 85% Speed, rounded, minimum 2.

The chase drive gauge

BandDistance per actionHandling / check

YellowUp to rounded 1.5 × Speed−1 Handling; Medium Wheels check.
RedUp to rounded 2 × Speed−2 Handling; Hard Wheels check.

Driving into a new band asks for its check once in that action. Movement is measured cumulatively, not reset by making several short drags. With Body 0, red is limited to the yellow distance. The green/yellow/red gauge belongs to chase actions; ordinary travel still checks collisions.

Passing over another motor

A move whose swept path crosses another vehicle’s body triggers an evasive manoeuvre, including normal travel outside combat. With automatic travel evasion enabled (default), the driver’s real Wheels roll appears in chat without opening a dialog. Turn that setting off for an owner/GM roll button. A player-owned empty vehicle drag can use the owner’s character; seat a driver for an unambiguous pilot.

Evasion is Easy in green/ordinary travel, Medium in yellow and Hard in red. The unresolved roll and damage response hold movement and the next turn. An overlap already present at the start of a move is ignored so vehicles can separate. The crash is logged on the vehicle.

Road and vehicle abilities

Ordinary motors suffer −2 Wheels off-road. Off-road kit changes that to +1; nimble bikes avoid the penalty. Blue lights give +1 Wheels and ask traffic to yield. A cab’s tight turn adds +1 at junctions. Exposed seats have no cover; windowless seats cannot shoot out. Foldable vehicles can be carried only when empty. Docked hire bikes have no fence value. ANPR-equipped drivers can target a plate within 12 squares and scan it.

Rams, tyres and control

A ram does margin + 2 × attacker Size to the target. The attacker takes half that against a motor or a quarter against a person, rounded up. A person hurt by a ram is knocked Prone. A called shot at tyres is −2 to hit and blows one tyre when it succeeds. Resolve a PIT or ram defence card before either side advances.

Jobs

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

  1. Get into a job-capable motor as driver. Right-click it or use the Blower to start the matching shift.
  2. Accept or decline the incoming Blower offer. Read its current stage and follow the sat nav to the named pickup, patient, incident or stop.
  3. Use the linked roll button when prompted; supply a free passenger, prisoner or patient seat when needed. Complete the handover to finish the call.
  4. Cash, XP and any standing are paid to the recorded shift driver. Crew may help with authorised call rolls; cash is not automatically split among riders. End the shift when done.
WorkLoop
TaxiPick up with a spare seat, drive to the destination; fare and tip depend on the route, time and ride result.
CourierCollect then deliver; time left and parcel damage affect the pay.
PoliceANPR sweep, scripted pursuit or disturbance; make the arrest, load a cage seat and hand over at custody.
ParamedicTreat with Savvy Medium, load a free patient seat, stabilise on the way and hand over at A&E.
FireGet on scene and hose it down: Grit Hard, 4 progress before 3 consequences.
BusFour stops including a district crossing. Each stop pays; completing the route adds £10 and 1 XP.
The ChainringAsk Pat for an order, find the specified models, deliver the accepted stolen motors to her.

Deadlines and patient deterioration use the job clock. Pausing the world/shift clock protects remaining time; resuming adjusts the deadlines. A Banana Watch calendar jump is a different clock. Map transitions carry active calls, passengers and routes with you.

Money and Shops

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Stand at the named shop/service zone and use Shops or Local services. A shop checks the customer, location, cash, stock and Rep gate; the quote is the actual price. Food, medicine, ammo and tools have Use buttons; wear armour and outfits to apply them. Stock and district prices vary.

Cash is what you carry. Use a safehouse stash to put cash and items aside; the stash survives Busted/Wasted. With automatic purchase handling off, follow the GM’s approval prompt instead of subtracting money twice. Shop gates are Rep 3, 6 and 9 for progressively restricted shelves. Chainring 3 gives Pat’s 10% discount, Street 5 gives 10% in shops, and Wide Boy gives 10%; combined discounts cap at 20%.

Theft and selling

Approach an accessible bike or motor and use its Theft action. The lock sets the Graft difficulty; tools and the chosen roll determine whether the attempt succeeds. Occupied motors require the carjack procedure rather than taking an occupied driver seat. A stolen motor must have its theft marker to sell. Pat buys eligible bikes, Bow Breakers eligible motors, and docked hire bikes are refused. Payout depends on value, Body, whether it is hot, buyer and Rep; use the quoted sale.

Field repair is a separate action

The vehicle-sheet Patch up move is limited until a garage repair and uses its own result card. A Toolkit use rolls Graft, Medium, and changes one flat first; otherwise it repairs 1 / 2 / 4 / full Body on Just About / Sorted / Smashed It / Legendary. Read the item control being used; neither is a paid garage visit.

Chases and Police Stops

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

Police vehicles roll speed dice from Performance: d4 gives 1d6; d6/d8 2d6; d10/d12 3d6; d20 4d6. A driver uses the better of their own action count and the motor’s. Two flat tyres or 0 Body each remove one vehicle die, minimum one; burning and parked police units have no driving actions. Ordinary civilian traffic uses its shared phase instead of individual speed dice.

Assistance starts OFF

Chase combat does not start itself by default. The GM can start a chase from the Combat Console; a participating player can manage it in Self-play. World settings can opt into automatic chase starts or NPC assistance. Turn Assist on or off for the current chase in the Console.

  1. Begin a round and reveal speed dice. PCs and each police unit receive their own action entries. Ordinary, unoccupied civilian traffic receives one shared Traffic phase at the end of the queue.
  2. For a PC action, move and choose your action, answer its chat cards, then press Done. A police unit acts separately. With Assist on, it takes only that action, animates it, and stops for Continue.
  3. Resolve every pending hit, driving check, evasive manoeuvre, PIT or police decision before advancing. Responses do not time out. Police and ambient traffic hold while a decision is open.
  4. All moving civilian traffic advances together in its shared phase. Review the round, then press Begin round. No automatic chain of new rounds.

NPC assistance waits 3 seconds by default before acting; the world setting allows 2–10 seconds. The Continue gate remains whatever delay you choose. The helicopter follows through its turns rather than teleporting to the suspect.

Finish the pursuit

At round end, a wanted PC more than 30 squares from every pursuing police unit loses one star. Repeat escapes until 0. If the police lose visual contact (all beyond 14 squares), the chase can enter searching; the search checks whether you remain unseen rather than bringing police straight back to you. The helicopter still matters outdoors at high Heat. A successful stop response follows the one-star and one-opening procedure below.

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

A map exit waits for pending decisions. After crossing, the chase resumes on the destination map with a new round. A police-shift pursuit callout has its own small gap track; its rules are in Work the Borough and do not replace this wanted-PC chase.

Blower, Radio and Sat Nav

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

The Blower

Alt+B or the phone control opens your Blower. Choose your PC and read Heat, cash, current ride, shifts, Pat’s orders and mission briefs. Use the card’s current action and sat nav; older completed chat cards are records of what happened.

Sat nav

Alt+N or the navigation control opens the map route. It follows real roads and the next active destination. Choose a contact or service manually when needed. Routes are private to your player; fold, zoom or use heading-up view. A wanted-ride sale route sends you to a suitable target until you are actually driving the motor the buyer wants, then points to the drop-off.

Pirate radio

Open the radio from the Blower or scene controls. Choose one of six live presets and press Listen to unlock audio in your browser. Audio is streamed from the station, so availability depends on that station. In a shared car the driver chooses the station; each rider keeps their own volume and mute. Off-car listening is personal. Studio links open the station’s chat or contact site/app; they do not send a message for you.

Crew bar

Your assigned PC comes first. Hover for Health, Hustle, cash and Heat; click to view the character, right-click to open the sheet. Use the grip to move the bar and double-click to fold it. The GM can view the whole crew.

Banana Watch and drug effects

The Banana Watch shows the world clock, or real London time if selected. Unpaused world time normally advances one second per second. The GM’s crown can set the date or jump by 15 minutes, an hour, six hours, a day or a week. Drug screen effects are personal to your owned PC: Full, Subtle or Off in client settings; reduced-motion uses Subtle. The GM has a preview. Turning the screen effect off does not remove the condition’s mechanical effects.

Missions and Faction Standing

THE CREW’S REFERENCE

The Mission Board holds 125 missions: the twelve On Your Bike opening jobs, the rest of twelve faction careers, and twenty local cases. CH1–CH3 are the first three opening missions, not three extra payouts.

  1. In Story mode (default), the GM starts, ticks and finishes story missions. Players see the jobs started for them and can still work shifts and Pat’s side orders.
  2. In Self-play, a player who owns a PC can start available missions, tick objectives and finish them. A GM account must remain logged in to process world actions.
  3. Register the participating characters before starting. Mission predecessors and faction Renown gates control offers; the GM can override them for the story.
  4. Read the brief on the Blower. Use Prepare this mission’s maps, follow the route and tick fictional objectives when earned. Map visits, qualifying sales, services, buys and completed job events can tick their matching automatic objectives.
  5. When all objectives are done, Mission Passed pays the listed rewards. Per-head cash and XP go to each registered PC; a crew fee is split as floor(fee ÷ registered crew count).

Mission rewards are separate from money already earned by fencing or a shift. A mission can give a crew fee, per-head cash, XP, personal standing and faction Renown; read its exact breakdown. Renown is shared crew standing with a faction. Local cases with a Renown choice need the appropriate faction selected.

A qualifying mission restores its listed Influence up to the rank cap. Stances are open, allied, strained and hostile. The GM edits standing through Factions. Spending Influence on favours, granting keys, opening rooms, running rivals and moving pressure fronts are GM decisions; a rank does not itself animate an NPC or unlock every door.

Running The Smoke

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

Give London a face and a demand. Pat wants bikes, Mo wants rent, Vale wants a name, the crew wants an opening. Set the stakes before the dice, show the price of the result and keep the next choice legible.

  1. Install the complete system folder as Data/systems/the-smoke and restart Foundry. Choose The Smoke for the world.
  2. As active GM, open Street Control → Set up the world or the welcome card. Import London, kit, cast, pregens and guides. Assign a PC to each player.
  3. Check the scene and your players’ ownership. Start in Your Flat or Hackney Central, then open the Blower and the Mission Board.
  4. Choose Story or Self-play. Leave automatic chase start and assistance off until the table wants them.

Setup adds missing content. A version upgrade refreshes shipped journal pages and preserves user-created pages. If a shipped page was edited, its original text is copied into a GM-only backup before the current rule page is restored. IDs and campaign links remain stable; do not reimport duplicate guides over the world’s copies.

Present one immediate problem and ask what the crew does. Resolve the chosen action, show the consequence and offer the next meaningful decision. Let a quiet job end cleanly. Use the job clock pause for discussion and the Console’s response gates for fights.

Choose the table’s mode

Story is the default. The GM controls mission starts and chase management. Self-play lets owners of PCs run missions and participating players manage their chase. A GM remains connected as world authority in both modes. Player ownership still applies to rolls and character responses.

Hazards

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

Guard = passive 3 + base Guard (normally 4) + the better Moves/Grit modifier + equipped armour’s Guard bonus + conditions. A vehicle uses 6 + twice Size. An attack total that reaches Guard hits.

Damage = max(0, floor(margin + Impact − armour reduction)). Spend the correct ammo and resolve the chat card. The target’s owner or GM can Take hit or use an available Dodge reaction. A successful Moves roll reaching the incoming attack total avoids the whole hit; trying still spends the reaction. One card cannot apply damage twice.

DamageSeverityGM condition choices
0No harmNone
1–2Minor — bruised, shaken, knocked downBruised, Shaken, Prone
3–4Moderate — hurt, stunned, heldHurt, Stunned, Restrained
5–6Severe — bleeding, broken, scared stiffBleeding, In Pain, Broken, Bricking It
7+Critical — down and maybe outDown, Broken, Bleeding

With automatic damage off (the default), the GM may add one appropriate severity condition on a hit. It is a choice, not the whole list. A weapon’s own effect may also apply. Automatic damage changes who applies the numbers; it does not turn every suggested condition into an automatic effect.

At 0 Health, Down is added and you cannot act; Down also gives −4 Guard. In the Console, each round spent Down adds one to the counter. At three Down rounds you are Wasted. A Proper Mess on the Grit / Stay Conscious check can make you Wasted immediately; an ordinary failed check does not do so by itself.

The sheet’s First aid action targets someone within 2.2 squares: roll Savvy, Medium. On success the patient’s owner or GM presses Apply: +2 Health and remove Bleeding and Hurt. Only one treatment applies per injury; new damage opens a new opportunity. Healing above 0 removes Down and resets its counter.

A First Aid Kit is a separate consumable: its own Savvy check, healing and removals are shown in the kit table. A failed use consumes the kit. Do not apply the consumable and the sheet’s treatment as if they were the same button.

Resolve the situation

Stop the bleeding, get the casualty safe, and choose help or surrender when appropriate. Review Wasted and Busted costs before the GM applies those outcomes.

Rams, tyres and control

A ram does margin + 2 × attacker Size to the target. The attacker takes half that against a motor or a quarter against a person, rounded up. A person hurt by a ram is knocked Prone. A called shot at tyres is −2 to hit and blows one tyre when it succeeds. Resolve a PIT or ram defence card before either side advances.

Size 3+ adds 1 Body damage to a loss of control. The incident stops the move; a severe result also applies Shaken. A collision uses both vehicles’ sizes and the pace; read its chat card for each motor’s damage.

At 0 Body, a motor catches fire. In a chase it explodes at the end of the next round; outside one, after 15 seconds. A hit dealing 3+ to a burning motor can detonate it immediately. Get everybody out.

For a fall, fire, crushing door or environmental threat, agree the difficulty and harm before rolling. Use the same damage and condition controls; a fictional hazard is not automatically a weapon attack.

Crime Heat is added when a crime is witnessed, and each crime has a ceiling it cannot push you past. Thieving, carjacking, graffiti and bad driving never take you above 1 star, however often you do them. A fight tops out at 2 stars and gunfire at 3. Only taking a life brings 4 stars and armed police; a second killing, or killing a police officer, brings 5. A police witness adds +1, up to the same ceiling (killings excepted). A lesser crime never lowers your Heat. The GM can report a crime or set stars on the sheet. The system records recent crimes for stop outcomes; setting stars alone does not invent a gun crime.

Police vehicles sent: 1 at 1 star, 2 at 2 stars, 2 and the helicopter at 3 stars, 3 at 4 stars including an Armed Response Vehicle, and 6 at 5 stars with roadblocks. There are never more than the GM's Heat: most police vehicles on a map setting (4 unless changed); the helicopter and officers on foot are extra. When the stars come down, extra units that no character can see go back to base.

On ordinary streets, stay more than 14 squares from police to cool down. At 3+ stars the helicopter observes outdoors across the map; get indoors or resolve the chase. During a turn-based chase, use its round-end escape and search rules. Ordinary cooldown does not run over a live Console fight or an unresolved police stop.

A police stop

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

Busted and Wasted

Busted: custody, Heat 0, at least 1 Health and +1 Known to police. Lose the smaller of your cash or max(£100, rounded 20% of cash). Weapons except Fists, ammo, drugs and police/paramedic uniforms are confiscated. Conditions clear except Broken. Your stash is safe.

Wasted: hospital, full Health and Heat 0. Lose the smaller of your cash or max(£50, rounded 10% of cash). Conditions clear except Broken; Down counters reset. Wasted does not promise a Hustle refill. Stash remains safe.

Police vehicles roll speed dice from Performance: d4 gives 1d6; d6/d8 2d6; d10/d12 3d6; d20 4d6. A driver uses the better of their own action count and the motor’s. Two flat tyres or 0 Body each remove one vehicle die, minimum one; burning and parked police units have no driving actions. Ordinary civilian traffic uses its shared phase instead of individual speed dice.

Assistance starts OFF

Chase combat does not start itself by default. The GM can start a chase from the Combat Console; a participating player can manage it in Self-play. World settings can opt into automatic chase starts or NPC assistance. Turn Assist on or off for the current chase in the Console.

  1. Begin a round and reveal speed dice. PCs and each police unit receive their own action entries. Ordinary, unoccupied civilian traffic receives one shared Traffic phase at the end of the queue.
  2. For a PC action, move and choose your action, answer its chat cards, then press Done. A police unit acts separately. With Assist on, it takes only that action, animates it, and stops for Continue.
  3. Resolve every pending hit, driving check, evasive manoeuvre, PIT or police decision before advancing. Responses do not time out. Police and ambient traffic hold while a decision is open.
  4. All moving civilian traffic advances together in its shared phase. Review the round, then press Begin round. No automatic chain of new rounds.

NPC assistance waits 3 seconds by default before acting; the world setting allows 2–10 seconds. The Continue gate remains whatever delay you choose. The helicopter follows through its turns rather than teleporting to the suspect.

Finish the pursuit

At round end, a wanted PC more than 30 squares from every pursuing police unit loses one star. Repeat escapes until 0. If the police lose visual contact (all beyond 14 squares), the chase can enter searching; the search checks whether you remain unseen rather than bringing police straight back to you. The helicopter still matters outdoors at high Heat. A successful stop response follows the one-star and one-opening procedure below.

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

A map exit waits for pending decisions. After crossing, the chase resumes on the destination map with a new round. A police-shift pursuit callout has its own small gap track; its rules are in Work the Borough and do not replace this wanted-PC chase.

Awards and unlocks

A completed job gives 1 XP; Pat’s order gives 2; selling a motor for £500+ gives 1. Typical minor/major mission awards are 3/5, with the Mission Board’s actual reward taking precedence. Busted and Wasted give no XP. A GM-awarded Advance is a separate stat step within your current tier cap; it does not buy a Rep level.

Unlock
Rep 3 — Uncle sells you shooters (guns and ammo out the back of Uncle's Cafe)
Rep 3 — Pat gives you the bigger orders
Rep 6 — A known supplier: fences pay you 10% more for nicked rides
Rep 6 — Uncle's "good stuff": SMGs, pump shotguns, proper vests
Rep 9 — Pat's car jobs (motors, not bikes), and Uncle's "don't ask" shelf
Rep 13 — Top Boy: your own crew, hire NPCs to work for you
Rep 27 — Empire: stats can reach d20
Chainring 3 — Pat knocks 10% off at The Arches
Street 5 — Known on the street: every shop knocks 10% off
Known to police 3 — Stops start at Wanted: they know your face

The crew-hiring and property ambitions are story permissions for the GM to develop. Shop gates, discounts, XP and the level-up wizard are implemented controls. Old five-level characters migrate as Rep 1→1, 2→3, 3→6, 4→9, 5→14.

The Mission Board holds 125 missions: the twelve On Your Bike opening jobs, the rest of twelve faction careers, and twenty local cases. CH1–CH3 are the first three opening missions, not three extra payouts.

  1. In Story mode (default), the GM starts, ticks and finishes story missions. Players see the jobs started for them and can still work shifts and Pat’s side orders.
  2. In Self-play, a player who owns a PC can start available missions, tick objectives and finish them. A GM account must remain logged in to process world actions.
  3. Register the participating characters before starting. Mission predecessors and faction Renown gates control offers; the GM can override them for the story.
  4. Read the brief on the Blower. Use Prepare this mission’s maps, follow the route and tick fictional objectives when earned. Map visits, qualifying sales, services, buys and completed job events can tick their matching automatic objectives.
  5. When all objectives are done, Mission Passed pays the listed rewards. Per-head cash and XP go to each registered PC; a crew fee is split as floor(fee ÷ registered crew count).

Mission rewards are separate from money already earned by fencing or a shift. A mission can give a crew fee, per-head cash, XP, personal standing and faction Renown; read its exact breakdown. Renown is shared crew standing with a faction. Local cases with a Renown choice need the appropriate faction selected.

A qualifying mission restores its listed Influence up to the rank cap. Stances are open, allied, strained and hostile. The GM edits standing through Factions. Spending Influence on favours, granting keys, opening rooms, running rivals and moving pressure fronts are GM decisions; a rank does not itself animate an NPC or unlock every door.

Automation and Table Pace

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

Choose the table’s mode

Story is the default. The GM controls mission starts and chase management. Self-play lets owners of PCs run missions and participating players manage their chase. A GM remains connected as world authority in both modes. Player ownership still applies to rolls and character responses.

ControlDefault / behaviour
Automatic chase startOff. Opt in in world settings; the Console can start one manually.
NPC chase assistanceOff. Assist is also a per-chase Console toggle.
NPC assistance delay3 seconds, adjustable 2–10; every NPC action still waits for Continue.
Automatic travel evasionOn. Rolls real Wheels when crossing another vehicle’s body; manual setting offers a chat roll button.
Automatic hit damageOff. Target owner/GM responds to the hit card.
Automatic crime HeatOn; witnessed incidents feed the Heat rules.
Street Life / jobs / shopsConfigure their world settings; pause the job clock to discuss a callout without losing its deadline.

Unanswered cards are deliberate pauses. Inspect the pending item in chat and resolve it before Done, Continue or Begin round. Do not start another Console fight over the same scene to work around a pending response.

What the GM supplies

Automatic event ticks, cash/XP, seat movement, dice, heat and traffic support the scene. NPC motives, fictional costs, influence favours, campaign fronts, access rights and plot outcomes still need decisions. Pick one consequence and offer the next meaningful choice; do not repeat cards after the situation is settled.

Police vehicles roll speed dice from Performance: d4 gives 1d6; d6/d8 2d6; d10/d12 3d6; d20 4d6. A driver uses the better of their own action count and the motor’s. Two flat tyres or 0 Body each remove one vehicle die, minimum one; burning and parked police units have no driving actions. Ordinary civilian traffic uses its shared phase instead of individual speed dice.

Assistance starts OFF

Chase combat does not start itself by default. The GM can start a chase from the Combat Console; a participating player can manage it in Self-play. World settings can opt into automatic chase starts or NPC assistance. Turn Assist on or off for the current chase in the Console.

  1. Begin a round and reveal speed dice. PCs and each police unit receive their own action entries. Ordinary, unoccupied civilian traffic receives one shared Traffic phase at the end of the queue.
  2. For a PC action, move and choose your action, answer its chat cards, then press Done. A police unit acts separately. With Assist on, it takes only that action, animates it, and stops for Continue.
  3. Resolve every pending hit, driving check, evasive manoeuvre, PIT or police decision before advancing. Responses do not time out. Police and ambient traffic hold while a decision is open.
  4. All moving civilian traffic advances together in its shared phase. Review the round, then press Begin round. No automatic chain of new rounds.

NPC assistance waits 3 seconds by default before acting; the world setting allows 2–10 seconds. The Continue gate remains whatever delay you choose. The helicopter follows through its turns rather than teleporting to the suspect.

Finish the pursuit

At round end, a wanted PC more than 30 squares from every pursuing police unit loses one star. Repeat escapes until 0. If the police lose visual contact (all beyond 14 squares), the chase can enter searching; the search checks whether you remain unseen rather than bringing police straight back to you. The helicopter still matters outdoors at high Heat. A successful stop response follows the one-star and one-opening procedure below.

  1. Choose Talk, Run, Surrender or Resist. The owner or GM answers; the scene holds.
  2. Talk: Front Hard below 3 stars, Long Shot at 3+. Run: Wheels for a seated driver, otherwise Moves; Medium below 3 stars, Hard at 3+.
  3. A success removes exactly one star. At 0 the police stand down. Otherwise they fumble and you choose one opening: an accessible vehicle or on foot.
  4. Take that escape move with nobody else moving: the vehicle’s green Speed, or 6 squares on foot. Press Finish escape move. Finishing does not remove an extra star; the police pursue or search until the remaining stars are gone.
  5. A failed Talk/Run normally means Busted. At Heat 4+ with a recorded shooting, murder or police killing, armed enforcement instead posts an answerable incoming shot and a new decision. Resolve the hit, then choose. Surrender always goes to custody. Resist starts a fight.

A map exit waits for pending decisions. After crossing, the chase resumes on the destination map with a new round. A police-shift pursuit callout has its own small gap track; its rules are in Work the Borough and do not replace this wanted-PC chase.

METRO POLICE · HACKNEY PROPERTY CRIME UNIT
RESTRICTED — FOR POLICE USE

Subject: Organised cycle theft, E8/E9. OIC: DS H. Vale.

1. Reported cycle thefts within 800m of Morning Lane are up 41% on last quarter. High-value road bikes (Carbon Whippet, Trailblazer) are being taken to order.

2. Intelligence suggests stolen cycles are stripped within hours at premises in the railway arches, Morning Lane, and frames moved east across the Lea.

3. A rival group operating from Leyton ("Lea Boys") is believed responsible for a number of thefts and at least one assault with a bike chain.

4. Officers on patrol are asked to note youths on BMX cycles loitering near cycle stands, and to run ANPR checks on vans leaving Morning Lane after 22:00.

5. A tracked bait cycle will be deployed on Broadway Market. Do not intervene — follow it home.

The Hackney Gazette

Page 7, under the planning notices.

BIKE THEFT "OUT OF CONTROL", SAY CYCLISTS

By our Hackney reporter

Cyclists in Hackney have described bike theft in the borough as "out of control" after a spate of thefts outside cafés on Broadway Market and London Fields.

"I went in for a coffee and came out to a cut lock," said one rider, whose £1,800 carbon road bike was taken in under five minutes. "Nobody saw anything. Everybody saw everything."

A Metro Police spokesperson said officers were "aware of organised activity" and urged cyclists to use two locks and register their frames.

Meanwhile, a Morning Lane cycle repair shop has been praised by local residents for its "very reasonable" prices on second-hand bikes.

Hackney Missions — On Your Bike

How the Missions Work

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

The Mission Board holds 125 missions: the twelve On Your Bike opening jobs, the rest of twelve faction careers, and twenty local cases. CH1–CH3 are the first three opening missions, not three extra payouts.

  1. In Story mode (default), the GM starts, ticks and finishes story missions. Players see the jobs started for them and can still work shifts and Pat’s side orders.
  2. In Self-play, a player who owns a PC can start available missions, tick objectives and finish them. A GM account must remain logged in to process world actions.
  3. Register the participating characters before starting. Mission predecessors and faction Renown gates control offers; the GM can override them for the story.
  4. Read the brief on the Blower. Use Prepare this mission’s maps, follow the route and tick fictional objectives when earned. Map visits, qualifying sales, services, buys and completed job events can tick their matching automatic objectives.
  5. When all objectives are done, Mission Passed pays the listed rewards. Per-head cash and XP go to each registered PC; a crew fee is split as floor(fee ÷ registered crew count).

Mission rewards are separate from money already earned by fencing or a shift. A mission can give a crew fee, per-head cash, XP, personal standing and faction Renown; read its exact breakdown. Renown is shared crew standing with a faction. Local cases with a Renown choice need the appropriate faction selected.

RenownRankInfluence cap
0Unproven1
3Known2
7Trusted3
12Connected4
18Insider5
25Pillar6

A qualifying mission restores its listed Influence up to the rank cap. Stances are open, allied, strained and hostile. The GM edits standing through Factions. Spending Influence on favours, granting keys, opening rooms, running rivals and moving pressure fronts are GM decisions; a rank does not itself animate an NPC or unlock every door.

The twelve opening jobs

These pages keep the campaign scenes and hooks. Each mission’s current Board rules strip gives the actual gates, objective ticks and reward split. Hand the players the brief; keep GM twists in this book.

Mo bangs on the door: rent is due Friday, and Pat "wants a word". Pat wants two bikes by tonight. Nothing fancy. Kez will show you where.

£60 each3 XP+1 Chainring

How it plays

Start everyone in Your Flat. Walk out through Chicken Palace onto Mare Street; The Arches are round the corner on Morning Lane (the door on the Hackney map, or ride straight up to the yard).

Pat gives the order on the phone (Ask Pat for an order) or in person. Street Life puts chained bikes on every map; Kez's tip-offs are a map or two away. This is the mission to teach the lock roll, Heat (the first time someone watches), and selling at The Arches — Pat whispers an offer with a Sell button when they pull up.

GM Screen: Street → Kez's tip-off bike spawns a target near them; Checks → Spot the Old Bill before they cut the lock.

Complication

One of the bikes belongs to a Lea Boy. He saw. Next session he wants it back — or Stretch does.

Next: Pat has a buyer for something better: Mission 2.

How it plays

The lock is Hard. Bolt cutters make it Medium; the angle grinder makes it Easy — but it shrieks, and Broadway Market on a Saturday is full of phones (witnessed: +1 Heat).

If it becomes a vehicle pursuit, use the Combat Console for individual actions and resolve each driving or defence card before moving on. For a non-combat tail, use opposed Wheels checks agreed with the GM. The police-shift gap mini-game belongs to callouts, not this story scene.

THE SMOKE · GM

The Sandbox Campaign

Twelve firms, ninety-six jobs, twenty local cases and 160 venues. Every one of them mapped.

The opening, On Your Bike, is where the crew starts: nicking bikes for Auntie Pat and keeping Mo off their backs. This book is everything after. Twelve outfits with eight jobs each, a local case in every district, and one big stitch-up — the Quiet Ledger — sitting under some of the crimes. Not all of them. Most of Hackney's grief is just Hackney.

How to use it

Every job and case is on the Mission Board (GM Screen → Tools, or the Missions app on the Blower). Pick a firm or Local cases at the top of the list. When a job lands, the giver's texts come through as a thread — that's the hook. Renown with each firm opens its next job and gets paid out automatically when you pass a mission; Factions & Renown on the board keeps Renown, Influence and who's fallen out with who.

Every page names its rooms, and every venue has its own map. Hit Prepare this mission's maps on the board to pull them in, or just walk through a venue's ENTER pin on the street map.

Every job, the same shape

The call (what the giver texts), the score (what's really on offer), how it goes down (one line per scene, with the room codes and the rolls), the heat (what lands if they hang about), your call (the decision), what it leads to, and the twist — the bit nobody saw coming. Use the twist or don't; they're all listed together in the Quiet Ledger chapter so you can keep the double-crosses straight.

What the crew gets up to, and how 160 venues come into play.

Where it all starts

You've got the twenty street maps, the four rooms from the opening — Pat's Arches, the flat over the Chicken Palace, Homerton A&E and the custody suite — and the London overview. On top of that, every street district now has eight venues of its own: six real places round the manor and two made-up premises. That's 160 venues, 960 rooms, every one of them drawn. Some real places get two maps — the New Spitalfields produce hall and its admin block, say — because they're two different bits of the same site, not two venues.

What the crew gets up to

Nicking bikes and sound systems. Getting back stuff that three people say is theirs. Running dodgy cargo. Looking after witnesses — or selling them out. Working the Halo trade. Chasing missing people and missing tapes. Fighting over money and who runs what.

Twelve outfits, eight big jobs each. Twenty local cases, one per district: thefts, sporting stitch-ups, debts, one murder, and a handful of proper mysteries. Under some of it — not all of it — sits the Quiet Ledger, the big conspiracy. Not every crime in Hackney is part of it. Most of them are just Hackney.

How the doors open

A job tells the GM which rooms it needs. Take the job and those venues come into play, along with a way in: a name on the guest list, a booking, an intro at the depot, a visitor meeting — or a dodgy unsponsored way in that might go very wrong. Do the job well and you might get asked back. Later on you get the private rooms, a slice of a made-up business, or a partnership with somebody who matters.

The public bits — bars, foyers, churches, shops — are open from day one. The unlocks are about the story space and the people you've won over, not about bouncers.

Real places, made-up trouble

The real names and addresses put the game in real London. The room layouts are invented for play — they're not floor plans of the actual buildings. Every contact, crime, private do, tenant and outfit in this campaign is fictional. A villain having a drink in a real pub doesn't make the landlord part of the firm.

Renown, Influence and Interior Access

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

The Mission Board holds 125 missions: the twelve On Your Bike opening jobs, the rest of twelve faction careers, and twenty local cases. CH1–CH3 are the first three opening missions, not three extra payouts.

  1. In Story mode (default), the GM starts, ticks and finishes story missions. Players see the jobs started for them and can still work shifts and Pat’s side orders.
  2. In Self-play, a player who owns a PC can start available missions, tick objectives and finish them. A GM account must remain logged in to process world actions.
  3. Register the participating characters before starting. Mission predecessors and faction Renown gates control offers; the GM can override them for the story.
  4. Read the brief on the Blower. Use Prepare this mission’s maps, follow the route and tick fictional objectives when earned. Map visits, qualifying sales, services, buys and completed job events can tick their matching automatic objectives.
  5. When all objectives are done, Mission Passed pays the listed rewards. Per-head cash and XP go to each registered PC; a crew fee is split as floor(fee ÷ registered crew count).

Mission rewards are separate from money already earned by fencing or a shift. A mission can give a crew fee, per-head cash, XP, personal standing and faction Renown; read its exact breakdown. Renown is shared crew standing with a faction. Local cases with a Renown choice need the appropriate faction selected.

A qualifying mission restores its listed Influence up to the rank cap. Stances are open, allied, strained and hostile. The GM edits standing through Factions. Choose the table’s mode

Story is the default. The GM controls mission starts and chase management. Self-play lets owners of PCs run missions and participating players manage their chase. A GM remains connected as world authority in both modes. Player ownership still applies to rolls and character responses.

SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

The Quiet Ledger (GM Truth)

What actually happened. Keep it off the table — let them dig it up.

This is what actually happened. The players don't get to read this page. They find it out — or they don't.

The six buildings

Meridian Renewal want six occupied made-up premises: @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB8} Orchard Lease Office, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8} Clapton Union Rooms, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB8} Essex Dry Goods, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW8} White Post Workers Rooms, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF8} Roman Rooms Printworks and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF8} Carpenters Breakfast Club. Celia Voss signed off on buying them using fake "vacant" reports and a lot of leaning on people. Some of the folk in there would've taken a fair move — the fake mandate took away their chance to haggle for one.

Where the money goes

Evan Lark runs it all through Quayline Advisory, at the @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG8} Quayline Records Suite: options, consultancy fees and event contracts that look like they've got nothing to do with each other. No single folder proves the lot. An early dated offer, a tenant's copy and a payment that matches — that's what makes the property story stand up. The crew can blow it open, haggle with it, buy in, or sell a solid account to someone who'll know what to do with it.

The muscle

Martin Rusk, out of the @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW8} East Cross Security Compound, cranked up the intimidation and cooked up a false official story to make the six places look like lost causes. Owen Pike signed off the bad Halo swap after Rusk paid for some "disruption". Inspector Holt took consultancy money and helped the official version along. PC Dunn kept her original notes. DS Vale goes after the offences she can actually back up — she can't promise anyone immunity and she can't order the whole Met about.

The fake broadcast

Rusk paid a freelance producer, Bram Senn, through Owen, to put together a "warning" out of old, genuine Nia recordings. Seth Calder kept an earlier mix at the @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW7} Wallis Tape Rooms. Gemma Hale, the cleaner, has her own copy. The @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM8} Silt Listening Bunker has an earlier rehearsal, and Leon at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF8} can spot the old station ident. Some of the voice is real. The message is a fake.

Nia's alive

Nia "Switch" Bell is alive and well at the @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW7} Willow Cabin with Asha Stone when the campaign starts. She'd been comparing an early tenant offer with what callers were telling her on air — then she heard her own old voice in that fake warning. So she dropped out of sight. Finding her, getting her story, keeping her originals safe and saying where she is are four separate decisions. Asha will set up a meeting if someone she trusts agrees to Nia's terms.

The Quiet Hour

It all comes together on one night: a public broadcast, the property signatures, the removal vans and a carefully timed official story. Each of those has its own control point and its own people in charge. The crew doesn't need to max every faction or crack every case first. Three solid strands of evidence are enough to step in properly; one narrower fact can still win a smaller deal. A full public account has to say where its evidence came from and what it can't prove.

Changing it through play

That's who's responsible at the start, not how it has to end. Payments can be redirected, a buyer can pull out, a witness can say "don't print it", a faction can get a new boss. Write down what the crew actually proved and what's still a guess. A crew of crooks might keep part of the scheme going for the money — so show who gains and who's left with a claim.

Three ways to every piece of the truth

When the crew gets to the right source, they get the lead. Rolls decide how fast, how much it costs, where they stand and whether they get extra leverage. Each truth has independent routes, so the mystery still works if they turn down a faction or lose an original.

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.948ae5161dabd8fe]{LB1}Rent in ArrearsThe broker bought the debt from Vic Randle's loan office — Vic's been selling Lea Bridge debts on the quiet.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.edb072b261a9b83d]{LB2}Stretch Wants His CutThe crate's empty. The paperwork inside it is what everyone paid for: lease options on six 'empty' buildings.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cc7f487551ebb84f]{LB3}The Larch JobThe invoice says the load was changed at the depot two days ago — and signed for by somebody from 'East Cross Security'.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.f4d5d00a1615da84]{LB4}Halo With TeethThe courier who got hurt is Daz's little brother. Daz doesn't know yet.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cd772286b56d8cd9]{LB5}The Boy Who Kept ReceiptsHalf the 'debts' in the book were invented on instruction from Meridian's people — squeezing tenants until they'd sign anything.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.6aca308e65358a4d]{LB6}Terms From AboveThe 'consultancy' the Lea Boys would be paid for is clearing tenants out of the six buildings.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cb91b5ade40c2d38]{LB7}Who Speaks for the Lea BoysStretch has already signed. The Meridian deal went through last week. Tonight's vote is about whether anyone honours it.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.3ad0e65c45f2f9b3]{LB8}The Price of a PatchDaz has been selling the firm's plans to Rusk all along. He's in the car park with Rusk's people.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.1e66ff0301850ed1]{VC1}The Sound Went MissingThe 'unpaid hire' was paid — in cash, out of the Halo float. The supplier just won't say so out loud.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.e90759230df2d2c6]{VC2}No Guest List for the MissingThe 'debt' is Owen's. He borrowed against the performer's fee and spent it.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.7e68c241b410998e]{VC3}Cash Before CurtainThe 'payer' at the gala is Evan Lark. The benefit was a laundromat with a raffle.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.4317f82b3e99cd92]{VC4}The Last Good BatchThe worker trying to leave is the one who made the switch. He's got Rusk's phone number saved as 'Uncle'.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.f59964430f7423d5]{VC5}A Set for NobodyThe 'collector' is Bram Senn — the producer who made the fake. He's cleaning up after himself.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.1d4d2bc6c9dbe042]{VC6}The Sponsor Behind the SponsorThe guarantor is Martin Rusk. Owen's 'nightlife partnership' is a security contract with a sound system.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.497596f8e42e159e]{VC7}Last Dance Before the SaleOwen isn't running from his creditors. He's running from Rusk, who wants the book more than anyone.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.c19a5cc4367c0ae7]{VC8}Who Owns the NightMara Sol has been recording every promoters' meeting for a year. She'll trade the tapes for her freedom — or broadcast them.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.cc77fcdd90b2424a]{TU1}The Wrong CaseThe cassette in the case is an old Dead Air session with Nia on it. Someone's collecting her voice.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.c8625b2897481410]{TU2}The Van and the DebtThe hire firm's registered to an address at the Quayline Records Suite.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.ab969db53150ff8e]{TU3}The Driver Who Wasn't ThereThe replacement driver's pickup was a box of files from the Clapton Union Rooms — the night before it was 'found empty'.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.88aa051ba2f9976f]{TU4}The Route BookSix of the addresses in the book are the six 'empty' buildings. The book proves they were occupied when the vacant reports were filed.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.1b91cd2cc2d33577]{TU5}Not the Person in the PhotographThe person who leaked the photo works in Meridian's 'community engagement' team.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.8b693ddfca554a5e]{TU6}The Contract That Eats the RouteMeridian don't want the network for deliveries. They want it for the Quiet Hour: every van in the East End, on one night, on their schedule.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.5f6a9fc17d4ae6dc]{TU7}Four Loads One CustomerThe 'band's backline' is Rusk's crew and their gear, hidden in flight cases.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.01b43c4291081cb5]{TU8}The City Still Has to MoveTern sold the board to Meridian an hour before the night started. Your plan is running on their network — and they can see every move.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.00bd39565f9bc810]{GE1}The Wrong ProvenanceThe bike was nicked from Pat's patch. Pat would very much like it back.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.3e3e6c8f62b9dee1]{GE2}The Coat With the AppointmentThe note in the lining is an appointment at the Quayline Records Suite — with a name on it that isn't Oona's. She was the messenger and never knew.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.5b2b7a5f03feae52]{GE3}The House ClearanceThe letters behind the print are tenancy agreements for the Clapton Union Rooms — signed, dated, and very much alive.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.fc89b613c810bf69]{GE4}Loaned and LostThe broker's private deal was with Celia Voss's personal art adviser. The piece was a sweetener.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.f438e557eae74cba]{GE5}A Picture of the Wrong NightThe 'visitor' is Inspector Gavin Holt, in plain clothes, on Meridian's dime.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.bddb5d733296d877]{GE6}An Auction for Empty HomesThe winning bidder is a shell company. The shell company is Clement Wren.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.7b8613ed6d44dd53]{GE7}The Collection That Can SpeakOwen's 'final component' is the original fake broadcast tape — with Bram Senn's invoice tucked in the box.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.83431aeb57e528e2]{GE8}What Is Worth KeepingWren's retiring — to Spain, tonight. The keys to the saleroom are in the envelope with your fee.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.a45353aa41ff25d1]{BB2}The Wrong WinnerThe middleman isn't fixing it for himself. He's fixing it for Daz — who needs the money to pay off Vic.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.0001dbbd03496b6f]{BB3}Cash on the Guest ListThe person being asked to sign the duplicate invoice is Frankie Wu. She refuses — and asks you to get her out.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.5638dde8af04b423]{BB4}A Result Before the RaceThe 'live' broadcast was made in the same studio, by the same producer, as the fake Nia warning.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.fd474eac904a0150]{BB5}Your Name in Someone Else's BookThe fake entry was written the week of the funeral, by the same 'helpful' bloke who sorted the flowers. He's done it to every grieving family on the estate.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.f9a723352bb81bd2]{BB6}Land on CreditVic's 'option' on the Arches is Pat's old loan. He's already sold it on to Quayline — and he hasn't told Pat. Or you.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.934d64446b75f8cc]{BB7}The Final AccountEddie Lane photographed every page months ago. He's been waiting for someone he could trust.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.781c362363e7650b]{BB8}The House Changes HandsEddie Lane and the staff have quietly bought half of Vic's book with the wages Vic owed them. Whoever signs tonight, Eddie's at the table.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.519c3256dd58f8f9]{NM1}Stall SeventeenThe 'collectors' are on Len Fisk's payroll. He wants Pearl looking weak before the concession talks.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.5086e6b32e6611c5]{NM2}One Box Two BuyersThe rare recording is the original Nia session the fake warning was cut from — with the date written on the label.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.f283c4a5d428f552]{NM3}Everything Must GoThe missing man drove for East Cross Security. The watch has a delivery schedule scratched in the case back.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.5c1e5a2f8704cd49]{NM4}Protection by PostThe print order was paid from the same account that paid for the fake debt entries in Vic's book (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.fd474eac904a0150]{BB5}).
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.b52f12aa67f4c1b9]{NM5}The Borrowed ExhibitionThe 'private buyer' is Oona Reyes, buying on behalf of the Glasshouse Exchange. Wren wants a hold over the gallery's board.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.709d3aec915ec003]{NM6}The Market That Sold ItselfThe signatures are real — copied off the repair forms. The person who swapped the pages works in Meridian's sales pavilion.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.712e9b663aeacd7d]{NM7}A Night to TradeThe promoter's money comes from Owen Pike. The rival trying to cancel it? Also Owen Pike.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.cfd60ddff09185c9]{NM8}Who Gets a Place at the TableThe corporate buyer is Len Fisk, fronting for Meridian. He's been on their books since @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.519c3256dd58f8f9]{NM1}.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.32a92965918487e6]{BM1}A Meal and a ReceiptThe fake debt comes from the same duplicate book that's been forging Vic's entries (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.0487b331fc4a6aa5]{BB1}).
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.e6bc4fc2e3d4b80d]{BM2}Benefit Night Rain CheckThe double booking wasn't an accident. Owen Pike booked the pavilion for a Velvet Circuit 'pop-up' — to see if the Mutual would fold.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.dbfa4bc0c98be132]{BM3}The Signatures UpstairsThe new wording was ordered by the same middleman who forged the trader mandate in @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.709d3aec915ec003]{NM6}.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.20b3857b08eff2d6]{BM4}After the BatchThe swap was paid for by Owen Pike, with Rusk's money. The Lea Boys didn't cut it — someone wanted them blamed.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.6a5bcd7797fbc470]{BM5}The Homes on the ListAll three 'incidents' were logged by the same insurance assessor. He used to work for Celia Voss.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.7c22a3ed7b4c1f3b]{BM6}Who Can Promise a HomeThe financier is Vic Randle. He's betting both ways.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.0221821e57adf8d4]{BM7}A Witness Chooses a DoorThe rival tailing you isn't after the witness. He's after you — Rusk wants to know where the crew sleeps.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.71478f1c8a685daf]{BM8}The Neighbourhood Gets a VoteThe neglected household is Auntie Pat's sister. Pat never asked for help. Rosa knew.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.cfe055768cdea049]{LD1}The Bait BikeThe bike went through the Arches. Pat sold it on. Vale already knows — she wanted to see if you'd tell her.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.7b640abfbcb175ce]{LD2}The Uniform in the PhotographThe 'different visitor' in Dunn's note is Inspector Holt himself.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.0decc348c7790f3f]{LD3}A Report With No VisitThe report was signed by an inspector who'd been dead three weeks. Someone borrowed his login.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.ef0b9e188b6e7cd1]{LD4}Someone Else's PropertyIt's the same watch from @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.f283c4a5d428f552]{NM3}. Pearl sold it on. Vale wants to know who to.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.179900d7fa46d217]{LD5}The Person Behind the FileThe 'rival's car' is Holt's personal motor. He came himself.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.6d63a16302606476]{LD6}The Inspector's Other EmployerThe consultancy is a Meridian subsidiary. The authoriser is Celia Voss's PA, signing in her name.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.1fb049db18a7ccb6]{LD7}Four Notices Before MidnightOne of the four addresses is Auntie Pat's arches. It was never a decoy.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.1c4e1b25b685d24d]{LD8}A Case That Survives Its WitnessesVale's being transferred. Her replacement? Inspector Holt's protégé. She wants you to keep the file.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.07d7c50413fd3f37]{MR1}The Missing Survey CaseThe case is empty. Rusk already has the survey. He wanted to see if you'd open it.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.d05eaf4a2f271cf3]{MR2}The Model ApartmentThe family's grandfather made it. In Auntie Pat's arches, in 1974.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.8b155178b6ba57c7]{MR3}An Invoice for a DriverThe journey was the Quiet Hour dry run. The van was carrying blank vacancy notices.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.b6a16f3432ae9a6d]{MR4}The Report and the DoorThe later instructions came from Evan Lark's account — the same one Vic Randle's been lending through (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.f9a723352bb81bd2]{BB6}).
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.845c46ff4dd242ae]{MR5}Vacant on PaperThe rival bid is Borough Mutual's co-op — and it's being bankrolled by Vic Randle.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.0d1b02a56098407d]{MR6}Buy the FrequencyCelia doesn't want the station's coverage. She wants its archive — and whatever Nia left in it.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.1c6a4266500f4558]{MR7}The Quiet HourCelia isn't in the building. She's at the North Park Hospitality Lodge with a lawyer, ready to blame Rusk for everything if it goes wrong. Rusk knows.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.ef36c4beb45f8e3a]{MR8}The City on the BrochureCelia's already resigned. The 'permanent role' is hers. So are all her liabilities.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.0d1854ec0da2448e]{RT1}The Empty SlotThe person who tore down the poster is Asha — Nia's closest mate. She did it because Nia asked her to.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.7f8125d11258c230]{RT2}The Watch After MidnightThe 'second searcher' is paying with money from Rusk's security budget. He was hired to find her — and nobody's told you why.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.be46259208fcc6c4]{RT3}A Photograph Without a CaptionThe other man in the photo — the one everyone cropped out — is Martin Rusk. Lark and Rusk go back a long way.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.25ee7f45599e1ca8]{RT4}The Night That RepeatedThe editor was paid through Owen Pike — with Rusk's money. The fake was built to make the Lea Boys look guilty.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.686cfe0a6ca772f2]{RT5}Six Addresses Before the TroubleThe early option on @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8} was witnessed by the same insurance assessor who later wrote up the 'incident' there (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.6a5bcd7797fbc470]{BM5}). Same signature, both papers.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.f371e3df5645797b]{RT6}The Woman Who Chose to VanishNia didn't go missing. She went quiet — on purpose — the night she found a seventh address on Quayline's list: Auntie Pat's Arches.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.a24b58c37ba6a994]{RT7}Who Holds the OriginalThe funder demanding every original is the same 'charitable foundation' that paid for the Evering flat. New name, same Celia.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.4189bb0e67e391ed]{RT8}A Record of What HappenedNia wants to read the final account on Dead Air herself. Live. Tonight.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.3abb9c0858b90c27]{S01}The Voice at the Book ClubThe 'dead' joke is about a Dead Air pirate night in 1998 — and Leon was there.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.53588614167a9b45]{S02}The Alarm Before the SongThe organiser owes Miri for three gigs, not one. He's been doing it to everybody.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.9702d4565150f22d]{S03}The Wrong Brother on the BoatThe musician is the brothers' cousin. Christmas is going to be very awkward.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.a9f00cd7d7afe9ea]{S04}The Dog at the FundraiserEllis's 'separate debt' is one of the forged duplicate-book entries from @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.0487b331fc4a6aa5]{BB1}. He never owed a penny.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.059e8ffa356bd818]{S05}The Missing MascotThe shared loan's from Vic's book. The ex is trying to pay it off before the collectors come.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.7afd4aa798ff9c84]{S06}The Cat in the CatalogueWren knew about the fakes. He wanted someone else to find them — so it couldn't be traced to him.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.65e8d1244a07177d]{S07}The Silent SetThe promoter's fee cut was Owen Pike's idea. Velvet Circuit takes a skim off every show it 'supports'.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.3d3e4cd2b4928c68]{S08}The Chicken Palace KeyThe old tenancy was Nia's. She lived in your room before you did.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.0bd54542d877e827]{S09}The Projector Belongs to Both of UsThe visiting promoter is the projector's original maker. He thinks it's still his.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.43e544512ad2ec27]{S10}The Sponsor Who Never ArrivedCallum Redd's real name is on the duplicate book. He owes Vic more than he's stolen.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.36b9822f2ba1cc66]{S11}The Painting That Keeps Coming BackThe painting's of Auntie Pat's arches, 1970s. The kid's grandad painted it.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.e7dec5e9cb377bdd]{S12}The Wedding DubplateThe bride's nan was a Dead Air DJ in the 80s. Leon trained under her.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.6990428a48394631]{S13}Big Sal on the PosterThe rival was paid by the same middleman who's been printing fake 'Stretch' letters (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.5c1e5a2f8704cd49]{NM4}).
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.a84161b0e2203e61]{S14}The Passenger Paid TwiceThe business partner being cheated is Pearl Okonkwo.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.14360fc735fcdf24]{S15}The Lucky JacketThe guest is Celia Voss's nephew. She'll pay a lot for this to stay quiet.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.a14c33cbaa75c638]{S16}The Cabinet and the DebtThe watch belongs to the missing East Cross driver from @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e88d889809aabec7.JournalEntryPage.f283c4a5d428f552]{NM3}'s clearance. It's been in the drawer the whole time.
@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.29f6bfb5c06395f9]{S17}The Riding ContestThe 'rushed business' is a bike courier firm. Tern's already thinking of buying it.
