SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

Starting Nights and Personal Stakes

The first three nights, and what the pregens are really after.

The opening stays

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.0fb97a2328543408]{CH1 On Your Bike}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.b24d3a40394a0516]{CH2 The Whippet} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2d9fbb694ed5e2d2.JournalEntryPage.31fe63f142ee4d21]{CH3 Lights and Sirens} stay exactly as they are. CH1 starts with Mo and Pat at the flat and the Arches, then spills out into London Fields and the @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7} storehouse. CH2 is back on Broadway Market, nicking off the coffee racks. CH3 keeps Morning Lane, Waterden and Bow Breakers, and opens up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM7}. The new rooms add to the opening — they don't replace its people or its order.

The first three nights

Night one: run CH1 and show them the first storehouse. Offer @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.7052e00fca53338b.JournalEntryPage.531b033a95279cd6]{AD1} (somebody's speakers have walked) and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.32a92965918487e6]{BM1} (a hot meal and a dodgy receipt).

Night two: follow whichever they picked, or run CH2. Show one comeback from someone who reckons they've been wronged.

Night three: offer CH3, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.cc77fcdd90b2424a]{TU1} and the local case in whichever district they like best. Any career can start at job 1 the moment a named sponsor agrees to it.

The pregens and what they want

Jaz Kaur

21, from Dalston. Rider, mechanic, wants a proper legit shop and has history with Kez. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8} could be a garage, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR8} a riding workshop, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.957a87da24e85625]{CH8} a real slice of the business. Let Jaz put down a deposit and pick her own customers — don't hand her a shop off one lucky roll.

Danny "Tealeaf" Doyle

24, from Homerton. Owes Pat for his mum's funeral and wants one big score to clear it. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.541dbf4f06b2aa0b]{CH4}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cc7f487551ebb84f]{LB3} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.bddb5d733296d877]{GE6} put bigger and bigger prizes in front of him, each with someone else saying it's theirs. Pat might knock some off the debt instead of cash — Danny decides if he'll take it.

Femi Adebayo

19, from Clapton. Ran for his school, wants a trainer sponsorship. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.91c2e8f69243e771]{CH5}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.43e544512ad2ec27]{S10} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.29f6bfb5c06395f9]{S17} give him races and real introductions. A proper sponsor wants appearances and a clean name; a crooked patron pays faster and wants a different kind of loyalty.

Big Sal Moretti

26, from Bethnal Green. Pat's nephew, and he wants to run the crew. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.168214c02948a6c4]{CH7}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cb91b5ade40c2d38]{LB7} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.6990428a48394631]{S13} offer leadership, a public scrap and the knock-on for everyone else. A vote, or a stake everyone's agreed, beats "my auntie said so". Sal can build his own firm or line up behind somebody else's.

SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

The Final Night and Later Campaigns

The Quiet Hour, three turns, and every way it can end.

When to kick it off

Start the final night once the crew's picked a side that matters and the guilty parties are ready to make their move. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.7052e00fca53338b.JournalEntryPage.ff3b1ea8bdffa686]{AD8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.c19a5cc4367c0ae7]{VC8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.01b43c4291081cb5]{TU8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.71478f1c8a685daf]{BM8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.1fb049db18a7ccb6]{LD7}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.1c6a4266500f4558]{MR7}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.4189bb0e67e391ed]{RT8} are all different ways into the same night. Run the night once. The other career finales become the prep or the aftermath, each with its own payday for its own work. You don't need every other finale done first.

Three turns, called out loud

Arrival: who's there, and what each front does next. Commitment: the signatures, the cargo and the broadcast slot start moving. Consequence: whatever nobody stopped happens.

The crew gets one main job on the ground each turn and can hand named allies other jobs they can actually do. Say what they can handle — people, wheels, permission — before you agree a plan. A big Influence score doesn't magic up an army.

The broadcast

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST8} Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage runs the mobile programme. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC2} Round Chapel, or the event wing at @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST2}, can host a public crowd. The Dead Air lot, the Velvet Circuit and the Red Thread each bring a different version and different acts. A report that stands up, a propaganda slot, a private deal or pulling the plug — each one changes who trusts the station afterwards. Any transmitter site or stage beyond these is still NEED MAP.

The money and the signatures

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7} Meridian Sales Pavilion and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG8} Quayline Records Suite hold the deals; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB5} can host a made-up hearing. Celia and Lark can offer a cut, sign new terms, walk away or dig their heels in. The crew can haggle with all the evidence or just some of it. A frozen contract doesn't pay the workers or decide where anyone lives.

The buildings and the people in them

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW8} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8} are where the "who stays, who goes, who gets looked after" calls happen. Borough Mutual, the people living there and whoever the crew's brought decide what stuff, rooms and deals they'll protect. One tenant can take a fair, open offer while their neighbour holds out. Even a crook's base needs a real deal with the people who used it before.

The vans and the official story

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7} sends out the timed loads; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW8} is where Rusk runs his contractors; @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF6} is a public meeting point on the platform. The Towpath Union can turn a willing driver round, the Lantern Desk can keep one record safe, and the Chainring can get one particular motor back. The crew has to say which load or which person they're moving. Ordinary market business carries on — it's not the same as the forced removals or the evidence run.

How it can end

It all comes out

A solid public account with the originals still around can stop particular deals and start an investigation. Write down who's actually implicated and what's still owed. Next season is about paying people back, traders who've lost their pitch, a station with a hole in its budget, and rivals bidding for whatever's now up for grabs.

The people win

The crew helps the tenants, drivers, performers and the station put together a funded alternative. They get a say, or a stake — and the job of keeping it alive. Next season opens with a supplier going bust, a row over who gets what, and a very tempting takeover offer.

The crew takes over

The crew uses the evidence, the Halo debt or their grip on transport to take the made-up premises and the faction income. Track the new enemies: the patrons they pushed out, unpaid workers, customers, and a couple of very interested detectives. That power makes protection, recovery and succession jobs — not an automatic moral verdict.

The crew goes corporate

The crew takes a Meridian role or negotiates a changed buy-up. Write down the price, who actually signed, who's protected and whose claims got left out. Later: an investor pulls out, the new owners can't afford a promise, and a rival's sitting on a surviving copy.

Cash out, or fall out

A private sale can buy Pat's workshop, fund Jaz's garage or clear Danny's debt — and leave the other fronts hanging. If the crew splits, each lot gets something real and something they owe. A failed attempt changes the buildings, the programme or the patron; it doesn't wipe the sandbox.

Who's rubbing who up the wrong way, and what the crew can do about it.

WhoThe aggroWhat the crew can do about it

The Smoke — Sandbox Campaign

Map Production and Approach Insets

GM FILE · TABLE NOTES

London has an overview, twenty district street maps, four starter interiors, and the campaign’s venue interiors and approach maps. Travel at an exit using its button; ENTER pins take you to the prepared venue. Riders and their vehicle travel together. Sat nav carries the next stop over the boundary.

The Mission Board’s Prepare this mission’s maps imports the relevant locations and cast. The Venue Register links each key to the mapped room/approach; the GM controls access and discovery. Existing-world setup adds missing content and repairs backgrounds without moving placed PCs. A chase keeps its scene and waits for unresolved responses before travel.

Approach maps show entrances, cover and the street context for a venue; interiors show its rooms. Use the venue’s own key and register link. Prepare maps ahead of play so an entrance does not interrupt a decision.

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.cd201b2206536334]{← Previous} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.ced14cab1f6d94db.JournalEntryPage.3e9358c94b97eef0]{Rules index}
SANDBOX CAMPAIGN

Source Notes and GM Records

Where it all came from, and what to write down at the table.

Where it came from

The map list started from the original source archive, the-smoke-source-v0.1.3.zip: its twenty street maps, four interiors, content and overview (source hash d5b94bbe72e68d1162cbaf58e0e72f16ce197ebb71c740a496bc06f4e9d5b6e1).

The real places were checked against public venue, operator, council, heritage and directory pages. Each real venue in the register links to its page. A source tells you the place exists and where it is — not the made-up contact, the room layout, the fictional crime or the game price.

A few places sit just off the edge of a drawn street or tile. Their district is a game choice, and the approach maps fill the gap. The atlas is a game map, not a survey.

Everything was checked: all 160 venue uses, eight venues per district, 960 room references, every "continue with" code, every street anchor and every route between districts. It's an outline for prep — nobody's claiming it's been playtested to death.

Keeping track at the table

RecordWhat to write down
FactionRenown, rank, Influence, how they feel about you right now, and who your patron is.
VenueMap status; Known, Entered, Trusted or Claimed; who sponsored you; which rooms you're actually allowed in; what it costs and what you owe.
EvidenceOriginal or copy, where it came from, what it really shows, what's still a guess, who's holding it and who it's promised to.
JobWho the client is, the fee, exactly what counts as done, what the other side does next, the deadline, and anyone still with a claim.
City turnWho got the chance to move, the one thing you showed happening, which person or building it hit, and when the crew can next do something about it.
PropertyWho actually owns it, the share or lease, the deposit, weekly costs, staff, stock and what's still owed.

FACTION · CH

The Chainring

Pat's lot. Bikes off the rack at nine, sold on by teatime, and nobody on Morning Lane saw a thing.

Auntie Pat runs the arches like a corner shop with a back door. Out front: tyres, inner tubes, a kettle that never goes cold. Out back: the biggest bike-nicking operation in E8, and a ledger in her head that goes back to 1989. She'll buy anything with two wheels and a frame number she can grind off, and she pays cash, on the nail, no haggling.

But don't get it twisted. Pat's got rules. You don't rob the old boy on the estate, you don't rob a kid's bike off the school railings, and you don't make a frightened neighbour pay for your fun. Take a risk with someone who can afford it, fine. Bring trouble to her door, and you're out. When she offers you a stake in the business — and she will, if you last — it comes with the debts, the claimants and the weekly rent, not just the wonga.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{AR4 Pat's Office [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7 Chainring Storehouse [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Spanner Rob wants a proper workshop with proper invoices, the soppy sod. Kez wants the runners treated like mates, not like something you scrape off your shoe. Pat likes it quiet. And Big Sal — Pat's own nephew — wants it loud, bigger, harder, and there's a few younger lads who'd follow him there. Nobody in the Chainring speaks for all of it, whatever they tell you.

Crossing them (and making up)

Leave a recovery Pat promised someone, or sell her buyers to a rival, and the shutter stays down when you knock. Hold your hands up to a cock-up, pay it back in full, and she'll put the kettle on again. Probably.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownPat puts you in front of one of her buyers. Be on time.
R7 TrustedThe workshop is yours for agreed jobs: stands, tools, Spanner if he likes you.
R12 ConnectedOne recovery motor kept back for you, when there is one.
R18 InsiderA say in which jobs the crew takes and what the suppliers get.
R25 PillarA proper stake: a cut of the business or a seat at the co-op table.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — A valuation, or Pat makes a call and gets you a foot in a door round here.

2 — A slot on the stands, or a motor on loan (deposit up front, bring it back clean).

4 — Pat calls the meeting nobody else could and puts one of her own favours on the table.

Places that open up

Earn the stands at the Chainring Storehouse (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7}) and the Clifden Crew Garage (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8}) comes up for grabs — Kez's mate's old garage. Keys to the Arches (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.db462a370713a911.JournalEntryPage.957a87da24e85625]{CH8}) is where you find out what a share actually costs: the price, the people still owed, and who's opening up on a Monday.

The score

Pat's done a bulk buy and it's gone a bit Pete Tong. The Oddments Lockup in Highbury is full of frames — some fair game, some nicked off a kids' cycling club, and one bag with a courier's whole life in it. A collector's paid a deposit on the lot and his lorry's coming. Get in, sort the wheat from the chaff, and get the dodgy ones somewhere nobody's looking.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB7.2} Oddments Lockup, sorting floor: forty frames, one torch, one hour. Savvy to read the stickers and frame numbers; the courier's papers are in a saddlebag in @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB7.3}.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW1.4} Hackney Marshes Centre: the club organiser's on a Thursday committee night. She'll tell you which bikes were donated — if you don't look like the people who nicked them. Front.
  • The run: load the disputed bikes and get them across to the Clifden Crew Garage before the lorry. Wheels if you're spotted leaving.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8.2} Clifden Crew Garage: identify every bike (Graft). In @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8.4}, a vehicle title in a biscuit tin — the garage could be yours one day.

Route: HB / CG / DA / HC / WW / HC

The heat

The collector's removal lorry pulls up outside @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB7} after your second nose about. Two blokes, a tail lift and a clipboard. Pay them, stall them, or argue the toss — otherwise they load everything that isn't nailed down and that's that.

Your call

Fence the lot and laugh all the way to the bank. Separate the club's bikes and send them home. Keep the courier's papers as leverage. Or take less money and a repair contract with the club.

What it leads to

The Oddments Lockup becomes somewhere you can stash. Help the club and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8}'s repair bay opens, with a tenancy on the cards. Keep the pricey groupset and its owner hires someone to come and get it.

The twist

The collector's deposit was paid by Quayline Advisory — the same lot that's been buying up leases on Morning Lane.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1 The six premises were selected before the public trouble}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

The score

A bike nicked off Pat's patch has been given a respray and entered in a sponsored showcase at the Lee Valley VeloPark. The sponsor reckons it's theirs, the rider reckons it's his, and Pat reckons it's hers. Get in, get it, get out — ideally before they put it on a podium in front of the cameras.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY1.3} Leyton Orient stadium, hospitality: the showcase's launch do. Blag an invite and a lanyard (Front).
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON1.4} Lee Valley VeloPark, club room: the bike's being prepped for the meet. Graft to lift it from the stand, or wait for the race.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF7.3} Kingsland Courier Arch: the courier who delivered it knows who paid. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW5.3} The Kenton: that's where the next handover is.
  • The set piece: a rival rider takes the bike out on the track towards the prize-giving. Chase him round the velodrome (Moves), nick it in the pits, or meet his price.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR8.2} Goldsmiths Riding Workshop: Kez shows you what a legit future looks like — if you fund it.

Route: LY / ON / ST / VW / WS / LF / DA / HC / WW / HC / DA / LF / HR

The heat

The rival rider wheels the bike towards the prize-giving with a photographer in tow. Once the sponsor presents it on camera, it's theirs in the eyes of everyone who matters.

Your call

Hand Pat her score. Ransom it back to the sponsor for a fee. Expose the sponsor's paperwork. Or put the money into Kez's riding workshop and walk away with a future instead of a payout.

What it leads to

The VeloPark and the stadium both open up for event work; the Courier Arch gives you dispatch contacts. Fund @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR8} and you own an asset with running costs. Sell privately and the original owner is still out there, still angry.

The twist

The 'rival rider' is the original owner. He nicked it back from the thief first.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The call

Auntie Pat

Bloke called Lark came in the shop today. Nice suit. Smelt of money.

Offered me a tidy sum to walk away from the arches. Said half the street's already empty.

It isn't. I want to know who Lark works for before I sign anything, sweetheart. Find out.

Where

The score

Meridian Renewal's fixer, Evan Lark, is buying Pat out — and quietly telling everyone else on the street that it's already a ghost town. It's a con. Six occupied premises have been written up as empty so they can be bought for peanuts. Pat wants the paperwork, the names, and the real price of her shop.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB8.4} Orchard Lease Office, deed archive: break in after hours, or blag the morning clerk. The acquisition schedule is dated weeks before any of the 'trouble' on the street. Savvy to read the dates.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB8.4} Essex Dry Goods: the workers got the same offer as Pat — word for word. They're scared, not stupid.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8.3} Clapton Union Rooms: the repair office has a copy of the 'vacant' survey. Someone was living there when it was signed.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB5.3} Stoke Newington Town Hall: a property meeting in the committee room. Lark's there, smiling. Front him out in public, or corner him in the car park.

Route: HB / CG / DB / CG / DA / HC / CL / SN / HB

The heat

Lark ups his offer to Pat the minute the tenants start comparing copies — a cheque on the counter, today only. The meeting closes one offer, but the owners and the records are still out there afterwards.

Your call

Look after Pat and only Pat. Get the whole street to bid together. Sell the dated schedule to whoever pays most. Or shake Lark's hand and take a job with Meridian.

What it leads to

Whatever you settle sets Pat's Renown. The six-property stitch-up becomes a real lead (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1}). A private deal keeps the shop open but the neighbours find out what you signed sooner or later — and they don't forget.

The twist

The 'surveyor' who signed the vacant report is Esther Cole — and she didn't sign it. Somebody forged her.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The score

Turf war or treaty — it's decided in one room. Stretch wants to carve up East London's bike and van trade, and Pat would rather her crew held the pen. Get the votes, deal with Daz, and walk out with a compact people actually stick to.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{AR1} Pat's Cycle Repairs: Pat's terms, over a brew. Write them down.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL7.2} Lea Bridge Social Rooms, members' room: the Lea Boys are split down the middle — Stretch's lot and Moth's lot. Find out who's wobbling.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF7.3} Roman Exchange and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX7.2} Tern Wharf Dispatch: the fences and the drivers. Whoever they back, wins.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC5.4} MOTH Club back room: the sit-down. Front for the talking, Savvy to spot whose debts are real, Muscle and Bottle if it kicks off.

Route: HC / CL / HC / WS / BG / OF / BG / HR / HX / DB / CG / DA / HC

The heat

Daz barges in mid-meeting with a 'recovered' tool chest and a car full of youngers ready to take it back by force. Deal with the box while the room decides whether to stay at the table or walk.

Your call

Guarantee a limited peace. Back Moth. Side with Stretch. Grab the whole lot for yourselves. Or let them all split and pick up the pieces. Whatever you pick, name who pays each real debt — out loud.

What it leads to

The compact opens the back rooms at the Social Rooms, Roman Exchange and Tern Wharf for proper talks. Threats, broken promises and public wins all turn into names — friends and enemies — who'll be back.

The twist

The tool chest has a false bottom: Rusk's payment ledger for the 'trouble' on Morning Lane (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5}).

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5 Private payments and the official story overlap}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

The score

Endgame for the Chainring. Pat offers the crew a real stake on the same night Meridian tries to close every deal in the district. Pick a base, find the money, be in the room when the pens come out, and stop another crew walking off with something Pat pledged years ago.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7.5} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8.4}: walk round both yards with Pat. Which one's home? What does it cost a week, who's still owed, who opens up on Monday?
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7.2} Glasshouse Saleroom: a buyer — or a backer — at the auction floor. Clement Wren's people are about.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7.4} Meridian Sales Pavilion, signing room: the papers. Celia's there. So's Lark.
  • Meanwhile: another crew is on its way to collect the thing Pat pledged. Wheels to beat them to it.

Route: HC / DA / CG / DA / HC / WS / VW / ST

The heat

Rusk's collector and a tenants' delegation both turn up expecting a promise you can't give both of them. Each turn of the final night, sort one recovery or one deal — no more.

Your call

Keep it a fence. Turn it into a repair co-op. Take over the whole patch. Take Meridian's buyout. Or move the lot somewhere they'll never find it. Pat gets her say in whichever you choose.

What it leads to

Write it down: your actual share, the keys, the kit, the debt. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7} or @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC8} becomes your headquarters for good; the other stays someone else's unless you agree otherwise.

The twist

The pledged asset is the arches' own lease. Pat put it up against a loan from Vic Randle years ago to keep Sal out of trouble — and Vic sold the debt to Quayline last month.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1 The six premises were selected before the public trouble}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

FACTION · AD

Dead Air Collective

Pirate radio off a tower-block roof. No licence, no sponsor, no boss — and they'd like to keep it that way.

Dead Air's been on 98.something since before half your crew could walk. Jungle at midnight, gospel on a Sunday morning, phone-ins about the council, shout-outs to the mandem and their nans. The rig lives in the back of Backspin Studio in Dalston; the archive lives in Leon Marsh's spare room and his head. Everyone round here listens. Nobody admits it to the Bill.

What they want is simple and nearly impossible: enough money and enough reliable bodies to stay on air without selling the airwaves to a sponsor or a street boss. The crime's mostly the broadcasting, plus a bit of creative borrowing when it comes to speakers. Most of the people on the mic are just ordinary people with something to say — which is exactly why somebody's started faking one of their voices.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA7 Backspin Studio [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF8 Englefield Listening Flat [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Dee Hassan wants Dead Air standing on its own two feet — no sponsors, no favours, nobody's logo on the wall but theirs. Leon Marsh wants the archive treated proper; forty years of tapes ain't a prop. And Nia 'Switch' Bell tells her own story, ta very much, and nobody twists it. Patch'll bend if it keeps the signal on air. The young DJs want airtime; the old guard reckon if every show turns into a court case, the listeners'll be gone by Friday.

Crossing them (and making up)

Grass up a contributor who was promised they'd stay anonymous, or put words in the station's mouth, and you've burnt it. Want it back? Get on air, own it, and make it right with something they can actually use.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownPatch books you in to meet the right person, at a proper time.
R7 TrustedYour own regular slot. Shout-outs to your mum optional.
R12 ConnectedThe archive — the bits the contributors have cleared for use.
R18 InsiderA say in who the station partners with.
R25 PillarA seat on the editorial table, or your own independent show, on paper.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — Leon names that tune or that voice, or someone agrees to meet you.

2 — First dibs on the recording kit, or an appeal read out on air at a set time.

4 — A live phone-in or public forum, run by station volunteers, on your terms.

Places that open up

Get in with Patch and Backspin Studio (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA7}) is yours to work out of. Leon opens the Englefield Listening Flat (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF8}) for archive sessions by appointment. Win the last night and the Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST8}) can become a paid-for mobile studio with your name on the editorial terms.

The score

Patch's sound system has been hijacked by paperwork. Someone changed the name on the hire account at the Queensbridge Sound Store, and a rival promoter's already got the cases on a tail lift. No rig, no night, no station. Get it back — or get something — before the Round Chapel doors open.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR7.2} Queensbridge Sound Store, speaker hall: the stacks with Dead Air's gaffer tape still on them. Savvy to spot the doctored hire slip.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA2.3} Cafe OTO, mix desk: a visiting performer let slip who booked the 'replacement' rig. Front.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA7.3} Backspin Studio live room: Patch's HQ. Plan the snatch, or plan a smaller show.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC2.2} Round Chapel event hall: the night itself — or the showdown with the rival promoter in front of three hundred people.

Route: HR / LF / DA / HC

The heat

After your second enquiry the van starts loading. If it pulls off, it's a Wheels job through Haggerston traffic. And the Round Chapel doors open at eight whether you've got the full rig or a borrowed PA and a prayer.

Your call

Nick the speakers back. Hire replacements and eat the cost. Move the whole night. Or back the rival promoter for a bigger fee and let Patch find out later.

What it leads to

Do right by Patch and Backspin Studio's working room is yours, plus the next station job. The Sound Store becomes a hire contact; stiff a supplier and they become a creditor who rings every Friday.

The twist

The rival promoter is working for Owen Pike — the Velvet Circuit wants Dead Air's audience, not its speakers.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The score

Nia 'Switch' Bell, Dead Air's best voice, has gone quiet. A seller turns up with a reel of her 'latest message' — but it opens with a station ident that hasn't been used in over a decade. Someone's selling a ghost, and Patch wants to know whose.

FACTION · LB

The Lea Boys

Debts, doors and a cold store full of trouble. Lea Bridge belongs to them — for now.

The Lea Boys run collections from Lea Bridge to Leyton: debts, 'insurance', a bit of everything that falls off a lorry, and the Halo trade that's got the whole of East London on edge. Stretch is the face — tall, quiet, always in a fresh tracksuit, always two moves ahead. He sees your crew as handy labour today and competition tomorrow.

Moth is the one to watch. She's been in since she was a teenager and she's sick of the firm being used as everyone's fall guy. Stretch has been talking to money men in nice suits. Moth thinks the deal will chew up the Lea Boys' own and spit them out. Back the right horse and you'll have a seat at the table. Back the wrong one and you'll be the next debt they collect.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL7 Lea Bridge Social Rooms [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8 Larch Cold Store [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Tessa 'Moth' Price is all about loyalty to the patch. Daz Riley, the collector, just wants quick money and a big reputation — and he's not fussy how. Stretch fancies a partnership with Meridian; Moth wants a base nobody can sell from under them. Daz and some of the younger lot want to go harder. Others want out of debts they never signed up for.

Crossing them (and making up)

Rob from a settlement you agreed, or grass a protected source to an enemy, and whoever backed you turns on you — properly. You can't undo the Renown, but you can split the firm, pay it back, or find yourselves a new patron.

1 — An intro to a local who wants to help (or wants it known they did).

2 — A sit-down arranged, or a key to one Lea Boys room for a night.

4 — Moth or Stretch spends real political capital to broker a big truce.

Places that open up

The Lea Bridge Social Rooms (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL7}) open collector meetings; the Larch Cold Store (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8}) opens the cargo side — and its mysteries. Who Speaks for the Lea Boys (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.cb91b5ade40c2d38]{LB7}) decides who runs the firm; The Price of a Patch (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.3ad0e65c45f2f9b3]{LB8}) decides what your crew is inside it.

The call

Moth

Halo. A whole load of it, sat in the Larch Cold Store waiting for Stretch's buyer.

I want it gone before he collects.

Owen Pike'll pay more if it ends up with his promoters instead. Your choice. Don't get nicked.

Objectives

  1. Get the pickup time from the collector at The Crooked Billet (ticks itself)
  2. Get into the Larch Cold Store and reach the stock (ticks itself)
  3. Deal with the other crew when they show up
  4. Your call: deliver to Moth, sell to Owen at the Blue Hour Basement, keep it, trade it, or have it pulled

£160 crew fee3 XP+2 Renown · The Lea Boys+1 InfluenceOffered at Renown 3

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL3 The Crooked Billet} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8 Larch Cold Store} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8 Blue Hour Basement} MAPPED

The score

A warehouse job, proper GTA. A consignment of Halo is chilling in the Larch Cold Store waiting for Stretch's buyer. Moth wants it lifted from under his nose; Owen Pike's offering more if it lands with his promoters. Get in, get the goods, get out — and try not to bump into the other crew who had the same idea.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL3.2} The Crooked Billet, snug: a collector who's had a few tells you the pickup time.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8.2} to @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8.5} Larch Cold Store: in through the loading hall, past the night office, into the damaged-goods cage. Graft for the locks, Savvy for the guard's rounds.
  • The other crew turns up mid-job. Muscle, or a very quick deal.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8.5} Blue Hour Basement cash room: Owen's cash-for-cargo swap, if you go that way.

Route: CL / HM / LY / HM / CL / HC / DA

The heat

The rival crew lands the moment you commit. Then the handover van rolls in early, so the stock, a warehouse worker who shouldn't be there, and the invoice are all in the same place at once.

Your call

Deliver to Moth. Sell to Owen. Keep it. Trade it to another faction. Or arrange for it to disappear, quietly, for compensation.

What it leads to

Your patron pays for the result they agreed. The cold store opens the bad-batch mystery (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E2}); the Blue Hour opens the nightlife network. Get caught selling it twice and you've made a very specific enemy.

The twist

The invoice says the load was changed at the depot two days ago — and signed for by somebody from 'East Cross Security'.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E2 The Halo load was deliberately changed}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

The score

The Halo batch put people in hospital. Stretch wants the leftovers back on the street; Moth's convinced the Lea Boys were set up to take the fall for a switch somebody else made. Follow it from the people who got hurt to the booking that changed — while a collector moves what's left.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG8.3} Approach Recovery Rooms, support room: a courier who got hurt, who'll talk if you treat him like a person.

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8.5} Larch Cold Store, night office: the changed booking. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{AE3} Majors, Homerton A&E: an independent hospital account, if the witness gets there.

A collector starts shifting the rest of the load at the same time one witness needs an ambulance. You can't do both — pick a priority and name an ally for the other.

Your call

Carry on trading. Steal the stock. Get it pulled off the street. Or sell the proof that it was switched.

What it leads to

The accounts link Owen and Rusk to the switch (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E2}). What you do with the trade changes named people and the Halo front. Telling one faction doesn't mean every rival finds out.

The courier who got hurt is Daz's little brother. Daz doesn't know yet.

The Boy Who Kept Receipts

The Coach and Horses · Well Street Loan Office · The Red Lion · Interview Room

One of our juniors kept receipts. For debts that never existed.

Objectives

Where

The score

A young collector's been keeping a little black book of made-up debts — who was squeezed, for what, on whose say-so. Stretch wants the book and the kid. Moth wants the book to use against Stretch. The kid wants to get on a coach at Victoria and never come back. Everyone else wants a piece.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY6.3} The Coach and Horses, function room: the kid, nervous, selling. A rival's watching from the bar.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.25c01e80cc3ba50e]{WS8.4} Well Street Loan Office, ledger store: the duplicate books. Graft.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN4.2} The Red Lion, snug: the handover — or the ambush. Moves if it turns into a foot chase.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{CU4} Interview Room: the other road. DS Vale will take the book and the kid, on terms.

Route: LY / HM / CL / HC / WS / HC / CL / SN

The heat

The kid's got a ticket and a rival on his tail. After two scenes, the book moves — with or without a deal — and someone gets it the hard way.

Your call

Deliver the book. Deliver the book and the kid. Help him get away. Sell it twice. Or take it to Vale for a supervised settlement.

What it leads to

Whoever you deliver to moves up. If the handover goes wrong, the driver, the duplicates and whoever ended up holding it keep the trail warm (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5}).

The twist

Half the 'debts' in the book were invented on instruction from Meridian's people — squeezing tenants until they'd sign anything.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5 Private payments and the official story overlap}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

Stretch has shown the lads a deal. Meridian Renewal. Money, 'consultancy', a future.

Everyone's gassed. I'm not.

Find out what it actually costs before anyone signs. Please.

The score

Stretch has brought a gift home: a partnership with Meridian Renewal. Money for the lads, consultancy fees, respectability. Moth smells a stitch-up. Get behind the champagne and find the invoice that shows what the Lea Boys are really being paid to do.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON8.3} North Park Hospitality Lodge, private lounge: the pitch. Canapés, a PowerPoint, Celia Voss's best smile.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB3.3} De Beauvoir Block, meeting room: a hired suite with a 'consultancy invoice' in the filing cabinet. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG8.2} Quayline Records Suite, boardroom: Lark and the money man in one room. Front for a counter-offer — Bottle to turn down a fortune.

Route: ON / ST / VW / WS / LF / DB / CG

The heat

Celia offers Stretch a cushy retirement while the members expect more work and more patch. The reception ends with a handshake that's nearly a signature.

Your call

Back the deal. Renegotiate. Help Moth split the firm. Sell the documents. Or take your own consultancy fee and smile.

What it leads to

Whoever you backed counts it. The property options link together (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1}). A leak changes everything once it's traced or goes public — but the debts are real either way.

The twist

The 'consultancy' the Lea Boys would be paid for is clearing tenants out of the six buildings.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1 The six premises were selected before the public trouble}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

Who Speaks for the Lea Boys

York Hall · Lea Bridge Social Rooms · Hackney Marshes North Pavilion · MOTH Club

See the vote through at the MOTH ClubAutomatic map event

XP5 to each registered PC.

The call

Moth

I'm challenging him. Out loud. At the MOTH Club.

Stretch don't get to sign us all away.

Your crew's got a name now. Where you stand changes who leads us. Or splits us.

Objectives

  1. Sort out the disputed pledge at the York Hall fight night (ticks itself)
  2. Gather the members' demands at the Lea Bridge Social Rooms (ticks itself)
  3. Protect the threatened runner at the Hackney Marshes North Pavilion (ticks itself)
  4. See the vote through at the MOTH Club (ticks itself)

£640 crew fee5 XP+5 Renown · The Lea Boys+1 InfluenceOffered at Renown 15

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG3 York Hall} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL7 Lea Bridge Social Rooms} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM1 Hackney Marshes North Pavilion} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC5 MOTH Club} MAPPED

The score

Coup night. Moth's calling Stretch out in front of the whole firm. The crew's reputation could tip it — new boss, same boss, or two firms where there used to be one. Gather the votes, protect the vulnerable, and keep the knives in pockets for as long as possible.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG3.3} York Hall training hall: a fight night. A pledge was made on the result — and it's disputed.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL7.2} Lea Bridge Social Rooms: the members' demands. Write them down; they'll matter.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM1.4} Hackney Marshes North Pavilion, club room: a runner who's been threatened for picking a side.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC5.4} MOTH Club back room: the vote. Front to build a coalition, Bottle to make the challenge, Muscle if it all goes off.

Route: BG / WS / HC / CL / HM / CL / HC

The heat

Daz turns a real debt into a public humiliation in front of everyone. A scrap breaks out and gets attention while the members weigh up who'll keep them paid.

Your call

Keep Stretch. Back Moth. Take the top job yourselves. Split the firm down the middle. Or negotiate a way out. Name the members and the money behind each side.

What it leads to

The new leadership offers you @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.985bf9584d9294e7.JournalEntryPage.3ad0e65c45f2f9b3]{LB8}. The losers don't vanish — they keep members, debts and witnesses. You get a political position, with real limits and real responsibilities (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5}).

The twist

Stretch has already signed. The Meridian deal went through last week. Tonight's vote is about whether anyone honours it.

The score

The final night, from the Lea Boys' side. Meridian's moving on every building at once. The firm can ride the wave, fight it, or sell a chunk of the patch and walk. Whatever deal you broker, the members have to accept it — or it won't hold past breakfast.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8.3} Clapton Union Rooms: the residents' claim. They want the Lea Boys gone as much as Meridian.

The heat

One offer saves the core business by throwing another household under the bus. Collections, publicity and signatures all happen on separate final-night turns — you can't be everywhere.

Your call

Build a smaller, tighter street crew. Take the whole patch. Go into business with Meridian. Or sell the patch and get out with your skin.

What it leads to

Top rank gets you the role or the independent branch you agreed. Write down the real premises, income, creditors and enemies — and remember the real venues belong to their owners, not the firm (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6}).

Daz has been selling the firm's plans to Rusk all along. He's in the car park with Rusk's people.

FACTION · VC

The Velvet Circuit

Club nights, guest lists and a cash room behind the DJ booth. Owen Pike's circuit — until somebody reads his books.

The Velvet Circuit is every promoter who matters east of Kingsland Road, held together by Owen Pike's phone and Owen Pike's money. Basement raves in Dalston, warehouse do's in the Wick, benefit nights with your favourite DJ's favourite DJ. They decide who gets booked, who gets paid, and who gets blacklisted for asking about it.

Owen's the problem. Lovely bloke, mate — everyone's mate — with a hand in the Halo supply and a much bigger hand reaching for Meridian's property money. The staff, the punters and the actual venues aren't in on any of it; they just want a good night and their wages. Owen's spent years making sure nobody looks too closely at the account book. Your crew is about to look very closely.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8 Blue Hour Basement [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON7 North Echo Rehearsal Rooms [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Door manager Reece Hale wants his staff paid, on time, every time. Mara Sol, the performer everyone wants on their flyer, wants a career that isn't owned by Owen. Owen's busy hiding the Halo switch and where his money came from. The working promoters want independence, the staff want wages and a safe night, and the corporate sponsors just want nothing embarrassing on the bill.

Crossing them (and making up)

Make up a claim in the Circuit's name or leave promised wages unpaid and the promoter who backed you goes cold. Anyone you hurt doing their dirty work becomes a named victim with friends — and a grudge.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownAn intro to a promoter who returns your calls.
R7 TrustedPaid bookings come to you first.
R12 ConnectedA seat in the private scheduling meetings — who plays where, when.
R18 InsiderA vote when a sponsor comes knocking.
R25 PillarA real share: ownership, a co-op seat, or your own venue deal.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — A performer happy to meet you.

2 — A rehearsal slot booked, or a rig on agreed hire.

4 — A whole benefit night: named acts, a budget that actually adds up.

Places that open up

The Blue Hour Basement (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8}) opens sound work, the cash room and the private promoter meetings. North Echo Rehearsal Rooms (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON7}) is where the acts warm up. Who Owns the Night (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.c19a5cc4367c0ae7]{VC8}) can land you a cut of fictional club money — with the debts attached.

The score

Owen's rig has vanished days before his club night. The lads who moved it say he never paid for it in the first place — and a rival promoter's already paid for it to land at his gig instead. Owen wants it back. Whether he deserves it is another question.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8.3} Blue Hour Basement, DJ booth: Owen's version, with a lot of hand gestures.

The rival's paid for same-day delivery. The hired driver's got another job after this one and leaves after your second enquiry — with or without the case.

Steal back the rig. Settle Owen's unpaid hire bill. Bring in a smaller system. Or sell the booking to the rival promoter.

A clean recovery opens @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.e90759230df2d2c6]{VC2} and repeat supplier contacts. Do it dirty and you get criminal money — and a worker or buyer with proof of the debt.

The twist

The 'unpaid hire' was paid — in cash, out of the Halo float. The supplier just won't say so out loud.

A headliner's vanished a week before the show and their costumes are being held hostage over a debt nobody can explain. Owen wants his act on stage. The act wants out of Owen's world. And a hired heavy called Harlan Black is moving the kit tonight.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA3.4} Dalston Superstore, back room: a visiting promoter describes the missing act — and who they've been seen with.

Harlan Black's hired muscle is moving the belongings before the final rehearsal. The performer has their own plan and a rival employer's offer in their pocket.

Your call

Force the booking through. Rescue the performer and their stuff. Broker a clean exit. Or take a replacement fee from the rival.

What it leads to

Whoever you backed pays out. Cross Harlan and he's a freelance enemy for life. The performer can become a contact, a rival or a witness — and they're not part of Meridian's scheme, whatever anyone tells you.

The 'debt' is Owen's. He borrowed against the performer's fee and spent it.

Get the cash back. Steal it for yourselves. Expose the missing fee. Credit a different sponsor. Or run a smaller, agreed bill.

What it leads to

Proof here opens the money trail (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5}). Whatever you settle keeps a show alive — or leaves an unpaid claim that follows Owen and you into later jobs.

The twist

The 'payer' at the gala is Evan Lark. The benefit was a laundromat with a raffle.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5 Private payments and the official story overlap}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

Someone's had a Halo shipment off me. Robbed. Proper liberty.

Owen calls it theft. The supplier says the contents were switched. A rival's paying a premium for what's left. Meanwhile real people are in hospital. Walk into the middle of all of it and decide which story's true — and who gets the case.

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY8.3} Larch Cold Store, stock room: the disputed stock. Graft to get to it, Savvy to see it's been tampered with.

Your call

Deliver the stock. Get it withdrawn. Take the rival's fee. Or trade the paperwork that comes with it for something better.

What it leads to

Your sponsor pays out. The evidence backs up the deliberate switch (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E2}). Carry on trading and the harm lands on named people, who become your opposition — no free money here.

The score

An unreleased DJ set has the same room tone and samples as the fake 'Halo warning' — proof it was stitched together. Owen wants it back (and buried). The performer wants it preserved. A collector's paid for the original and is threatening to blacklist the artist if it surfaces.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN5.5} The Shacklewell Arms, green room: a backstage meeting that names the session.

The heat

The collector's paid for the original and is threatening to finish the performer's career. The handover goes contested the moment the private listening starts.

Your call

Sell the rough mix. Keep a copy somewhere safe. Hand it to Owen. Or bargain for a limited public release.

What it leads to

An authenticated version proves the warning's fake (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E3}). Lose one original and the rehearsal and Leon's word still stand; whoever holds the original now has a lever on the next event.

The twist

The 'collector' is Bram Senn — the producer who made the fake. He's cleaning up after himself.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

How it goes down

The guarantor is Martin Rusk. Owen's 'nightlife partnership' is a security contract with a sound system.

The score

Final night. The Circuit's future is up for grabs and the crew's being offered a share. Owen's account book is the bargaining chip in every room. Get it, divide the deliveries, and stand on a stage at the London Stadium to announce who owns the night — before someone else does.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA8.5} Blue Hour Basement, cash room: the book, or whoever's holding it and their price.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7.2} Marshgate Delivery Depot, dispatch office: allocate the last deliveries — kit, cash, people.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST2.5} London Stadium event wing and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST8.3} Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage: the programme and the live link. Front for ownership; Bottle for the final promise.

The heat

Two promoters both claim the right to make the announcement. Staff threaten to walk if the show hides their unpaid wages. Another buyer's waving cash for your stake, right now.

Your call

Form a promoters' co-op. Take criminal control. Accept corporate funding. Split the Circuit. Or sell your stake and go.

What it leads to

Write down your real share, venue deals, debts and promised work. Top rank keeps the Circuit running — with rival promoters and the workers you affected shaping next season (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6}).

The twist

Mara Sol has been recording every promoters' meeting for a year. She'll trade the tapes for her freedom — or broadcast them.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

FACTION · TU

The Towpath Union

If it moves in East London — parcels, passengers, a van that shouldn't exist — Tern's lot moved it.

The Towpath Union started as a handful of cycle couriers on the canal and grew into the dispatch network everyone uses and nobody admits to: vans, bikes, drivers, a radio room above a wharf in Hoxton and a depot at Marshgate. Mara 'Tern' Boyd runs the board. If she says a delivery's on, it's on.

Most of the Union is just graft — parcels, flowers, flat-pack furniture up five flights. Some of it's dodgier, and every driver chooses what they'll carry. What the Union wants is steady routes, paid workers, and the right to say no to a job that stinks. Keep your promises when two clients are pulling in opposite directions and you'll go far. Lose a passenger you swore to deliver and you'll walk home.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX7 Tern Wharf Dispatch [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7 Marshgate Delivery Depot [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Gita Mercer, the dispatcher, looks after the drivers like they're her own kids. Yasmin Dale wants contracts that can't bin her staff overnight. Tern's tempted by a big-money sale to Meridian. The independent drivers would rather a smaller co-op. And a fat criminal client can drag the same members two ways at once.

Crossing them (and making up)

Sell someone's private route contacts, or leave a passenger you promised standing on the kerb, and that's a named breach with a named victim. Fixing it means paying them back and agreeing new terms with the person you let down.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownA dispatcher who answers when you call.
R7 TrustedFirst dibs on paid runs.
R12 ConnectedAn invite when the routes get planned.
R18 InsiderA say in who gets which contract.
R25 PillarAuthority over dispatch, or a defined share if it sells.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — A message delivered, or a quote for a run.

2 — A driver and a vehicle booked, on clear terms.

4 — A small multi-vehicle job: volunteers, fuel and seats all named and counted.

Places that open up

Tern Wharf Dispatch (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX7}) opens the radio room; the Marshgate Delivery Depot (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7}) opens the wider fleet. The City Still Has to Move (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.01b43c4291081cb5]{TU8}) hands out real contracts, real vans and real fuel — not free taxis for life.

The score

A wrong delivery that's starting to look like a right one for somebody. A music case went to the wrong customer, signed for under a fake name, and it's already on the market. Tern wants it back before her driver gets the blame — and wants to know why anyone would bother.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF7.3} Kingsland Courier Arch, parcel bench: two deliveries, one route, one very confused driver. Front.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX7.2} Tern Wharf Dispatch: the board shows a substitute driver nobody booked. Who?
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR5.3} Hackney City Farm meeting room: a volunteers' meeting, and a collector who wants what's inside the case — sheet music and a cassette, nothing valuable. So why? Graft to get it back.

Route: LF / DB / HX / HR

The heat

A second customer is already selling the case. After two enquiries, a paid delivery moves it on from where you last saw it — Moves to catch the courier.

Your call

Get the right case back. Pay off the customer who got muddled. Steal both loads. Or sell it on privately and settle with Tern after.

What it leads to

Do it right and dispatch work opens, with the Courier Arch and the Wharf as your contacts. A missing case leaves a named buyer, sender and payment — the trail doesn't vanish.

The twist

The cassette in the case is an old Dead Air session with Nia on it. Someone's collecting her voice.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The score

One van, three owners. Pat says it's her recovery, the hire firm says it's theirs, the cargo buyer says he's paid. Tern's drivers are caught in the middle. A dockside dinner on a barge should settle it — until a second recovery crew shows up.

How it goes down

  • EX-BREAKERS Bow Breakers Yard: where the van actually changed hands.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC7.5} Chainring Storehouse, office: Pat's frame inventory — what was really in the back.

The heat

The second crew's claimant has already paid, and the van's promised to another job tonight. Somebody's leaving that dock unhappy.

Your call

Compensate one claimant. Divide the cargo. Steal the van back. Or sell it to a rival and live with the leftover debt.

What it leads to

A documented recovery opens bigger transport jobs. Barge East becomes a regular meeting spot. A missing van can still be got back from a named hirer or buyer — on their terms (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1}).

  5. Your call: give the book back, keep a copy, sell it to Meridian, help the courier vanish, or broker a new deal

£240 crew fee3 XP+3 Renown · The Towpath Union+1 InfluenceOffered at Renown 5

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF5 The Duke of Wellington} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX5 The Narrowboat} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM7 Orient Night Shed} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW2 HBC Community Centre} MAPPED

The score

Tern's route book — every address, every gate code, every back door the Union's ever used — has gone missing with a courier who dumped a delivery and ran. The courier says the book shows a pattern: the places in it are being targeted. Somebody's already trying to sell it. Canal-side chase, anyone?

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF5.2} The Duke of Wellington, snug: a buyer quietly offering the book for sale.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX5.2} The Narrowboat: the canal-side handover. Watch the towpath.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM7.6} Orient Night Shed, service yard: the chase or the intercept — Moves on foot, Wheels if she gets on a bike.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW2.3} HBC Community Centre, meeting room: the courier's new patron, offering her a way out.

Route: LF / DB / HX / DB / CG / DA / HC / CL / HM / WW

The heat

A collector follows the courier through a packed public meeting. Sort the chase or the bargain first — then worry about the pattern.

Your call

Return the book untouched. Keep a copy for yourselves. Sell it to Meridian. Help the courier leave. Or broker a new dispatch agreement that keeps everyone working.

What it leads to

Your settlement restores or splits the Union's routes. Customers are still their own people. A lost original can be rebuilt — at a cost, while a rival nicks one contract (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1}).

The twist

Six of the addresses in the book are the six 'empty' buildings. The book proves they were occupied when the vacant reports were filed.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1 The six premises were selected before the public trouble}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

TU5 · THE TOWPATH UNION · MARA "TERN" BOYD

Not the Person in the Photograph

London Aquatics Centre · Lee Valley Hockey and Tennis Centre · Bethnal Green Library · Hub67

MISSION BOARD · TU5

Offer: TU Renown 8. Suggested personal Rep 1; the Board’s predecessor and faction gates control availability.

ObjectiveTracked by

Find the real booking at the Lee Valley Hockey and Tennis CentreAutomatic map event
Date the photo at Bethnal Green LibraryAutomatic map event
Find the later witness at the Hub67 screeningAutomatic map event

The call

Mara "Tern" Boyd

There's a photo going round. One of mine, supposedly driving Nia the night she went missing.

It's not him. I know for a FACT two drivers were each told half that journey.

Clear his name before he loses his job. Quick.

Objectives

  1. Pin down the claimed pickup at the London Aquatics Centre (ticks itself)
  2. Find the real booking at the Lee Valley Hockey and Tennis Centre (ticks itself)
  3. Date the photo at Bethnal Green Library (ticks itself)
  4. Find the later witness at the Hub67 screening (ticks itself)
  5. Your call: clear the driver, give Vale the account, sell the photo, or trade the truth for a contract

£320 crew fee5 XP+3 Renown · The Towpath Union+1 InfluenceOffered at Renown 8

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST3 London Aquatics Centre} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON2 Lee Valley Hockey and Tennis Centre} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG5 Bethnal Green Library} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW6 Hub67} MAPPED

The score

A photo's doing the rounds of one of Tern's drivers apparently ferrying Nia away the night she vanished. It's being used to smear him and the Union. Tern knows the job was split between two drivers who were each told half. Prove what really happened — without giving away where Nia is now.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST3.4} London Aquatics Centre, club room: the claimed pickup — an event meeting, lots of witnesses.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON2.4} Lee Valley Hockey and Tennis Centre, club room: the real booking, in the bookings book. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG5.3} Bethnal Green Library, study room: the photo's an old public appearance — date it.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW6.3} Hub67, meeting room: a screening, and a later witness who saw the actual car. Front.

Route: ST / ON / ST / BF / OF / BG / OF / VW / WW

The heat

The lie spreads at shift change. You can kill it fast, or protect a source while another driver loses work.

Your call

Clear the driver. Give DS Vale a proper account. Sell the photo. Or trade the truth for a transport contract.

What it leads to

The journey proves part of Nia's story (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E4}) and contradicts the official version of who moved whom. The sports and community venues open passenger work — without giving away Nia's hideout.

The twist

The person who leaked the photo works in Meridian's 'community engagement' team.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E4 Nia is alive and chose to leave her routine}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

The Contract That Eats the Route

Temple Mills International Depot · The Baring · Meridian Sales Pavilion

MISSION BOARD · TU6

Offer: TU Renown 11. Suggested personal Rep 1; the Board’s predecessor and faction gates control availability.

ObjectiveTracked by
Find the paying customer at Temple Mills International DepotAutomatic map event
Find the real guarantor at The BaringAutomatic map event
Take the sale — or a counter-offer — to the Meridian Sales PavilionAutomatic map event
Your call: sell the network, fund a co-op, split the routes, or take a private feeGM / Self-play tick
RewardCurrent payout
Crew fee£480 shared; each registered PC gets floor(£480 ÷ crew count).
XP5 to each registered PC.
Crew RenownTU: +4.
InfluenceRestore 1 with the paying faction, capped by rank.

Fencing and shift payments are separate. The GM runs story decisions; Self-play owners can tick objectives in that mode. Register the crew before starting.

The call

Mara "Tern" Boyd

Meridian wants to buy our contracts. All of them.

They'll keep the drivers they like. The rest? Not their problem.

Before I say yes or no, I want to know EXACTLY who gets left behind.

Objectives

  1. Find the paying customer at Temple Mills International Depot (ticks itself)
  2. Find the real guarantor at The Baring (ticks itself)
  3. Take the sale — or a counter-offer — to the Meridian Sales Pavilion (ticks itself)
  4. Your call: sell the network, fund a co-op, split the routes, or take a private fee

£480 crew fee5 XP+4 Renown · The Towpath Union+1 InfluenceOffered at Renown 11

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM5 Temple Mills International Depot} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX6 The Baring} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7 Meridian Sales Pavilion} MAPPED

The score

Meridian's offering to buy the Union's contracts and hire the drivers it fancies. It's a lot of money. Tern's tempted. But she wants to know who gets binned, who's paying, and what Meridian actually wants with a courier network.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM5.3} Temple Mills International Depot, workshop: a 'visitor interview' that names the paying customer.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX6.3} The Baring, function room: the real guarantor at a private meeting. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7.3} Meridian Sales Pavilion, investor lounge: the sale — or your counter-offer. Front; Bottle when they offer you a cut.

Route: HM / CL / HC / DA / CG / DB / HX / DB / LF / WS / VW / ST

The heat

The customer's next load leaves while the members argue. After two scenes, name one livelihood your crew has protected — or traded away.

Your call

Sell the network. Fund a smaller co-op. Split the routes. Or take a private fee for delivering a rival's contracts.

What it leads to

The deal opens @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.5f6a9fc17d4ae6dc]{TU7} and exposes the shared payer (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6}). Blow the negotiation and one customer goes elsewhere — you get a recovery job, not the end of the world.

The twist

Meridian don't want the network for deliveries. They want it for the Quiet Hour: every van in the East End, on one night, on their schedule.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6 The Quiet Hour is coordinated across four fronts}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

Four Loads One Customer

Marshgate Delivery Depot · The View Tube · New Spitalfields Market produce hall

MISSION BOARD · TU7

Offer: TU Renown 15. Suggested personal Rep 1; the Board’s predecessor and faction gates control availability.

ObjectiveTracked by
Compare the four dispatch sheets at the Marshgate Delivery DepotAutomatic map event
Clear one harmless load with the courier at the View TubeGM / Self-play tick
Link a load to the property visits through the trader's goods at New SpitalfieldsAutomatic map event

XP5 to each registered PC.
Crew RenownTU: +5.
InfluenceRestore 1 with the paying faction, capped by rank.
