The call

Mara "Tern" Boyd

Four deliveries on the big night. One payer.

Most of it's ordinary trade. One of the loads ISN'T.

And I've got one van free. One. Make it count.

Objectives

  1. Compare the four dispatch sheets at the Marshgate Delivery Depot (ticks itself)
  2. Clear one harmless load with the courier at the View Tube
  3. Link a load to the property visits through the trader's goods at New Spitalfields (ticks itself)
  4. Decide which loads move, which stop, and which get redirected

£640 crew fee5 XP+5 Renown · The Towpath Union+1 InfluenceOffered at Renown 15

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7 Marshgate Delivery Depot} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF2 The View Tube} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM2 New Spitalfields Market produce hall} MAPPED

The score

Four drops on the final night, all paid for by the same account. Three are normal — veg, flat-packs, a band's backline. One's part of Meridian's operation to clear the six buildings. One van's free. Work out which is which before the wrong cargo reaches the wrong door.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF7.2} Marshgate Delivery Depot, dispatch office: the four dispatch sheets, side by side. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF2.3} The View Tube, side booth: a courier who can vouch one load's harmless.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM2.4} New Spitalfields Market, packing room: a trader's goods that link another load to the property visits.

Route: BF / OF / VW / WW / HM

The heat

Two collections are due at the same time and you've got one van. A second run needs an actual driver, an actual vehicle and actual room in it.

Your call

Keep honest business moving. Deliver all four for the fee and ask no questions. Expose the harmful job. Or redirect a named consignment somewhere it'll do some good.

What it leads to

A transport plan proves the night is coordinated (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6}) and gives the finale real vehicles. Get a load wrong and its actual owner wants compensation — or revenge. Ordinary work carries on regardless.

The twist

The 'band's backline' is Rusk's crew and their gear, hidden in flight cases.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6 The Quiet Hour is coordinated across four fronts}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

The City Still Has to Move

Tern Wharf Dispatch · Pudding Mill Lane DLR station · Ambulance Bay · Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage

MISSION BOARD · TU8

Offer: TU Renown 20. Suggested personal Rep 1; the Board’s predecessor and faction gates control availability.

ObjectiveTracked by
Allocate the drivers at Tern Wharf DispatchAutomatic map event
Run the passenger-and-case handover at Pudding Mill LaneAutomatic map event
Get the urgent run to the Homerton ambulance bayAutomatic map event
Collect the broadcast van from Bridge NineGM / Self-play tick
Decide who gets priority: a witness, a passenger, a paid load, a contract, or a dealGM / Self-play tick
RewardCurrent payout
Crew fee£1000 shared; each registered PC gets floor(£1000 ÷ crew count).
XP5 to each registered PC.
Crew RenownTU: +5.
InfluenceRestore 2 with the paying faction, capped by rank.

Fencing and shift payments are separate. The GM runs story decisions; Self-play owners can tick objectives in that mode. Register the crew before starting.

The call

Mara "Tern" Boyd

Every firm in East London wants priority transport tonight.

I'm handing you dispatch. The whole board. 📻

Make a plan that actually works and it's yours for keeps. Mess it up and someone's stood in the rain. Over.

Objectives

  1. Allocate the drivers at Tern Wharf Dispatch (ticks itself)
  2. Run the passenger-and-case handover at Pudding Mill Lane (ticks itself)
  3. Get the urgent run to the Homerton ambulance bay (ticks itself)
  4. Collect the broadcast van from Bridge Nine
  5. Decide who gets priority: a witness, a passenger, a paid load, a contract, or a deal

£1000 crew fee5 XP+5 Renown · The Towpath Union+2 InfluenceOffered at Renown 20

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX7 Tern Wharf Dispatch} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF6 Pudding Mill Lane DLR station} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{AE1 Ambulance Bay} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST8 Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage} MAPPED

The score

The Quiet Hour, from the radio room. Every faction wants a van, a driver, a priority route. Tern hands the crew the dispatch board — if they can make a final plan that actually works. Witnesses, cases, patients and a broadcast van all need moving on one night with not enough wheels.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX7.2} Tern Wharf Dispatch: allocate the drivers. Front.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF6.2} Pudding Mill Lane DLR covered concourse: a passenger-and-case handover timed to a train pulling in. Moves.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{AE1} Homerton ambulance bay: an urgent hospital run.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST8.1} Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage, van bay: the broadcast van — or another final collection. Wheels.

Route: HX / HR / BG / OF / BF / OF / BG / WS / HC / WS / VW / ST

The heat

One van breaks down between two promises. Each final-night turn you can run one crew job yourselves, plus whatever your allies agreed to take on.

Your call

Put the witness first. Or the urgent passenger. Or the paid criminal load. Or the corporate contract. Or stitch a deal together that gets most of them there.

What it leads to

You get the dispatch role or sale share you agreed. Write down the vehicles you control, the drivers' terms, and every promise you missed. Tern Wharf can become your base if the ownership deal backs it (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6}).

The twist

Tern sold the board to Meridian an hour before the night started. Your plan is running on their network — and they can see every move.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6 The Quiet Hour is coordinated across four fronts}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

FACTION · GE

The Glasshouse Exchange

Art, antiques and anything worth more than it looks. Clement Wren will sell it — and he'll swear blind he never asked where it came from.

The Glasshouse Exchange is Clement Wren's world: auction rooms in Canonbury, a saleroom with a back door, restorers in Fish Island and buyers who pay in cash and never give their real names. Wren grew up in Bow and sounds like Chelsea — until he's annoyed. He loves good work, genuinely, and he'll happily make a fortune off a title he knows is iffy.

That's where your crew comes in. A sale needs judgement, nerve, sometimes a very discreet 'recovery' at three in the morning. Wren pays well and asks you not to talk about it. The trouble is, the biggest sale of his life is coming — property options on six 'empty' buildings that aren't empty — and staying neutral is about to get very expensive.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7 Glasshouse Saleroom [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF5 The Trampery Fish Island Village [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Restorer Luca Ferretti cares who actually owns a thing. Curator Iris Bellamy wants honest loans, full stop. Fixer Evie Slate likes it murky — murky pays. The restorers want a legit specialist business; the criminal buyers like things vague. Wren thinks he can keep both sides happy, right up until Meridian's money makes him choose.

Crossing them (and making up)

Fiddle an agreed valuation, or drag an unrelated client into the light, and Wren's door stays shut. Selling something honest to a buyer who knows exactly what they're getting? That's just business — even if the business is crooked.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownAn intro to a specialist buyer.
R7 TrustedPrivate valuation appointments.
R12 ConnectedInvites to the previews before the public sees anything.
R18 InsiderA broker's say in the big sales.
R25 PillarA proper partnership, or keeper of the archive.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — A valuation, or someone agrees to meet you.

2 — A specialist consultation or a preview slot.

4 — A multi-party sale, a restitution meeting, or a whole exhibition.

Places that open up

The Glasshouse Saleroom (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7}) opens valuations, previews and the auction floor. At The Trampery on Fish Island (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF5}) you book a project room — you're a tenant, not the owner, whatever Evie tells you.

The call

Clement Wren

Clement Wren. We haven't met. We're about to.

A vintage racing bicycle. Exquisite restoration. Genuinely beautiful work.

The seller's story of where it came from, however, is a work of fiction. I need it authenticated before Friday. Discreetly.

Objectives

  1. See the bike with the collector at The Highbury Barn Tavern (ticks itself)
  2. Get the mechanic at the VeloPark to say who really did the work (ticks itself)
  3. Deal with Evie Slate's offer to make the bike vanish
  4. Be at the Glasshouse Saleroom preview (ticks itself)
  5. Your call: recover it, buy the title, fence it to a buyer who knows, or certify the lie

£80 crew fee3 XP+1 Renown · The Glasshouse Exchange+1 InfluenceOffered at Renown 0

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB4 The Highbury Barn Tavern} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON1 Lee Valley VeloPark} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7 Glasshouse Saleroom} MAPPED

The score

Wren's got a buyer lined up for a stunning vintage racer. The restoration's real; the seller's tale of where it came from is pure porkies. Wren wants it authenticated before the sale — or at least wants to know how bad the lie is. Evie Slate wants it gone before anyone asks.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB4.2} The Highbury Barn Tavern, snug: a collector shows off the bike over a large red wine.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON1.4} Lee Valley VeloPark, club room: a visiting mechanic recognises the work — and who it was done for. Savvy.
  • Evie Slate turns up with an envelope of cash to make the bike disappear before the mechanic talks. Front or Graft.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7.3} Glasshouse Saleroom, preview room: the preview, where the real owner — or a rival bidder — can blow it all up.

Route: HB / CG / DA / HC / WW / ON / WW / HC / DA / CG

The heat

The buyer walks out after the preview and takes the argument with him to the next place he's going — find him there, or lose the sale.

Your call

Recover a stolen collectable. Buy the disputed title. Fence it to a buyer who knows exactly what it is. Or certify the lie for a bigger fee.

What it leads to

Done properly, it opens @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.6f05d96dac3745b1.JournalEntryPage.3e3e6c8f62b9dee1]{GE2} and the saleroom's preview rooms. A fake certificate pays fast — but the real owner keeps the proof and can hire someone to come and get it.

The twist

The bike was nicked from Pat's patch. Pat would very much like it back.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The call

Oona Reyes

Hi — Oona. I make costumes. I perform in them.

My coat's gone missing after a show. It's a year of my life, that coat.

There's a collector after it, and he doesn't care about the coat. He cares about the lining. I just want my work back.

Objectives

  1. Find out who borrowed the coat at the Rosemary Branch Theatre (ticks itself)
  2. Find the courier at the Sebright Arms (ticks itself)
  3. Get into the loan preview at Sutton House (ticks itself)
  4. Get the restorer at The Scolt Head to read the note in the lining (ticks itself)
  5. Your call: return the lot, sell the invitation, swap the costume, or expose who leaned on her

£120 crew fee3 XP+2 Renown · The Glasshouse Exchange+1 InfluenceOffered at Renown 1

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX3 Rosemary Branch Theatre} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR6 Sebright Arms} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC3 Sutton House} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB5 The Scolt Head} MAPPED

The score

A performer's coat has been 'borrowed' and won't come back. A collector's sniffing round it — not for the tailoring, but for what's stitched into the lining. Find the coat, read the lining, and work out who's been pressuring Oona to turn up where she's told.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX3.5} Rosemary Branch Theatre, dressing room: after a show — who borrowed the coat, and for whom.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR6.5} Sebright Arms, green room: the courier who carried it.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC3.4} Sutton House, workroom: an arranged 'loan preview'. Someone's showing off the coat. Front for the disputed loan.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB5.3} The Scolt Head, function room: a visiting restorer clocks the appointment note sewn into the lining. Savvy.

Route: HX / HR / BG / WS / HC / DA / CG / DB

The heat

The buyer's wearing the coat and getting ready to leave. Grab it during the party (Moves), or follow him to his next known stop.

Your call

Give Oona her coat and the note. Sell the invitation. Swap in another costume. Or expose the employer who pressured her into going.

What it leads to

A fair — or profitable — deal opens the private-buyer network. Keep the note and you've got a meeting to crash; whoever it was meant for can take it, refuse it or counter.

The twist

The note in the lining is an appointment at the Quayline Records Suite — with a name on it that isn't Oona's. She was the messenger and never knew.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

Routine. Except one buyer is paying a ridiculous sum for a dull framed print.

Nobody pays a ridiculous sum for a dull framed print. The removal men are already loading. Hurry.

The score

A house clearance in Canonbury. The executor wants the borrowed pieces identified and returned before the lot gets sold. One buyer's offering silly money for a boring framed print — which means it isn't boring. The removal van's already being loaded.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG2.3} Estorick Collection, viewing room: the loan enquiry — what came from where.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB3.5} St Mary's New Church, record cupboard: a visiting family historian names the original lender. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB7.4} Split Second Archive, photograph table: compare the letters behind the print with an old station photo.
  • The frame: secure a hold, or nick it before the hammer comes down. Graft.

Route: CG / HB / CG / DB

The heat

The removal crew starts loading while two buyers bid for the frame. After a preview and one more scene, it's sold — unless you've got a hold on it or it's already in your van.

Your call

Keep the letters for a collector. Return what was borrowed. Exploit the confused title. Or turn it into a public-history story.

What it leads to

A tidy clearance opens later specialist work and backs up the six-property story (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1}). If the frame sells early, the executor still has an inventory and the buyer is your next target.

The twist

The letters behind the print are tenancy agreements for the Clapton Union Rooms — signed, dated, and very much alive.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1 The six premises were selected before the public trouble}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

The score

An art caper, proper. A loan exhibition lost a piece one day and its papers the next. Wren wants the object; the artist who made it wants the truth about its sale out in the open. Two collectors are about to claim the final crate. Time for a switch, a snatch or a very smooth purchase.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG1.3} Young V&A, study room: an adults-only preview — find the missing crate.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF5.4} The Trampery, Fish Island: a tenant's workspace with the ordinary packing account. Savvy for who owned what.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG7.2} Glasshouse Saleroom, auction floor: the private viewing. A rival wants something loud to happen. Graft for the caper, Front for the buyer.

Route: BG / OF / BG / HR / HX / DB / CG

The heat

Two collectors both claim the final crate as the preview opens. Run it like a heist: theft, switch, purchase or recovery — every room has a challenge.

Your call

Return the object. Broker a sale. Keep the original and pass on a fake. Or expose the broker's private deal.

What it leads to

Sort the loan and you've got specialist access and more of the six-property story (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1}). A fake buys time — but the artist, the inventory and the buyer can all find out later.

The twist

The broker's private deal was with Celia Voss's personal art adviser. The piece was a sweetener.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

A slick presentation contains film of an 'inspection' that was shot before the inspection took place — and there's a visitor in the frame who shouldn't be. Wren's client wants the original quietly returned. Your crew wants to know who the visitor is and who paid him.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON4.3} The Stratford hotel, guest meeting room: a reception — the visitor's real appointment that day.

The client stalls by disputing the artist's fee. The hotel witness can only meet before clocking off. And a collector already has a rival offer on the table.

Your call

The 'visitor' is Inspector Gavin Holt, in plain clothes, on Meridian's dime.

Run the gala, work the three auction rounds, and decide whether Wren's biggest sale goes through, goes wrong, or goes to someone else entirely.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY4.3} Leyton Great Hall, committee room: the gala. Meet the bidders over warm fizz.

Three auction rounds, played out loud. Each one shows a bidder's hand and moves the ledger closer to its new owner. Split the crew up, or bring in named help.

Your call

Close the criminal deal. Steal the ledger. Force honest terms. Redirect the sale to a funded coalition. Or sell the occupiers an early warning.

You get a new role in the Exchange and back up the six-property story (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1}). Stopping the auction just moves it behind closed doors — the tenants' rights still need sorting.

FACTION · BB

The Backroom Bookmakers

Odds, IOUs and a back room above a bookies on the High Road. Vic Randle always gets paid. Eventually.

Victor 'Vic' Randle's been taking bets in Leyton since the days of chalkboards and blue biros, and lending money for nearly as long. The Third Half Bookroom is the shop front; the Shepherdess Coin Rooms is where the real business gets done — private tables, private loans, private ways of reminding people what they owe.

Vic loves numbers because he thinks numbers mean nobody's to blame. Debt's debt, son. Except somebody's been inventing debts — writing names in books for money never lent — and Vic's own fortune is riding on a property bet that only pays out if six buildings are 'empty'. As your crew climbs, you stop seeing what people owe and start seeing how the numbers got there.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY7 Third Half Bookroom [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX8 Shepherdess Coin Rooms [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Eddie Lane on the till wants real debts kept separate from the made-up ones. Frankie Wu, the accountant, wants books that'd survive an audit. Vic's big property bet puts the ordinary staff's jobs on the line. Eddie wants a fairer house. Some of the collectors prefer fear — fear means nobody checks whether the debt was ever real.

Crossing them (and making up)

Take two fees for jobs that cancel each other out, or cook an account, and a named creditor wants your head. Fix the record and the real money's still there to argue about.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownA cashier who knows your face.
R7 TrustedYour own debts, on your own terms.
R12 ConnectedInvites to the money meetings.
R18 InsiderA say when the big debts get called in or written off.
R25 PillarA real stake — or backing for a different, fairer kind of lending.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — An account checked, or an introduction.

2 — A short extension, agreed by whoever's owed.

4 — Vic backs one big settlement with his own money, on stated terms.

Places that open up

The Third Half Bookroom (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY7}) and the Shepherdess Coin Rooms (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.357679fcd032b6ef]{HX8}) open the ledgers, the private tables and the counting room. The score

A charity kickabout on the Marshes has attracted the kind of bets that smell of a fix. Vic wants to know if his own middleman is rigging it behind his back. Somebody's leaning on a player, there's an envelope in a changing room, and the prize-giving's at half four.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL6.3} The Elderfield, function room: who approached the runner, and with what.

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b096f49f5fcfe272]{LY5.4} Score Leisure Centre, club room: a training session where the threatened athlete can face the payer. Moves for a challenge on the pitch.

Route: CL / HM / LY

The heat

The prize-giving starts after two main scenes. One middleman wants you to enforce the fix; the other wants the payoff robbed before it's counted.

Your call

Back the rigged result. Expose it. Steal the payoff. Cancel all bets. Or run a fair rematch with the organiser.

What it leads to

Sort it and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.0001dbbd03496b6f]{BB3} opens, plus sports contacts. A profitable fix leaves an athlete, a collector or a robbed punter who knows exactly who to come after.

The twist

The middleman isn't fixing it for himself. He's fixing it for Daz — who needs the money to pay off Vic.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

Vic fronted an advance for a big night. The promoter says it paid the acts; the acts say they got nothing. Owen Pike's desperate to keep it hush-hush. Follow the money from the budget to the cash room to a hired suite with a duplicate invoice and a nervous signatory.

What it leads to

A clean settlement opens regular event finance. A cover-up buys you Owen as an ally — and leaves a worker with an invoice that turns up again later (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5}).

The person being asked to sign the duplicate invoice is Frankie Wu. She refuses — and asks you to get her out.

Danny 'Tealeaf' Doyle's name has turned up in a loan book for money he never borrowed. Someone's manufacturing debts and selling them on. Vic wants the ledger — it's an opportunity, son. Danny might want something else when he sees what's written next to his name.

Your call

A verified correction proves the debt-making scheme (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E5}). The fake entry was written the week of the funeral, by the same 'helpful' bloke who sorted the flowers. He's done it to every grieving family on the estate.

FACTION · NM

The Night Market

Anything you want, nothing you can prove. Pearl Okonkwo keeps the stalls honest — mostly.

The Night Market ain't a place, it's a phone tree. A few hundred traders, house-clearers, record dealers and blokes-with-a-van who'll buy, sell or swap anything that fits in a Transit. Some of it fell off a lorry. Some of it was pushed. Pearl Okonkwo runs the Roman Exchange and sits in the middle of the lot, making sure nobody gets ripped off by anyone except the customer.

Pearl's thing is simple: strength in numbers. If the traders stick together, no developer, gangster or 'collector' can come in and say they own the pitch. Problem is, plenty of people would love to say exactly that — and a few of Pearl's own would happily sell her out for an exclusive. Stall Seventeen (a made-up unit in a real market — the honest traders around it are just doing their jobs) is where you start.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF7 Roman Exchange [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM2 New Spitalfields Market produce hall [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Nessa Grey on the stalls looks after her regulars like family. Len Fisk, the broker, wants one fat exclusive resale deal and doesn't care who he steps on to get it. Pearl wants everyone bargaining together. Len wants the corporate money. The independents can pick a side — or tell the lot of them nobody speaks for them, ta very much.

Crossing them (and making up)

Flog someone's gear or someone's phone number past what was agreed, and the traders you burnt will remember. Pearl's standing comes from the traders backing her — not from anyone pretending every stall in East London takes her orders.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownAn intro to a broker.
R7 TrustedFront of the queue for ordinary resale jobs.
R12 ConnectedA seat when the big house clearances get carved up.
R18 InsiderA say in how the network runs.
R25 PillarA cooperative seat — or a proper slice of a concession.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — Point you at a buyer or seller who wants to deal.

2 — Hold a stall or a specialist appointment at the usual rate.

4 — Pearl gets everyone round one table to settle who owns what, and puts her own name on it.

Places that open up

The Roman Exchange (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF7}) opens valuations and resale work. Stall Seventeen at the New Spitalfields produce hall (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM2}) is a made-up trader unit inside a real market; later on it pays off as a trader you can rely on — or a stake in the Exchange.

Pearl here, love. Bit of a mess at stall seventeen.

Half a delivery went to the wrong customer and the clerk knows it.

Find it before some clowns calling themselves 'collectors' use it to say they run my traders.

  3. See off the collector demanding a fee nobody agreed
  4. Settle it at the Roman Exchange (ticks itself)

The score

Half a load for Stall Seventeen walked off with the wrong punter, and a gang of self-appointed 'collectors' is circling, ready to use the cock-up to say they're in charge of the traders now. Pearl wants the gear traced and the chancers put back in their box.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM2.3} New Spitalfields produce hall, the trader's unit: the paperwork tells you what was ordered. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL2.2} The Princess of Wales, saloon bar: the van driver and the bloke who drove off with it, same table, one round each.
  • A 'collector' turns up mid-trading demanding a fee nobody agreed. Graft — or a firm word.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF7.2} Roman Exchange, front counter: the last chance to buy it back, sell it on, or hand it over.

Route: HM / CL / HC / WS / BG / OF

The heat

A collector strolls in during trading hours with his hand out. After two enquiries the next buyer drives off with the gear.

Your call

Get the load back. Buy the mistaken sale off the punter. Keep the best bits. Sign up with the collectors. Or show the whole market they're nobody.

What it leads to

Do it right and Pearl's network opens up. If the gear's sold on, the buyer and the unpaid bill are another job down the line. The real market around the stall isn't anyone's gang — don't treat it like one.

The twist

The 'collectors' are on Len Fisk's payroll. He wants Pearl looking weak before the concession talks.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The score

A middleman's waving a document that says the traders backed redevelopment. Pearl never saw it. The residents remember signing a form about fixing the roof. Meanwhile Len Fisk's been offered an exclusive and a collector's lining up a forced clearance.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB8.4} Essex Dry Goods, warehouse floor: what the workers were actually told.

The heat

Len Fisk offers Pearl a private concession while a collector gets ready for a forced clearance. One lot of traders will take the move; another lot won't budge.

Your call

Take the buyout. Expose the dodgy mandate. Negotiate a properly funded move. Split the network. Or sell the earlier version to someone who'll use it.

What it leads to

A settlement that holds supports @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1} and gives Pearl something to bargain with. Fail and the traders split into rival camps, each with its own next offer.

The twist

The signatures are real — copied off the repair forms. The person who swapped the pages works in Meridian's sales pavilion.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The score

Pearl's putting on a record-and-repair fair to fund the network's next move. A promoter's offering to plug the hole in the budget — as long as he controls the programme. Someone else is offering money to cancel it outright. And a projector and a master tape have gone missing from the hire returns.

A rival's waving cash to make the fair go away. Doors open after two prep scenes — a smaller do is still on the cards.

Run it independent. Take sponsorship, with the names on the poster. Sell exclusive access. Fence the valuable reel. Or call it off and pay the bills.

What it leads to

Pull it off and there's a real fund and a crowd who'll turn up again. Fail and you're left with contracts, unpaid hire and a recording whose owner can still do a deal.

The promoter's money comes from Owen Pike. The rival trying to cancel it? Also Owen Pike.

FACTION · BM

Borough Mutual

Hot dinners, cold facts. Rosa Baptiste keeps people in their homes — and she'll work with anyone who helps.

Borough Mutual started as a soup kitchen in a church hall and never stopped growing. Food parcels, rent advice, a van for moving day, a lawyer who works for biscuits. Rosa Baptiste runs it out of Saint Martha House with a clipboard, a kettle and zero patience for speeches that don't put a roof over anyone's head.

Rosa will work with a crew like yours if the job helps somebody. That don't mean she approves of what else you get up to, and she'll tell you so to your face. The Mutual's clout comes from people choosing to stick together — not from Rosa bossing the whole estate about. And right now, the whole estate's got a target on it.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN7 Saint Martha House [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF8 Carpenters Breakfast Club [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Adele Mensah, a tenant, wants it in writing or it didn't happen. Tariq Evans, the advocate, won't let anyone speak for someone who hasn't said yes. Gwen Price, the organiser, wants a funded future, not another protest. Some members will take a paid move. Others want a co-op bid, or a proper public fight. Rosa won't pretend a good speech pays the rent.

Crossing them (and making up)

Blab someone's private story when you promised you wouldn't, or pinch what was meant for a family, and you've burnt it. Want back in? Put it right with something real — and let the person decide if they'll have you back.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownAn organiser who answers your calls.
R7 TrustedAn invite to the planning meetings.
R12 ConnectedRunning one funded project.
R18 InsiderA voice for the Mutual — with limits everyone agreed.
R25 PillarA proper community mandate, with people holding you to it.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — An introduction, or a practical job agreed.

2 — A volunteer for a bit, or a room booked.

4 — A full campaign or support push, with the money and the people it helps named.

Places that open up

Saint Martha House (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN7}) opens a regular kitchen and advice night. The Carpenters Breakfast Club (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF8}) adds the residents' negotiations. A seat at the top needs the people who use it behind you, and a room budget you can actually afford.

The score

A family's getting hammered by two collectors at once — one's owed, one's a chancer with a fake book. Meanwhile Mo at the Chicken Palace is still waiting on the grub. Rosa wants both sorted tonight, and she don't care which order.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN7.1} Saint Martha House, kitchen: the food boxes and Rosa's terms. No freebies, no favours, just do it right.

Daz wants to make an example of someone right now. Mo wants his dinner. Hand a mate the means and they'll take one job off your plate.

Your call

Talk the collectors into a pause. Pay the genuine balance. Rob the collector. Expose the duplicate. Or take a private fee to enforce it yourselves.

What it leads to

Help that lands opens up Mutual work and the meeting room at Saint Martha. A missed delivery is still owed. How the collector reacts depends on who saw what.

The twist

The fake debt comes from the same duplicate book that's been forging Vic's entries (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.0487b331fc4a6aa5]{BB1}).

The score

Rosa's benefit gig has lost its room, its sound case and its fee in a single afternoon. Two crowds are getting rained on, and the case is about to leave on someone else's truck. Find a show, find a room, find the kit — or fold it honestly and pay the people who turned up.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM6.4} Leyton Jubilee Park pavilion, office: whoever double-booked it.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN6.3} St Paul's West Hackney, side hall: a smaller room. Tight but dry.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC1.5} Hackney Empire, scene dock: the missing stage case, about to go on the wrong lorry. Graft.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b1c3f967b6aa7594]{HR4.3} Haggerston Community Centre, meeting room: local acts happy to step up. Front.

Route: HM / CL / SN / CL / HC / DA / LF / HR

The heat

Rain shoves two crowds into a room built for one. The case leaves on another truck after the second scene; doors open on whatever you've managed to put together.

Your call

Get the case back. Hire a cheaper replacement. Merge the two nights. Take a sponsor's money with strings. Or cancel and pay the contracts properly.

What it leads to

A show that happens opens one funded community resource and venue contacts who'll call you back. Fail and there are workers, guests and creditors with your name on their lips.

The twist

The double booking wasn't an accident. Owen Pike booked the pavilion for a Velvet Circuit 'pop-up' — to see if the Mutual would fold.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

Rosa needs a coalition with teeth to stop the buy-ups. A lawyer's got a counter-proposal, the workers want their terms, and the town hall's given you one speaking slot in front of the buyer. There's a financier who'll back one plan — if you're straight about the debts.

A funded settlement means real, lasting Mutual clout. A speech that bombs still points at the next financier, owner or creditor. Shouting about it doesn't change who owns the deeds.

The financier is Vic Randle. He's betting both ways.

FACTION · LD

The Lantern Desk

A detective who wants the truth, and a crew who'd rather she didn't look too close. Awkward.

DS Harriet Vale ain't your mate. Get that straight from the off. She's Old Bill, she knows exactly what your crew does for a living, and she'll nick you the day it suits her. But right now she's after bigger fish — bent reports, bought officers, and a run of 'accidents' that keep landing on people who were in the way.

The Lantern Desk is Vale, a borrowed flat in Bethnal Green, and whoever she can trust this week. It's not the Met and you're not joining it. It's a source deal — you tell her things, she tells you some things back, and everyone pretends it's all above board. Her bosses would love her to stop digging. One of them's being paid to make sure she does.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG7 Lantern Case Flat [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{CU4 Interview Room [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

PC Isla Dunn wrote the original note and wants someone to actually read it. Inspector Gavin Holt wants awkward stories buried, and he's been taking consultancy money to help. Vale's careful, but she's ambitious too. Dunn's terrified of being the one who carries the can. Holt can lean on people — but he can't control every officer or shred every record.

Crossing them (and making up)

Get caught telling Vale porkies, or drop a source she promised to protect, and she'll stop picking up. Saying 'no thanks' to being her source is allowed — it don't make you guilty.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownA number she'll answer.
R7 TrustedRegular chats about the case — on the calendar.
R12 ConnectedA seat in one joint enquiry, with limits.
R18 InsiderA say in which lead she chases first.
R25 PillarA long-term source deal — or an independent review she'll stand behind.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — Set up a conversation everyone's agreed to.

2 — A proper enquiry, or an interview with a time on it.

4 — Vale burns her own credit to push for a review or protection for someone.

Places that open up

The Lantern Case Flat (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.78f07d621cc24fad]{BG7}) is a made-up meeting flat, and the Interview Room (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{CU4}) is the one you already know. What you get is reliable appointments, receipts for evidence and referrals that stand up — not a warrant card.

Build a case that holds. Steal the later draft. Use the contradiction to save one building. Or give Meridian time to fix it on the quiet.

FACTION · MR

Meridian Renewal

Glass towers, flat whites and 'exciting new communities'. Somebody's got to clear the old one out first.

Meridian Renewal sells the future. CGI flats with smiling couples on the balcony, a sales pavilion that smells of new carpet, and a launch party every other week. Celia Voss is the face of it — polished, posh and dead convinced that once the cranes go up, nobody'll care how the land was got.

How the land gets got is Martin Rusk's department. Head of 'security'. He's paid for fake vacancy reports, leaned on tenants, and hired crews like yours to do the bits that don't go in the brochure. Six occupied buildings stand between Meridian and the deal of the decade. You can help them get there, rob them blind on the way — or work out exactly where the bodies are buried and decide who to tell.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7 Meridian Sales Pavilion [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON8 North Park Hospitality Lodge [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Martin Rusk wants control and isn't fussy how. Esther Cole, the surveyor, just wants to do her job honestly — fat chance. Evan Lark, the middleman, handles the details nobody else wants to touch. The investors will take a cleaner deal if somebody pays for it. Get rid of Celia and the contracts are still sitting there.

Crossing them (and making up)

Flog Meridian's job to a rival behind their back and the executive you shafted becomes your enemy. Bring them a counter-offer openly — one that covers what's owed and has people behind it — and they might take it.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownAn intro to a contractor.
R7 TrustedFirst pick of the paid work.
R12 ConnectedAn invite to the project briefings.
R18 InsiderA voice in what gets proposed.
R25 PillarA consultancy or a slice of ownership — whatever the final deal actually gives you.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — A staff meeting in the diary.

2 — Kit hire on the account, or an authorised site visit.

4 — An executive backs one funded counter-proposal, with who wins and who pays spelled out.

Places that open up

The Meridian Sales Pavilion (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.7f001857f6166eed]{ST7}) and the North Park Hospitality Lodge (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.51d4cafdaaaa0837]{ON8}) open sales jobs, investor meetings and contract talks. Top rank gets you a consultancy or a share in a made-up asset — debts and all, out in the open.

A clean result opens corporate work. Keep a copy and you've got leverage — and a risk, if anyone finds out. Deliver it untouched and Esther and the freight note are still out there.

The score

Celia wants clearance papers dropped off and a report on which tenants will 'cooperate'. The papers say the opposite of what the surveyor wrote the first time. A tenants' delegation and a printer's runner both want the same proof, and Rusk wants you to write 'vacant' on rooms with people living in them.

A printer's runner and a tenants' delegation want the same proof. Rusk asks you to call occupied rooms vacant before the meeting opens.

Your call

Finish the bullying job and you've got named enemies. A leak only matters if someone can trace it back.

The later instructions came from Evan Lark's account — the same one Vic Randle's been lending through (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.f9a723352bb81bd2]{BB6}).

FACTION · RT

The Red Thread

Missing people, lost tapes, and stories nobody wanted told. Index wants every one of them on the record.

Ada March — Index to anyone who's met her twice — has a lock-up in De Beauvoir rammed floor to ceiling with tapes, flyers, photos and box files. The Split Second Archive. Every pirate show, every protest, every face on a 'missing' poster that the papers never bothered with. She don't forget, and she don't let the city forget either.

The Red Thread is Index, a solicitor, an oral historian and anyone who's ever lost someone and been told to stop asking. They find people by talking, checking and digging up what others tried to bin. And right now the one they're all looking for is Nia 'Switch' Bell — who, it turns out, might not want to be found by just anyone.

Where they hang out @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB7 Split Second Archive [MAPPED]} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF8 Englefield Listening Flat [MAPPED]}

Who's who, and who's fighting

Noel Harris loves the old stories, told in people's own words. Zoe Akande, the solicitor, wants everything signed and agreed. Nia Bell refuses to be turned into a face on a poster. Index wants a record that'll outlive them all. Some contributors want an exclusive that pays for the next job. Others would rather settle it quiet than be the face of anybody's cause.

Crossing them (and making up)

Putting out a story that stands up is one thing. Flogging someone's address is another. Cross a line you agreed and you'll need to put it right, pay it back, and let them decide if you're worth talking to again.

What your name gets you

RankWhat you get
R3 KnownAn intro to a researcher.
R7 TrustedArchive help, booked in.
R12 ConnectedAccess to cleared case files.
R18 InsiderA say in what gets published and when.
R25 PillarJoint keeper of the whole investigative network.
Calling in favours (Influence)

1 — Point you at a source who'll talk, or a record that exists.

2 — A bit of proper research, or an interview everyone's agreed to.

4 — Independent keepers get together to protect someone's testimony or an archive.

Places that open up

The Split Second Archive (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB7}) opens catalogue and oral-history work. The Englefield Listening Flat (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF8}) gives you listening appointments. Top rank means agreed stewardship of the archive, and agreed rules on what goes out.

The call

Ada "Index" March

Index. From the archive. You don't know me but I know you.

I want Nia found. Not rumours — Nia.

So far: a poster someone ripped down, a reel nobody can find, and an old credit on a programme. That's where you start.

The score

Index wants Nia Bell found — properly, not by chasing every 'I swear I saw her down Ridley Road' going. There's a missing poster someone took down, a reel gone walkabout from the archive, and an old programme credit with a name on it. And someone's paying people to report fake sightings.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB1.3} St Peter de Beauvoir, church hall: a worried friend with more questions than answers. Front.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB7.3} Split Second Archive, catalogue room: the entry that should be there — and isn't. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN1.2} Abney Park Chapel, recording session: an old voice someone recognises.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.d54307367c0dc599]{DA6.4} Dalston CLR James Library, local studies: the programme credit, and someone who's still around. Bottle against a well-paid fake sighting.

Route: DB / CG / DA / SN / DA

The heat

A paid-for fake sighting spreads faster than the truth. The person who took the poster down is scared their own past will be the next story.

Your call

Go public with an appeal. Search on the quiet. Take an exclusive fee. Steal the reel you've been offered. Or sell the first real contact to another faction.

What it leads to

A solid lead opens @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.7f8125d11258c230]{RT2} and @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.be46259208fcc6c4]{RT3}. Pull an appeal and the recording and transport enquiries carry on anyway. A fake sighting still tells you who paid for it.

The twist

The person who tore down the poster is Asha — Nia's closest mate. She did it because Nia asked her to.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The Quiet Ledger

Play it right and this job turns up @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E4 Nia is alive and chose to leave her routine}. Check the Quiet Ledger for what that does — and doesn't — prove.

The score

A woman's watch turned up at a pawnbroker's weeks after she was meant to have left London. The pawner says it was a straight sale. Index wants her found — but only if she wants finding. Someone else is out searching too, and they're paying good money for an address.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL1.4} Clapton Library, local studies: the watch's older owner. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL4.2} The Clapton Hart, front bar: the friend who bought it. Front.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5a3e0570dd504786]{LF2.3} The Prince Arthur, back room: an invitation to a handover.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW6.3} Hub67, screening: the owner — or someone she trusts — if she chooses to come. Moves to get there before the other searcher.

Route: CL / HC / DA / LF / DA / HC / WW

The heat

A second searcher is paying for an address. The woman left someone who controlled her; she'll decide whether she even hears your message before she moves on.

Your call

Return a family heirloom. Sell her address. Protect her right to leave quietly. Expose the false ownership claim. Or carry one message home — and nothing more.

What it leads to

Do right by her and Index rates you. This is a separate disappearance from Nia's. If she says no, the watch's ownership and the man looking for her are still live trouble.

The twist

The 'second searcher' is paying with money from Rusk's security budget. He was hired to find her — and nobody's told you why.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The score

There's an old Dead Air photo that looks a lot like one of today's money men, back when he went by another name. Index wants it checked inside out — because pinning the wrong name on someone would make a cracking headline and wreck an innocent life. A collector's about to buy the photo out from under you.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b2b52ca96e6558d1]{HC3.4} Sutton House, panelled room: the photo, at a loan viewing.

Route: HC / DA / LF / HR / HX

The heat

A collector buys the photo while an old-timer who was there is still on the bus. A wrong ID would make a huge story — and a real innocent target.

Your call

Publish what you can back up. Steal the original. Keep it as a private account. Sell it to the collector. Or trade the middleman's name to someone who'll pay.

What it leads to

Back it up and it points to Evan Lark of Quayline — and opens @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.d0f2613ac1d23e6b.JournalEntryPage.25ee7f45599e1ca8]{RT4}. A changed name on its own proves very little. Lose the photo and the loan list and repair history are still there.

The twist

The other man in the photo — the one everyone cropped out — is Martin Rusk. Lark and Rusk go back a long way.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The score

The exact same 'live' moment pops up on several recordings made in different places. Index reckons the famous Halo warning was cut and stuck together to send everyone chasing the wrong people. The editor will talk — if someone else carries the can. And somebody wants the master tape gone before tonight's screening.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.69084b39c04899a0]{HM8.3} Silt Listening Bunker, control room: the rehearsal. Savvy.

Your call

Prove the programme was doctored. Steal the source. Sell the leverage privately. Publish just the bit you can prove. Or knowingly back a patron's much bigger accusation.

What it leads to

Independent accounts establish @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E3}. Destroy the audio and the rehearsal, the artist and whoever commissioned it are still witnesses — you decide how to use what you've got left.

The editor was paid through Owen Pike — with Rusk's money. The fake was built to make the Lea Boys look guilty.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

Ada "Index" March

Six addresses. Listed for buying up.

BEFORE the 'incidents' that supposedly made them need buying up.

Prove the timing. Don't assume every deal's bent. Some people actually wanted to sell.

Objectives

  1. Find the early option at the Orchard Lease Office (ticks itself)
  2. Get the tenant's own copy at the Clapton Union Rooms (ticks itself)
  3. Date the first print proof at the Roman Rooms Printworks (ticks itself)

The score

Index has six addresses on a buyer's list dated before the fires, leaks and break-ins that were used to justify buying them. Prove the dates — and don't go assuming every single sale was crooked. Evan Lark's offering to buy the file off you as 'routine paperwork'. One resident genuinely wants the investment and will say so loudly.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB8.4} Orchard Lease Office, back office: the early option. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8.3} Clapton Union Rooms, office: a tenant's own copy. Front.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF8.3} Roman Rooms Printworks, proofing room: the date on the first proof, and who ordered the later version.
  • Lark's offer arrives with a smile and a chequebook. Bottle.

Route: HB / SN / CL / HC / WS / BG / OF

The heat

Lark wants to buy the file as routine clearance work. One resident really does want the investment and will contradict anything overcooked.

Your call

Build a case that holds. Sell the tenants a warning. Steal an option. Let an interested buyer make a killing. Or keep the timing up your sleeve for later.

What it leads to

Backing it up establishes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E1}. Lose a document and one of the other six addresses becomes useful instead (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.383dbdd7a30c9ab9]{VW8}, @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF8}). The people living there are still sources — and potential employers.

The twist

The early option on @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.11347b4b484f139e]{CL8} was witnessed by the same insurance assessor who later wrote up the 'incident' there (@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.6a5bcd7797fbc470]{BM5}). Same signature, both papers.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The call

Ada "Index" March

She's alive.

Nia's at the Willow Cabin. I want a meeting.

Asha wants to know what you're going to do with her story first. So do I, to be honest.

Objectives

  1. Hold the first conversation at the Willow Cabin (ticks itself)
  2. Meet the corroborator in the A&E discharge lounge (ticks itself)

The score

Nia's alive and she's at the Willow Cabin. Index wants a meeting. Asha, her best mate, wants to know what the crew plans to do with Nia's story before she lifts another finger. A driver's turned up offering to move Nia right now — no questions asked, and who's paying?

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.9f4c6205e899377d]{WW7.2} Willow Cabin, porch: the first proper conversation. Listen more than you talk. Front.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.ce26d88c705b4b63]{AE6} Homerton A&E, discharge lounge: someone who can back her story up — or the next place to meet.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.f1da74521bed61fd]{SN8.2} Evering safe flat, front room: a refuge on offer. What's the price, and who's asking? Bottle to keep a promise that costs you.
  • If she's already gone, her message at the cabin points to whoever's helping her now. Wheels for the journey.

Route: WW / HC / CL / SN

The heat

A driver shows up offering to move her immediately. If Nia's already left, her note at the cabin leads to her current supporter — not a dead end.

Your call

Respect a limited statement. Grab an exclusive. Arrange protection that isn't any faction's. Sell her location. Or trade her testimony for another faction's backing.

What it leads to

A real meeting, or an account she's agreed to, establishes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E4}. Betray her and she gets harder to reach — but her old recordings, her friends and other witnesses keep the mystery alive.

The twist

Nia didn't go missing. She went quiet — on purpose — the night she found a seventh address on Quayline's list: Auntie Pat's Arches.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

Before this all goes public, I want copies.

The score

Index wants copies of everything in the hands of people nobody can buy or bully before the big public account. The witnesses want one thing, the paying clients want another. A funder's demanding every original plus an exclusive interview — and one witness has just pulled their personal stuff out.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB7.3} Split Second Archive, catalogue room: every surviving version, laid side by side. Savvy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.cbb65680f5cc95c5]{CG8.4} Quayline Records Suite, server room: the middleman's account. Graft if it's contested.

The heat

A funder wants every original and an exclusive interview. One witness pulls their personal material but leaves the project documents.

Your call

Build a shared archive. Keep a private file. Steal the last account. Sell exclusive rights. Or split custody between factions.

What it leads to

A finished record makes @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E2} to @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.22bbb963020e86f8]{E6} usable wherever they're backed up. Failed talks split the archive between named holders — several roads to a partial ending, not one lost master file.

The twist

The funder demanding every original is the same 'charitable foundation' that paid for the Evering flat. New name, same Celia.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

It's done. The Quiet Hour's over.

The score

The Quiet Hour's finished and Index is handing the crew the keys to the whole story. Families want it all out there; some want compensation; some just want privacy; factions want a cut. One person's offering a genuine correction — alongside a not-very-subtle bung to keep quiet.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.5b42c691f95a7c91]{DB7.3} Split Second Archive, catalogue room: the full sequence, stuff you can actually back up. Savvy.

The heat

A named player offers a real correction with one hand and hush money with the other. Publish, narrow or protect the account before you take any archive money.

Your call

Make it public. Keep a protected collection. Sell a one-sided version. Share the keys. Or take your fee and walk.

What it leads to

Top rank gets you a proper investigative network and an archive role. Write down who holds each original and who actually got something out of it. Other crimes and faction plans carry on into later play.

The twist

Nia wants to read the final account on Dead Air herself. Live. Tonight.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

The call

Jonah Mills

Jonah from the Highbury book club. Bit of a weird one.

We taped last week's meeting. On the tape, Derek comments on the book.

Derek died two years ago. Before we flog the club archive, I'd like to know how.

Objectives

  1. Hear the tape at The Old Church (ticks itself)
  2. Compare the older programme at St Mary's New Church
  3. Confront the surviving member at the Rose and Crown gathering
  4. Your call: expose the edit, set up an informed sale, or keep a shared archive

£120 crew fee3 XP+1 Renown · Dead Air Collective or Borough Mutual

Where

@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB2 The Old Church} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB3 St Mary's New Church} MAPPED@UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB6 The Rose and Crown} MAPPED

The score

Jonah's book club recorded last week's natter. Clear as day on the tape, Derek — dead two years — has a pop at the novel. The club's about to sell its archive to a collector, and nobody's keen to vote with a ghost in the room.

What's really going on (GM)

A living ex-member spliced in an old private joke of Derek's to scare the collector off buying the archive. The collector's done nothing wrong and genuinely wants the stuff.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB2.3} The Old Church, vestry: listen to the tape. Leon can spot the repeated phrase — no roll needed.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB3.5} St Mary's New Church, parish room: the older event programme. Same joke, same year.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.a720d397aea87d6a]{HB6.3} The Rose and Crown, function room: the surviving member, mid-meeting, going a bit pale.

Route: HB — one district, every scene on the one street map

The heat

The collector turns up at the next meeting. Hang about and the club votes on the sale without knowing a thing; the member might cough to it once a mate recognises the joke.

How it can end

Expose the edit, arrange a sale where everyone knows the score, or talk the members into keeping a shared archive. Job done gets £120 and 1 AD or BM Renown, once. After that, the club'll book you a meeting room when you need one.

The twist

The 'dead' joke is about a Dead Air pirate night in 1998 — and Leon was there.

After two scenes the rival offers a replacement act on the spot. Take it and the booking's saved — but the original band can come after the organiser.

The organiser owes Miri for three gigs, not one. He's been doing it to everybody.

The musician turns up at the sale with a rival recovery crew. A chase can spill onto the mapped Lea-side approach; a boat cabin interior is optional extra.

Recover the sax, buy it back for the musician, or negotiate a paid walk-away. £160 and 1 TU or NM Renown once; the boat owner becomes a contact for the odd lift — not a free ride.

Perry Sloane's coat. They found Perry dead backstage. Find out who did it.

Objectives

  1. Compare the crate record at the Nunnery Gallery (ticks itself)
  2. Question Len Fisk at the Forman's gathering
  3. Intercept the bell at the Roman Exchange
  4. Decide who gets the truth about Perry — and what happens to Len

£240 crew fee3 XP+1 Renown · The Night Market or The Lantern Desk

Where

The score

A valuable stage bell has turned up at the market packed in a crate with stagehand Perry Sloane's bloodstained coat. Perry's been found dead offstage. This isn't a caper — it's a murder, and Pearl wants it treated like one.

What's really going on (GM)

Len Fisk killed Perry after Perry found out about Len's separate resale fraud. It's a standalone murder — not a Meridian hit, and nothing to do with Nia going missing.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF2.5} Nunnery Gallery, loading bay: the crate record. A witness remembers the row — no roll needed; rolls decide speed and what cooperation costs.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF6.3} Forman's Fish Island, private gathering: Len Fisk, all smiles. Front.
  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.0e780ec36ad51135]{OF7.4} Roman Exchange, back store: Len trying to get rid of the bell.

Route: OF — one district, every scene on the one street map

The heat

Len tries to sell the bell after the second interview. Tip him off and he runs to a buyer listed in the ledger — another chase.

How it can end

Get the bell back and decide who hears the truth, sell an honest ownership claim, or cover for the killer at a stated price. £240 and 1 NM or LD Renown once for the disclosed job; hide Len and Perry's family become enemies for good.

The twist

Perry had already posted a copy of Len's second set of books to Pearl. It's sitting in her letterbox at the Roman Exchange, unopened.

Use it or don't — it's yours. Every twist is listed in the Quiet Ledger chapter.

Mara "Tern" Boyd

A van. A performer called Mara Sol. And a handover she clearly didn't want.

Find her before one of my drivers gets the blame.

The score

A student film shoot accidentally caught a van handover in the background — a performer, Mara Sol, being made to go somewhere she didn't want to. Tern wants her found before one of her drivers carries the can.

What's really going on (GM)

Harlan Black, a crook working on his own, is forcing Mara to work off a made-up debt. It's separate from the Meridian plot. Mara wants her mate freed from another debt as well.

How it goes down

  • @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.cc6805cf975bde88.JournalEntryPage.b7a4eb23ff167c1b]{BF4.4} 3 Mills Studios, edit suite: get the filmmakers' OK to watch the rushes.

Route: BF — one district, every scene on the one street map

Black moves the van after the second enquiry. A station witness knows the next paid stop; a botched interception moves the meeting — Mara doesn't vanish from play.

How it can end

Get Mara out, buy out the debt then fight it, or seize Black's leverage. £240 and 1 TU or VC Renown once; Mara picks her own future bookings and can become a regular contact.

The twist

Harlan Black rents his vans from the East Cross compound. Rusk takes a cut of every job.

LONDON INTERIORS

Venue Register

160 venues and 51 approaches across twenty districts — plus the four rooms from the opening.

Every place a job or a case sends the crew is in here: who you'll meet, what's going on, the six rooms, where the door is on the street map, and when you can first get in.

The maps

Every venue is MAPPED: its own scene in the London Venues compendium, with six keyed rooms (the plaques carry the codes — DA7.2 is room 2 of DA7), the public way in at room 1 and the back way or loading bay at room 6. 101 venues open straight off the street; the other 59 sit behind one of 51 approach maps — a park, a yard, a square, a side street — with an ENTER pin for the front door and a SERVICE pin for the back.

On the street maps an ENTER pin marks the way in. Walk a character into it and they're through (the map is pulled from the compendium there and then); motors park outside. To get a job ready, open the Mission Board and hit Prepare this mission's maps; the scenes get filed under The Smoke — Venues, one folder per district. The sat nav takes you to the pin.

Four ways to know a place

Known — you've got a lead you can act on. Entered — you've been in. Trusted — you've earned a regular arrangement with somebody named. Claimed — made-up premises only, with a stake you've agreed. Write down who sponsored you and what you're allowed to do there.

Where it is. Marshgate & Pudding Mill [marshgate-pudding-mill]. Approaches @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.e9df8651707b9fcb.JournalEntryPage.cd201b2206536334]{APP-BF5} MAPPED.

The rooms. BF5.1 public foyer; BF5.2 seminar room; BF5.3 project studio; BF5.4 meeting room; BF5.5 exhibition store; BF5.6 delivery court. All six room zones MAPPED.

Getting in. Take @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.0decc348c7790f3f]{LD3} (once you've got Renown 3 with The Lantern Desk) and DS Harriet Vale gets you in the door for that visit. You'll usually have done @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.7b640abfbcb175ce]{LD2} first — or found someone else to vouch for you.

Coming back. Once they rate you, you can ask for a project meeting or public workshop appointment. Reckon on £40 per session; institutional access is not a rank reward.

Moving in. Renown 7: a regular slot. Renown 12: a room held for you. Renown 18: a say in the project. You still pay your way.

Jobs that send you here. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.0decc348c7790f3f]{LD3}

BF6 · Pudding Mill Lane DLR station MAPPED

Pudding Mill Lane · Real location · place source

Who you'll meet. Nia Switch Bell, radio presenter by arrangement.

What's going on. A handover on the platform, interrupted by the train. Split the crew: the nicked case, or the person with its receipt.

Where it is. Pudding Mill Lane [pudding-mill-lane]. New frontage court included in this MAPPED interior brief.

The rooms. BF6.1 street entrance; BF6.2 covered concourse; BF6.3 platform lobby; BF6.4 staff meeting room; BF6.5 store; BF6.6 service landing. All six room zones MAPPED.

Getting in. Take @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.179900d7fa46d217]{LD5} (once you've got Renown 8 with The Lantern Desk) and DS Harriet Vale gets you in the door for that visit. You'll usually have done @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.ef0b9e188b6e7cd1]{LD4} first — or found someone else to vouch for you. Shortcut: the local case @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.56b63421a2c8e19a]{S20} opens the rooms from day one.

Coming back. Once they rate you, you can ask for a reliable public rendezvous with a driver contact. Reckon on £20 in contact expenses; staff rooms require a new authorised appointment.

Moving in. Renown 7: a regular slot. Renown 12: a room held for you. Renown 18: a say in the project. You still pay your way.

Jobs that send you here. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.01b43c4291081cb5]{TU8} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.179900d7fa46d217]{LD5} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.56b63421a2c8e19a]{S20}

BF7 · Marshgate Delivery Depot MAPPED

Invented premises at the proposed atlas anchor · Fictional premises

Who you'll meet. Gita Mercer.

What's going on. Four final-night loads, one customer. One's routine business. Another's carrying a witness's whole life in boxes.

Where it is. Marshgate Block [marshgate-block]. New frontage court included in this MAPPED interior brief.

The rooms. BF7.1 reception; BF7.2 dispatch office; BF7.3 driver room; BF7.4 sorting hall; BF7.5 load cage; BF7.6 van yard. All six room zones MAPPED.

Getting in. Take @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.5f6a9fc17d4ae6dc]{TU7} (once you've got Renown 15 with The Towpath Union) and Mara Tern Boyd gets you in the door for that visit. You'll usually have done @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.8b693ddfca554a5e]{TU6} first — or found someone else to vouch for you. Shortcut: the local case @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.56b63421a2c8e19a]{S20} opens the rooms from day one.

Coming back. Do right by them and Gita Mercer will set up another meet, a work session or a bit of storage — about £20 a go. Vans, staff and goods are a separate conversation.

Moving in. Renown 7: regular work. Renown 12: your own room. Renown 18: a say in how it's run. Renown 25: maybe a real stake, if you can agree one. Gita and the drivers agree each contract and vehicle; a dispatch share needs £200 working capital and £50 weekly running costs plus fuel.

Jobs that send you here. @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.2fcc7b0410f4f526.JournalEntryPage.c19a5cc4367c0ae7]{VC8} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.992bca85973f5687.JournalEntryPage.5f6a9fc17d4ae6dc]{TU7} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.b6f2c39b51dec5f2.JournalEntryPage.934d64446b75f8cc]{BB7} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.5816796be7174f14.JournalEntryPage.1fb049db18a7ccb6]{LD7} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.1181185673dbd03b.JournalEntryPage.1c6a4266500f4558]{MR7} / @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.9f3d5bcde34ec080.JournalEntryPage.56b63421a2c8e19a]{S20}

BF8 · Carpenters Breakfast Club MAPPED

Invented premises at the proposed atlas anchor · Fictional premises

Who you'll meet. Gwen Price.

What's going on. One of the six. A redevelopment 'mandate' stitched together out of a repair petition.

Where it is. Carpenters Block [carpenters-block]. New frontage court included in this MAPPED interior brief.

The rooms. BF8.1 front kitchen; BF8.2 dining room; BF8.3 residents room; BF8.4 meeting office; BF8.5 pantry; BF8.6 rear court. All six room zones MAPPED.

Getting in. Take @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.6a5bcd7797fbc470]{BM5} (once you've got Renown 8 with Borough Mutual) and Rosa Baptiste gets you in the door for that visit. You'll usually have done @UUID[Compendium.the-smoke.guides.JournalEntry.380caf621239c12b.JournalEntryPage.20b3857b08eff2d6]{BM4} first — or found someone else to vouch for you.

Coming back. Do right by them and Gwen Price will set up another meet, a work session or a bit of storage — about £20 a go. Vans, staff and goods are a separate conversation.

Moving in. Renown 7: regular work. Renown 12: your own room. Renown 18: a say in how it's run. Renown 25: maybe a real stake, if you can agree one. Gwen and the current users decide room use after the false mandate is resolved; budget £25 weekly costs and a named kitchen rota.
